**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 1–2:**

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿A declaration of freedom from obligation from Allah and His Messenger﴾, meaning: this is a declaration of freedom from obligation from Allah. It is a verbal noun (masdar), like *al-nash'ah* (growing up) and *al-dana'ah* (baseness).

The exegetes (mufassirun) said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out for Tabuk, the hypocrites were spreading rumours, and the polytheists began breaking the treaties that existed between them and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So Allah, mighty and majestic, commanded the annulment of their treaties. This is His saying, mighty and majestic: "And if you fear treachery from a people, then throw back to them [their treaty] on equal terms" (al-Anfal 8:58).

Al-Zajjaj said: *Bara'ah* means that Allah, exalted, and His Messenger are free of responsibility for having given them treaties and for fulfilling them if they break them.

﴿To those with whom you made a treaty among the polytheists﴾: the address is to the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, although it was the Prophet ﷺ who made the treaties and agreements with them, because he made them while his companions were content with that. Thus it is as if they themselves had made the agreements and covenants.

﴿So travel freely in the land﴾: the discourse shifts from report to direct address, meaning: say to them, "Travel" (*siḥū*), that is, go about in the land, coming and going, secure and not fearing any Muslim.

﴿For four months. And know that you cannot escape Allah﴾: that is, you cannot elude or outrun Him. ﴿And that Allah will disgrace the disbelievers﴾: that is, He will humiliate them by killing in this world and by punishment in the Hereafter.

The scholars differed concerning this term (*ta'jil*, grace period) and concerning those with whom Allah and His Messenger declared freedom from the treaties that existed between them and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:

A group said: This is a grace period granted by Allah, exalted, to the polytheists. Whoever's treaty period was less than four months was extended to four months; whoever's treaty period was more than four months was reduced to four months; and whoever's treaty had no specified term was limited to four months. After that, he is at war with Allah and His Messenger, so he is to be killed wherever he is found and taken captive, unless he repents [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 14/96–97.]].

The beginning of this term was the day of the Greater Pilgrimage (*yawm al-ḥajj al-akbar*, the day of the great pilgrimage), and its end was ten days into the month of Rabi' al-Akhir.

As for those who had no treaty, their term ended with the expiry of the sacred months (*al-ashhur al-ḥurum*), which is fifty days. Al-Zuhri said: The four months are Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and Muharram [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 14/101.]], because this verse was revealed in Shawwal. The first view is the more correct, and the majority hold it.

Al-Kalbi said: The four months applied only to those who had a treaty of less than four months, and it was completed for them to four months. As for whoever had a treaty of more than four months, this was commanded to be fulfilled by His saying, exalted: ﴿Then fulfil their treaty to its term﴾ [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 14/102.]].

Al-Hasan said: Allah, mighty and majestic, commanded His Messenger ﷺ to fight those among the polytheists who fought against him, saying: "Fight in the way of Allah those who fight you" (al-Baqarah 2:190). So he would fight only those who fought him. Then He commanded him to fight the polytheists and to declare freedom from them, and He gave them a term of four months. None of them had a term longer than four months, neither those who had a treaty before the declaration nor those who had no treaty. So the term for all of them was four months, and after the term expired, He made the blood of all of them lawful to shed, both those with treaties and others.

It was also said: This was revealed before Tabuk.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq, Mujahid and others said: It was revealed concerning the people of Makkah. The reason was that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made a treaty with the Quraysh in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, that they would lay down war for ten years, during which people would be secure. The Khuza'ah entered into the covenant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Banu Bakr entered into the covenant of the Quraysh. Then the Banu Bakr attacked the Khuza'ah and inflicted harm on them, and the Quraysh helped them with weapons. When the Banu Bakr and the Quraysh backed one another against the Khuza'ah and broke their covenant, 'Amr ibn Salim al-Khuza'i set out until he stood before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said:

*O Allah, I appeal to Muhammad*
*by the covenant of our father and his father, the ancient one.*

*So help, may Allah guide you, with a help that is lasting,*
*and call the servants of Allah; they will come as a reinforcement.*

*White like the sun, rising high,*
*if his face is struck with dimness, it grows bright.*

*They attacked us by night in the noon-heat, while we slept,*
*and they killed us while we bowed and prostrated.*

*You were a father to us, and we were your children;*
*there we submitted, and we did not withdraw our hands.*

*In their midst the Messenger of Allah has come, stripped for battle,*
*in a host like a sea flowing with foam.*

*Indeed the Quraysh have broken their promise to you,*
*and violated your firm covenant.*

*They claimed that you would not save anyone,*
*while they are the most humiliated and the fewest in number.*

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "May I not be helped if I do not help you." He prepared to march to Makkah in the eighth year after the Hijrah.

When the ninth year came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wished to perform the pilgrimage, but then said: "The polytheists will attend, and they will circumambulate naked." So he sent Abu Bakr that year as commander of the pilgrimage season, to conduct the pilgrimage for the people, and he sent with him forty verses from the beginning of Bara'ah, to recite to the people of the season. Then he sent 'Ali, may Allah honour his face, after him, on his she-camel al-'Adba', to recite the beginning of Bara'ah to the people, and he commanded him to proclaim in Makkah, Mina and 'Arafah: "Indeed the protection of Allah and the protection of His Messenger ﷺ is withdrawn from every polytheist, and no naked person shall circumambulate the House."

Abu Bakr returned and said: "O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, has something been revealed concerning me?" He said: "No, but no one should convey this except a man from my family. Are you not content, O Abu Bakr, that you were with me in the cave, and that you are my companion at the Pool?" He said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah."

So Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, set out as commander of the pilgrimage, and 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, set out to proclaim Bara'ah. When it was the day before the Day of Tarwiyah (the eighth of Dhu al-Hijjah), Abu Bakr addressed the people, told them about their rites, and established the pilgrimage for the people. The Arabs in that year still kept to their places of the pre-Islamic pilgrimage. Then on the day of sacrifice (*yawm al-nahr*), 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah honour his face, stood up and proclaimed to the people what he had been commanded, and he recited to them Surah Bara'ah [[See: Sirah Ibn Hisham: 2/394–396, 545–546; Tafsir al-Tabari: 14/96–97.]].

Zayd ibn Yuthay' [[Zayd ibn Yutay' — with a dammah on the yā' (and the hamzah sometimes replaced), followed by a thā' with a dot, then a sākin yā', then an unmarked letter; al-Hamdani al-Kufi — trustworthy, a mukhadram (one who lived in both the Jahiliyyah and Islam) — from the second generation (al-Taqrib). In the original it was written "Tubay'".]] said: We asked 'Ali: "With what were you sent on that pilgrimage?" He said: "I was sent with four things: no naked person shall circumambulate the House; whoever has a treaty with the Prophet ﷺ, it remains until its term; whoever has no treaty, his term is four months; and no one enters Paradise except a believing soul, and the polytheists and the Muslims shall not gather after this year of theirs" [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 14/106. Al-Tirmidhi related it in al-Hajj: 3/610, and in al-Tafsir: 8/488, and said: this is a hasan sahih hadith. Imam Ahmad also related it in al-Musnad under no. (4) and no. (594), edited by Shaykh Ahmad Shakir. See also: Fath al-Bari: 8/319.]].

Then the Prophet ﷺ performed the Farewell Pilgrimage (*Hajjat al-Wada'*) in the tenth year.

If someone asks: How did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ send Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, and then remove him and send 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him?

We say: The scholars mentioned that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not remove Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him; he remained the commander. He sent 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, only to proclaim these verses. The reason for this was that the Arabs had a custom among themselves regarding making and breaking treaties, that such matters should be handled only by their chief or a man of his clan. So the Prophet ﷺ sent 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, to remove the pretext, lest they say: "This is contrary to what we know," which would contradict the breaking of the treaty.

The evidence that Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, was the commander is what 'Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi related to us, from Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi, from Muhammad ibn Yusuf, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Ishaq, from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim, from the son of the brother of Ibn Shihab, from his paternal uncle, who said: Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed me that Abu Hurayrah said: Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, sent me in that pilgrimage among the callers on the day of sacrifice, to proclaim at Mina: "No polytheist shall make the pilgrimage after this year, and no naked person shall circumambulate the House." Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman said: Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent 'Ali after him and commanded him to proclaim Bara'ah. Abu Hurayrah said: 'Ali proclaimed with us among the people of Mina on the day of sacrifice: "No polytheist shall make the pilgrimage after this year, and no naked person shall circumambulate the House" [[Related by al-Bukhari in al-Salah, chapter on what must be covered of the 'awrah: 1/477–478, and Muslim in al-Hajj, chapter: No polytheist should make the pilgrimage to the House, no. (1347): 2/982.]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 3:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And a proclamation﴾ is coordinated with His saying "a declaration of immunity" (bara'ah), meaning: a notification (i'lam). From this comes the adhan (call to prayer), as in: "I informed him (adhantuhu) so he was informed (fa-adhina)," meaning: I made him know. Its root is from the ear (udhun), meaning: I caused it to enter his ear.

﴿from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater hajj﴾. They differed concerning the day of the greater hajj. ʿIkrimah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that it is the Day of ʿArafah, and this is also reported from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab and Ibn al-Zubayr. This is the view of ʿAtaʾ, Tawus, Mujahid, and Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab.

A group said: it is the Day of Sacrifice (yawm al-nahr). It is narrated from Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, who said: ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) went out on the Day of Sacrifice upon a white mule, intending the al-Jabbanah, when a man came to him, took hold of the bridle of his mount, and asked him about the day of the greater hajj. He said: "It is this day of yours; let go of its reins." This is also related from ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Awfa and al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah. It is the view of al-Shaʿbi, al-Nakhaʿi, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, and al-Suddi.

Ibn Jurayj narrated from Mujahid: the day of the greater hajj is the time of the hajj, all the days of Mina. Sufyan al-Thawri used to say: the day of the greater hajj is all the days of Mina, like the expression "the day of Siffin," "the day of the Camel," and "the day of Bu'ath," by which is meant the period and the time, because these wars lasted many days.

ʿAbdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal said: the day of the greater hajj is the day on which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed the hajj. This is also the view of Ibn Sirin, because on it the hajj of the Muslims and the festival of the Jews, Christians, and polytheists coincided, and this had not occurred before it or after it.

They differed concerning the greater hajj. Mujahid said: the greater hajj is the qiran (combined hajj and ʿumrah), and the lesser hajj is the ifrad (hajj alone).

al-Zuhri, al-Shaʿbi, and ʿAtaʾ said: the greater hajj is the hajj itself, and the lesser hajj is the ʿumrah; it was called "the lesser" because of the deficiency of its acts.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿that Allah is free of obligation to the polytheists, and so is His Messenger﴾, meaning: His Messenger is likewise free of obligation to the polytheists. Yaʿqub read "wa-rasulahu" with a fatha on the lam, meaning: that Allah and His Messenger are free of obligation. ﴿So if you repent﴾, meaning you return from your disbelief and sincerely adopt monotheism, ﴿it is better for you; but if you turn away﴾, meaning you turn away from faith, ﴿then know that you cannot escape Allah. And give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 4:

﴿Except those with whom you made a covenant among the polytheists⦆ This is an exception from His saying: "A declaration of disavowal from Allah and His Messenger to those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant," except for the covenant of those among the polytheists with whom you made a covenant. They were the Banu Damrah, a tribe of Kinanah. Allah the Exalted commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to fulfil their covenant until its term, and nine months of their term remained. The reason for this was that they had not broken the covenant, and this is the meaning of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then they have not failed you in anything﴾ of their covenant which you made with them, ﴿nor have they supported anyone against you﴾ — they did not assist anyone of your enemies against you. Ata' ibn Yasar recited: "lam yanquduukum" with the dotted ḍād (ḍ), from naqḍ al-ʿahd (breaking the covenant). ﴿So fulfil for them their covenant until their term﴾ — so keep your promise to them, ﴿until their term﴾, until their appointed time which you agreed upon with them, ﴿indeed Allah loves the righteous﴾.

The Almighty's saying, ﴿When the sacred months have passed﴾: meaning, when they have ended and gone by. ﴿The sacred months﴾ — it has been said that these are the four months: Rajab, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and al-Muharram.

Mujahid and Ibn Ishaq said: they are the months of the covenant. Whoever had a covenant, his covenant lasts four months. And whoever had no covenant, his term runs until the end of al-Muharram, fifty days. It has been said that they are called "sacred" (ḥurum) because Allah, exalted is He, made it forbidden for the believers during them to shed the blood of the polytheists or to attack them.

If it is objected: this amount is only part of the sacred months, yet Allah, exalted is He, says: "When the sacred months have passed"?

It is answered: since this period was joined to what had gone before, the plural form was applied to it. Its meaning is: the stipulated period has passed, during which the sacred months come to an end.

The Almighty's saying: ﴿So kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ — within the sacred territory and outside it. ﴿And seize them﴾ and take them captive, ﴿and besiege them﴾, that is, confine them.

Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: He means, if they take refuge in fortresses, then besiege them, that is, prevent them from coming out.

It has also been said: prevent them from entering Makkah and from moving freely in the lands of Islam.

﴿And lie in wait for them at every place of ambush﴾, that is, on every road. The marsad is the place from which one watches for the enemy, from "rasadtu al-shay' arsudu", meaning I watched for the thing. He means: be watchers for them, so that you may take them from whatever direction they come.

It has also been said: lie in wait for them on the road to Makkah, so that they do not enter it.

﴿But if they repent﴾ from polytheism, ﴿and establish prayer and give zakat, then let them go their way﴾: he says, leave them alone, so that they may go about freely in their own cities and enter Makkah. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving﴾ toward whoever repents, ﴿Merciful﴾ to him.

Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: this verse abrogated (naskh) every verse in the Qur'an that mentions turning away from the disbelievers and patience over the harm of enemies. [[It was mentioned in an earlier context that some scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, have extended this matter, making the verse of the sword abrogating every verse in the Qur'an that contains a command to patience, forgiveness, or peaceful dealing. This is not accepted from them, for there is no contradiction between them, and they belong to "al-mansa'" (a category that, as al-Zarkashi and others say, is not abrogated), and are not among the abrogated verses.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 6–7:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if any one of the polytheists seeks your protection﴾, meaning: and if any one of the polytheists whom I commanded you to fight and kill seeks your protection, that is, asks you for safe-conduct after the sacred months have passed, in order that he may hear the words of Allah.

﴿Then grant him protection﴾, meaning: give him refuge and make him secure. ﴿Until he hears the words of Allah﴾, concerning what is for him and against him of reward and punishment. ﴿Then convey him to his place of safety﴾, meaning: if he does not become Muslim, convey him to his place of safety, that is, the place where he feels secure, which is the abode of his people. If he fights you after that and you gain power over him, then kill him. ﴿That is because they are a people who do not know﴾, meaning: they do not know the religion of Allah, exalted is He, and His oneness, so they are in need of hearing the words of Allah. Al-Hasan said: this verse is decisive (muhkamah) until the Day of Resurrection.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿How can there be a covenant with Allah and His Messenger for the polytheists?﴾ This is in the form of amazement, and its meaning is denial, that is: there is no covenant for them with Allah, nor with His Messenger, for they betray and break covenants. Then He made an exception, saying, exalted is He: ﴿Except those with whom you made a covenant at al-Masjid al-Haram﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: they are the Quraysh. Qatadah said: they are the people of Makkah with whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made a covenant on the day of al-Hudaybiyah.

Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So as long as they remain true to you, be true to them﴾, meaning: to the covenant. ﴿So they were not true to you, so be true to them﴾ — they did not remain upright; they broke the covenant and aided Banu Bakr against Khuza'ah. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), after the conquest, set for them a term of four months, during which they could choose their course: either to become Muslim or to join whatever lands they wished. They embraced Islam before the four months ended.

Al-Suddi, al-Kalbi and Ibn Ishaq said: they were from the tribes of Bakr: Banu Khuzaymah, Banu Mudlij, Banu Damrah and Banu al-Dil, and they were those who had entered into the covenant of the Quraysh on the day of al-Hudaybiyah. Only the Quraysh and Banu al-Dil of Banu Bakr broke the covenant, so He commanded that the covenant be fulfilled for those who had not broken it, and they were Banu Damrah.

This view is closer to the truth, because these verses were revealed after the Quraysh broke the covenant and after the conquest of Makkah. How, then, would He say of something that had already passed: "So as long as they remain true to you, be true to them"? Rather, they are those of whom He, mighty and majestic, said: "Except those of the polytheists with whom you made a covenant, then they have not failed you in anything," as the Quraysh failed you, and they did not back anyone against you as the Quraysh backed Banu Bakr against Khuza'ah, the allies of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who are mindful of Him﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 8:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿How (can there be a covenant), when if they gain the upper hand over you⟩ [[Omitted from "b".]] ﴿they do not observe regarding you any tie of kinship or pact⟩. This is connected to the first verse; its meaning is: "How can they have a covenant with Allah and His Messenger [how] [[Omitted from "b".]] when, if they gain the upper hand over you...?" ﴿They do not observe regarding you any tie of kinship or pact.⟩ Al-Akhfash said: "How do you not kill them, when they, if they gain the upper hand over you" — that is, if they prevail over you — "do not observe (lā yarqubū)": do not preserve? Al-Dahhak said: do not wait. Qutrub said: do not respect regarding you "illan." Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak said: kinship. Yaman said: blood-relationship. Qatadah said: "illan" is alliance. Al-Suddi said: it is covenant. Likewise "dhimmah," except that it was repeated because the two words differ. Abu Mijlaz and Mujahid said: "illan" is Allah, mighty and majestic. Ubayd ibn Umayr used to recite "Jabra'il" with the doubled letter, meaning "Abd Allah" (servant of Allah). It is reported that some people came to Abu Bakr from the people of Musaylimah the liar, and Abu Bakr asked them to recite the book of Musaylimah, so they recited it, and Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "This speech did not come from an 'il" — that is, from Allah.

The evidence for this interpretation is the reading of Ikrimah: "lā yarqubūna fī mu'minin īlan" with a yā', meaning Allah, mighty and majestic, like Jibra'il and Mika'il. "Nor a pact (dhimmah)," that is, a covenant.

﴿They please you with their mouths⟩, that is, they give you with their tongues the opposite of what is in their hearts, ﴿but their hearts refuse⟩ faith, ﴿and most of them are defiantly disobedient.⟩

If it is said: this refers to the polytheists, and all of them are defiantly disobedient, so how did He say "most of them are defiantly disobedient"? It is answered: He meant by defiance (fisq) the breaking of the covenant, and among the polytheists there were those who fulfilled their covenant, while most of them broke it; therefore He said, "and most of them are defiantly disobedient."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 9–11:

﴿They have sold the signs of Allah for a small price﴾. This is because they broke the covenant between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for a morsel of food that Abu Sufyan fed them. Mujahid said: Abu Sufyan fed his allies, ﴿so they averted [others] from His way﴾, meaning they prevented people from entering the religion of Allah. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: This is because the people of al-Ta'if supplied them with wealth so that they would strengthen them against fighting the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). ﴿Indeed, evil is what they have been doing﴾, meaning: how wretched is what they were doing.

﴿They do not observe toward a believer any tie of kinship or covenant﴾. He says: Do not spare them, O believers, just as they would not spare you if they gained the upper hand. ﴿And it is they who are the transgressors﴾ by breaking the covenant.

﴿But if they repent﴾ from polytheism, ﴿establish prayer and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion﴾, meaning: they are your brothers in religion. ﴿They have what we have and are subject to what we are subject to.﴾ ﴿And We detail the verses﴾, meaning We make the verses clear ﴿for a people who know﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: This verse made the blood of the People of the Qiblah sacred. Ibn Mas'ud said: It commanded them to pray and to give zakah, so whoever does not give zakah, there is no prayer for him.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliki informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Abu al-Yaman al-Hakam ibn Nafi' informed us, Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamzah informed us from al-Zuhri, who said: Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Utbah ibn Mas'ud informed us that Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed away, and Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) became his successor, and those among the Arabs who disbelieved did so, Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said to Abu Bakr: How can you fight the people when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been commanded to fight the people until they say, 'There is no god but Allah.' Whoever says 'There is no god but Allah' has protected his property and his life from me, except by its right, and his reckoning is with Allah"? Abu Bakr said: By Allah, I will surely fight whoever separates the prayer from zakah, for zakah is the right of property. By Allah, if they withheld from me a young she-goat that they used to give to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), I would fight them over withholding it. Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: By Allah, it was only that Allah had opened Abu Bakr's chest for fighting, and I knew that it was the truth. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-I'tisam, chapter on following the sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): 13/250, and Muslim in al-Iman, chapter on the command to fight people until they say: There is no god but Allah, no. (20): 1/51-52.]]

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliki informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Amr ibn Abbas informed us, Ibn al-Mahdi informed us, Mansur ibn Sa'd informed us from Maymun ibn Siyah from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever prays our prayer, faces our qiblah, and eats our slaughtered animal, that is the Muslim who has the protection of Allah and the protection of His Messenger." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Salah, chapter on the virtue of facing the qiblah: 1/496.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 12:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they break their oaths﴾ means they break their covenants, ﴿after their pact﴾ means their contract, meaning the idolaters of Quraysh, ﴿and attack﴾ means they disparage, ﴿your religion﴾ means they revile it. This is evidence that when a dhimmi (a non-Muslim living under Muslim protection) openly attacks the religion of Islam, he has no covenant left, ﴿then fight the leaders of disbelief﴾. The people of Kufa and Syria recited "a'immata" with two hamzas wherever it occurs, while the rest recited it with the second hamza softened. The leaders of disbelief (a'immat al-kufr) are the heads and commanders of the polytheists from the people of Makkah.

Ibn 'Abbas said: It was revealed concerning Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, Suhayl ibn 'Amr, 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, and the rest of the leaders of Quraysh at that time, who broke the covenant, and they were the ones who plotted to expel the Messenger [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 14/154, and in a longer version: al-Bukhari: 8/322. See also: al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/136.]]. Mujahid said: They are the people of Persia and Byzantium [[In al-Durr al-Manthur: from Mujahid who said, Abu Sufyan.]].

Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman said: The people of this verse have not yet been fought, and its people have not yet come. ﴿Indeed, they have no oaths﴾ means they have no covenants; it is the plural of yamin (oath). Qutrub said: they have no fidelity to the covenant. Ibn 'Amir recited "la iman lahum" with a kasra on the alif, meaning they have no true belief and no religion. It was also said: it derives from amān (safety), meaning do not grant them safety, and kill them wherever you find them. ﴿So that they may desist﴾ means so that they may cease from reviling your religion and aiding against you. It was also said: from disbelief.

Then he urged the Muslims to fight, and the Most High said: ﴿Will you not fight against a people who broke their oaths﴾, that is, violated their covenants. They are the ones who violated the treaty of peace at al-Hudaybiyah and aided the Banu Bakr against the Khuza'ah.

﴿And they plotted to expel the Messenger﴾ from Makkah, when they gathered in Dar al-Nadwah (the council house of the Quraysh), ﴿and they were the first to attack you﴾ with fighting, ﴿the first time﴾, meaning: on the Day of Badr. That is because they said, when the caravan was safe: "We will not turn back until we have uprooted Muhammad and his companions."

A group of the exegetes said: He meant that they began fighting the Khuza'ah, the allies of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

﴿Do you fear them?﴾ Do you fear them so that you abandon fighting them? ﴿Then Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾ in abandoning their fighting, ﴿if you are believers﴾.

﴿Fight them, and Allah will punish them by your hands﴾, Allah will kill them by your hands, ﴿and He will disgrace them﴾ and humiliate them through capture and subjugation, ﴿and give you victory over them and heal the breasts of a people﴾ and cure the disease of the hearts of a people, ﴿who are believers﴾, from the harm they used to suffer from them. Mujahid and al-Suddi said: He meant the breasts of the Khuza'ah, the allies of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when the Quraysh aided the Banu Bakr against them, so that they (the Khuza'ah) wreaked vengeance upon them; and Allah healed their breasts from the Banu Bakr through the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers.

﴿And remove the rage of their hearts﴾, its distress and grief caused by the Quraysh's support of Bakr against them. Then he said, as a new statement: ﴿And Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills﴾, guiding him to Islam, as He did with Abu Sufyan, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl and Suhayl ibn Amr, ﴿and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾. It is related that the Prophet (ﷺ) said on the day of the Conquest of Makkah: "Lift the sword, except against the Khuza'ah from the Banu Bakr, until the afternoon." ﴿Do you fear them?﴾ Do you fear them so that you abandon fighting them? ﴿Then Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾ in abandoning their fighting, ﴿if you are believers﴾.

﴿Fight them, and Allah will punish them by your hands﴾, Allah will kill them by your hands, ﴿and He will disgrace them﴾ and humiliate them through capture and subjugation, ﴿and give you victory over them and heal the breasts of a people﴾ and cure the disease of the hearts of a people, ﴿who are believers﴾, from the harm they used to suffer from them. Mujahid and al-Suddi said: He meant the breasts of the Khuza'ah, the allies of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when the Quraysh aided the Banu Bakr against them, so that they (the Khuza'ah) wreaked vengeance upon them; and Allah healed their breasts from the Banu Bakr through the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers.

﴿And remove the rage of their hearts﴾, its distress and grief caused by the Quraysh's support of Bakr against them. Then he said, as a new statement: ﴿And Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills﴾, guiding him to Islam, as He did with Abu Sufyan, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl and Suhayl ibn Amr, ﴿and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾. It is related that the Prophet (ﷺ) said on the day of the Conquest of Makkah: "Lift the sword, except against the Khuza'ah from the Banu Bakr, until the afternoon." [[Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf: 14/487, and Abu 'Ubayd in al-Amwal p. (131).]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 16–17:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or did you think﴾ (a'zanantum, "did you suppose") ﴿that you would be left﴾. It was said: this is addressed to the hypocrites. And it was said: to the believers for whom fighting was hard. So He said: Or did you think that you would be left without being commanded to strive (jihad), and without being tested, so that the truthful might be distinguished from the liar? ﴿And Allah had not yet known﴾ (wa lamma ya'lam Allah, meaning "and Allah had not yet seen") ﴿those of you who strove and did not take, apart from Allah and His Messenger and the believers, any intimate (waliyjah)﴾, meaning a close confidant and allies whom they befriend and to whom they disclose their secrets. Qatadah said: waliyjah means betrayal. al-Dahhak said: deception. Ata said: allies. Abu 'Ubaydah said: everything that you insert into something to which it does not belong is a waliyjah, and a man may be among a people while not being one of them, and he is their waliyjah. So the waliyjah of a man is the one who is specially entrusted with the innermost matters of his affairs apart from the people; it is said: "he is my waliyjah," and "they are my waliyjah," for both the singular and the plural.

﴿And Allah is Aware of what you do﴾.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah﴾, the verse.

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: When al-'Abbas was taken captive at the Battle of Badr, the Muslims reproached him for disbelief and severing the ties of kinship, and 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, spoke harshly to him. Al-'Abbas said: "Why is it that you mention our faults and do not mention our good qualities?" 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said to him: "Do you have good qualities?" He said: "Yes. We maintain the Masjid al-Haram, we guard the Ka'bah, and we give water to the pilgrims." So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed in reply to al-'Abbas: "It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah," [[Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. 278.]] meaning: it is not fitting for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah.

It is obligatory upon the Muslims to prevent them from this, because mosques are maintained only for the worship of Allah alone, so it is not proper for one who is a disbeliever in Allah to maintain them. A group of scholars held that what is meant is the well-known maintenance of mosques, namely building them and repairing them when they fall into ruin, so the disbeliever is prevented from it; even if he bequeaths it, the bequest is not carried out. Some of them interpreted "maintenance" here as entering the mosque and sitting in it. al-Hasan said: "It is not for the polytheists to be left so that they become the people of the Masjid al-Haram."

Ibn Kathir and the people of Basra read "masjid Allah" in the singular, meaning the Masjid al-Haram, in accordance with His saying: ﴿and the maintenance of the Masjid al-Haram﴾, and His saying: ﴿So let them not approach the Masjid al-Haram﴾. The others read ﴿masajid Allah﴾ in the plural, and what is meant by it is also the Masjid al-Haram. al-Hasan said: He said "masajid" (plural) because it is the qiblah of all mosques. al-Farra' said: The Arabs sometimes treat the singular as plural and the plural as singular; do you not see that a man rides a barbary horse (birdhawn) and says: "I have taken to riding barbary horses"? And it is said: "So-and-so has much dirham and dinar," meaning dirhams and dinars.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿testifying against themselves with disbelief﴾. He meant: "while they are witnesses." When "wahum" was dropped, the word took the accusative. al-Hasan said: They did not say "we are disbelievers," but their speech of disbelief is a witness against them of disbelief.

al-Dahhak reported from Ibn 'Abbas: Their testimony against themselves of disbelief is their prostration to idols. That is because the disbelievers of Quraysh had set up their idols outside the Sacred House near the foundations, and they used to circumambulate the House naked; whenever they completed a circuit they prostrated to their idols, and they did not increase thereby in nearness to Allah, may He be exalted, but only in distance.

al-Suddi said: Their testimony against themselves of disbelief is that the Christian is asked, "Who are you?" and he says, "I am a Christian," and the Jew says, "I am a Jew," and the polytheist is asked, "What is your religion?" and he says, "A polytheist." Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Those—their deeds have become void﴾, because they were for other than Allah, mighty and majestic, ﴿and in the Fire they will abide eternally﴾.

al-Kalbi reported from Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas: its meaning is "testifying against their messenger with disbelief," because there is no womb but that it bore him.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Only those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, establish the prayer, give the zakah, and fear none but Allah, will maintain the mosques of Allah.﴾ He did not fear anyone but Allah in matters of religion, and he did not abandon the command of Allah out of fear of anyone else. ﴿It is hoped that those will be among the guided.﴾ The word "'asā" (perhaps, it is hoped), when it comes from Allah, is binding. That is, they are indeed the guided ones, and the guided ones are those who hold firmly to the obedience of Allah, mighty and majestic is He, which leads to Paradise.

Abu Amr Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Nasawi informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Hiri narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us: Ahmad ibn al-Faraj al-Hijazi narrated to us: Baqiyyah narrated to us: Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mahdi narrated to us, from Amr ibn al-Harith, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When you see a man who attends the mosque regularly, then testify to his faith." Then Allah said: ﴿Only those who believe in Allah and the Last Day will maintain the mosques of Allah.﴾ [[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi in al-Iman, chapter on what has been related concerning the sanctity of prayer: 7/366, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith." And in the tafsir of Surah al-Tawbah: 8/490, and he said: "Hasan gharib." Also Ibn Majah in al-Masajid, chapter on remaining in the mosques and awaiting the prayer, no. 802: 1/263. Also al-Darimi in al-Salah, chapter on guarding the prayers: 1/222. Ibn Hibban authenticated it, p. 99 of Mawarid al-Zaman. Also al-Hakim: 1/212, 2/232, and al-Dhahabi criticized it, saying: "Darraj has many munkar narrations." Also recorded by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 3/68, 76, and al-Albani weakened it in his commentary on al-Mishkat: 1/244 and in Silsilat al-Da'ifah: 4/178.]].

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Ali ibn Abd Allah narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Mutarrif narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Aslam, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever goes to the mosque in the morning or in the evening, Allah prepares for him a place of hospitality in Paradise each time he goes in the morning or in the evening." [[Recorded by al-Bukhari in Salat al-Jama'ah, chapter on the virtue of one who goes to the mosque in the morning or evening: 2/148. Also Muslim in al-Masajid, chapter on walking to the prayer, by which sins are erased, no. 669: 1/463. Also al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/352.]].

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an informed us: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar al-Rayyani narrated to us: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh narrated to us: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far: my father narrated to me, from Mahmud ibn Labid, that Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him) wanted to build the mosque, but the people disliked that and preferred that he leave it. Uthman said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Whoever builds a mosque for Allah, Allah will build for him one like it in Paradise." [[Recorded by al-Bukhari in al-Salah, chapter on whoever builds a mosque: 1/544. Also Muslim in al-Masajid, chapter on the virtue of building mosques, no. 533: 1/378, in similar wording. Also al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/347.]].

And Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us: Abu Tahir al-Ziyadi informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan informed us: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Darabjirdi narrated to us: Abu Asim narrated to us with this same chain, and he said: "Allah builds for him a house in Paradise." [[See the same previous references.]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 19:

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Do you consider the giving of drink to the pilgrims and the maintaining of the Sacred Mosque﴾ — the verse.

Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us: Abu Ishaq Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha'labi related to us: Abdullah ibn Hamid ibn Muhammad al-Warran related to us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ubayd Allah al-Mu'afiri related to us: Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn al-Ash'ath al-Sijistani related to us: Abu Tawba al-Rabi' ibn Nafi' al-Halabi related to us: Mu'awiya ibn Salam related to us, from Zayd ibn Salam, from Abu Salam, who said: al-Nu'man ibn Bashir related to us, saying: I was beside the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when a man said: "I do not care if I do no deed after giving drink to the pilgrims." Another said: "I do not care if I do no deed after building up the Sacred Mosque." Another said: "Jihad in the way of Allah is better than what you two have said." So Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) rebuked them and said: "Do not raise your voices beside the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and it is the day of Friday. But when I have prayed, I will go in and ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about what you have disputed." So he did, and Allah, mighty and majestic, sent down: "Do you consider the giving of drink to the pilgrims and the maintaining of the Sacred Mosque as [equal to] one who believes in Allah and the Last Day and strives in the way of Allah? They are not equal in the sight of Allah, and Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people" [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Imara, chapter on the virtue of martyrdom in the way of Allah, no. (1879): 3/1499, and al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul p. (279).]].

Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: al-Abbas, when he was taken captive on the day of Badr, said: "If you have preceded us in Islam, emigration and jihad, then we used to maintain the Sacred Mosque and give drink to the pilgrims." So Allah, exalted, sent down this verse, and He informed that their maintaining of the Sacred Mosque and their attending to the water-giving does not benefit them along with polytheism in Allah, and that belief in Allah and jihad alongside the Prophet (ﷺ) is better than what they were upon [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 14/170; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi p. (279).]].

Al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: it was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib, al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and Talha ibn Shayba, who boasted. Talha said: "I am the keeper of the House; its key is in my hand." Al-Abbas said: "I am the keeper of the water-giving and the one in charge of it." Ali said: "I do not know what you are saying. I prayed toward the qibla six months before the people, and I am the one devoted to jihad." So Allah, mighty and majestic, sent down this verse: ﴿Do you consider the giving of drink to the pilgrims﴾ [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 14/171, and al-Wahidi pp. (279-280). Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya said in "Minhaj al-Sunna al-Nabawiyya" (5/18-19), the Imam University edition: "This wording is not known in any of the reliable books of hadith, and the signs of its falsehood are clear. Among them: Talha ibn Shayba does not exist; rather the servant of the Ka'ba was Shayba ibn Uthman ibn Abi Talha, and this shows you that the hadith is not sound. ... And Ali's saying, 'I prayed six months before the people,' is something whose falsehood is known necessarily, for between his Islam and the Islam of Zayd and Abu Bakr and Khadija there was a day or so; how then could he pray six months before the people?"]].

Al-siqaya (the giving of drink) is a verbal noun, like al-ri'aya (the tending) and al-himaya (the protecting).

His saying: ﴿and the maintaining of the Sacred Mosque as [equal to] one who believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾ — there is an ellipsis in it; its estimated sense is: "Do you consider the giving of drink to the pilgrims and the maintaining of the Sacred Mosque as equal to the faith of one who believes in Allah and the jihad of one who strives in the way of Allah?"

It is said: al-siqaya and al-'imara are in the sense of al-saqi (the one who gives drink) and al-'amir (the one who maintains). Its estimated sense is: "Do you consider the givers of drink to the pilgrims and the maintainers of the Sacred Mosque as equal to one who believes in Allah and the Last Day and strives in the way of Allah?" This is like His saying, exalted: ﴿and the good end is for the God-fearing﴾, meaning "for those who fear God." This is supported by the reading of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr and Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "Do you consider the suqat (givers of drink) of the pilgrims and the 'amara (maintainers) of the Sacred Mosque," in the plural of saqi and 'amir.

﴿Not equal in the sight of Allah are those who believe in Allah and the Last Day and strive in the way of Allah, and Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim related to me: Abu Usama related to us: Yahya ibn Muhallab related to us, from Husayn, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to the water-station and asked for a drink. al-Abbas said: "O Fadl, go to your mother and bring the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a drink from her." He said: "Give me to drink." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, they put their hands in it." He said: "Give me to drink." So he drank from it. Then he came to Zamzam, where they were giving drink and working in it. He said: "Carry on working, for you are upon a righteous work." Then he said: "Were it not that you would be overpowered, I would have descended and placed the rope upon this," and he pointed to his shoulder [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Hajj, chapter on the water-giving of the pilgrims: 3/491.]].

Isma'il ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us: Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi related to us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan related to us, from Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj: Muhammad ibn Minhal al-Darir related to me: Yazid ibn Zurayʻ related to us: Humayd al-Tawil related to us, from Bakr ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani, who said: I was sitting with Ibn Abbas by the Ka'ba when a Bedouin came to him and said: "Why do I see your paternal cousins giving drink of honey and milk, while you give drink of nabidh? Is it from need, or from miserliness?" Ibn Abbas said: "Praise be to Allah, we have neither need nor miserliness. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived on his mount with Usama behind him, and asked for a drink. We brought him a vessel of nabidh, and he drank and gave the remainder to Usama, and said: 'You have done well and excellently; so do likewise.' We do not wish to change what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded." [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Hajj, chapter on the obligation of spending the nights at Mina during the days of tashriq, no. (1316): 2/953.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 20–23:

Allah's statement: ﴿Those who believe, emigrate, and strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives are greater in rank﴾ in virtue ﴿with Allah﴾ than those who boast of providing water for the pilgrims and of maintaining the Sacred Mosque.

﴿And those are the ones who will be the triumphant﴾, the ones who are saved from the Fire.

﴿O you who believe, do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies﴾. Mujahid said: This verse is connected to what precedes it. It was revealed concerning the story of al-Abbas and Talhah and their refusal to emigrate [[Tafsir al-Tabari (a classical exegesis of the Qur'an): 14/176. He attributed it to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/157.]].

Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded the people to emigrate to Medina, some of them were clung to by their families and children, who would say: "We implore you by Allah not to abandon us." He would then take pity on them, remain with them, and give up emigration. So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed this verse [[Mentioned by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 280). Ibn Hajar attributed it to al-Tha'labi through the narration of Juwaybir from al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas. See: al-Kafi al-Shafi (p. 74).]].

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning the nine men who apostatized from Islam and joined Mecca. Allah forbade taking them as ﴿intimates and friends﴾, so Allah revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies﴾ [[Ibn Hajar attributed it to al-Tha'labi. The same reference.]] as intimates and friends, for you would then reveal your secrets to them and prefer remaining with them over emigration. ﴿If they prefer disbelief over faith﴾, that is, choose it ﴿and whoever of you takes them as allies﴾,

by informing them of the weaknesses of the Muslims and preferring to remain with them over emigration and jihad, ﴿then those are the wrongdoers﴾. At that time, faith was not accepted except from one who emigrated. This is the meaning of His statement: ﴿Then those are the wrongdoers﴾.

It was revealed concerning the story of al-Abbas and Talhah and their refusal to emigrate [[Tafsir al-Tabari (a classical exegesis of the Qur'an): 14/176. He attributed it to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/157.]].

Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded the people to emigrate to Medina, some of them were clung to by their families and children, who would say: "We implore you by Allah not to abandon us." He would then take pity on them, remain with them, and give up emigration. So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed this verse [[Mentioned by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 280). Ibn Hajar attributed it to al-Tha'labi through the narration of Juwaybir from al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas. See: al-Kafi al-Shafi (p. 74).]].

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning the nine men who apostatized from Islam and joined Mecca. Allah forbade taking them as ﴿intimates and friends﴾, so Allah revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies﴾ [[Ibn Hajar attributed it to al-Tha'labi. The same reference.]] as intimates and friends, for you would then reveal your secrets to them and prefer remaining with them over emigration. ﴿If they prefer disbelief over faith﴾, that is, choose it ﴿and whoever of you takes them as allies﴾,

by informing them of the weaknesses of the Muslims and preferring to remain with them over emigration and jihad, ﴿then those are the wrongdoers﴾. At that time, faith was not accepted except from one who emigrated. This is the meaning of His statement: ﴿Then those are the wrongdoers﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 20–23:

Allah's statement: ﴿Those who believe, emigrate, and strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives are greater in rank﴾ in virtue ﴿with Allah﴾ than those who boast of providing water for the pilgrims and of maintaining the Sacred Mosque.

﴿And those are the ones who will be the triumphant﴾, the ones who are saved from the Fire.

﴿O you who believe, do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies﴾. Mujahid said: This verse is connected to what precedes it. It was revealed concerning the story of al-Abbas and Talhah and their refusal to emigrate [[Tafsir al-Tabari (a classical exegesis of the Qur'an): 14/176. He attributed it to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/157.]].

Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded the people to emigrate to Medina, some of them were clung to by their families and children, who would say: "We implore you by Allah not to abandon us." He would then take pity on them, remain with them, and give up emigration. So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed this verse [[Mentioned by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 280). Ibn Hajar attributed it to al-Tha'labi through the narration of Juwaybir from al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas. See: al-Kafi al-Shafi (p. 74).]].

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning the nine men who apostatized from Islam and joined Mecca. Allah forbade taking them as ﴿intimates and friends﴾, so Allah revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies﴾ [[Ibn Hajar attributed it to al-Tha'labi. The same reference.]] as intimates and friends, for you would then reveal your secrets to them and prefer remaining with them over emigration. ﴿If they prefer disbelief over faith﴾, that is, choose it ﴿and whoever of you takes them as allies﴾,

by informing them of the weaknesses of the Muslims and preferring to remain with them over emigration and jihad, ﴿then those are the wrongdoers﴾. At that time, faith was not accepted except from one who emigrated. This is the meaning of His statement: ﴿Then those are the wrongdoers﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 24–25 (part 1 of 2):

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to those who stayed behind from the Hijrah (migration to Madinah): ﴿If your fathers﴾. This is because when the first verse was revealed, those who had accepted Islam but had not emigrated said: "If we emigrate, our wealth will be lost, our trade will perish, our houses will be ruined, and we will sever our ties of kinship." So He revealed: ﴿Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your spouses, and your kinsfolk﴾. Abu Bakr, on the authority of Asim, recited "'ashiratukum" (with an alif, in the plural), while the others recited it without an alif, in the singular. The plural of 'ashirah (kinsfolk) is 'asha'ir. ﴿And wealth you have acquired﴾, meaning, that you have earned; ﴿and commerce whose slump you fear﴾, ﴿and dwellings you are pleased with﴾, that is, those you find pleasant, meaning the palaces and homes; ﴿are more beloved to you than Allah and His Messenger and jihad in His cause, then wait﴾, meaning, then await, ﴿until Allah brings His command﴾. Ata said: "His decree." Mujahid and Muqatil said: "The conquest of Makkah." This is a command of warning. ﴿And Allah does not guide﴾, meaning, does not grant success or guidance, ﴿the defiant people﴾, meaning those who go out of obedience.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah has already given you victory in many battlefields﴾, meaning, in many occasions of battle, ﴿and on the day of Hunayn﴾. Hunayn is a valley between Makkah and al-Ta'if. Urwah said: "It is beside Dhu al-Majaz."

The account of Hunayn, as the narrators related it [[See: Sirat Ibn Hisham: 2/437 onwards; al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/158 onwards.]], is that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered Makkah with a few days of the month of Ramadan remaining, then he went out to Hunayn to fight Hawazin and Thaqif with twelve thousand men: ten thousand from the Muhajirun and two thousand from the Tulaqa (those freed at the conquest). Ata said: "They were sixteen thousand."

Al-Kalbi said: "They were ten thousand, and they were then more numerous than they had ever been. The polytheists were four thousand from Hawazin and Thaqif. Over Hawazin was Malik ibn Awf al-Nasri, and over Thaqif was Kinanah ibn Abd Yalil al-Thaqafi. When the two hosts met, a man from the Ansar called Salamah ibn Salamah ibn Waqsh said: 'We will not be defeated today through lack of numbers.' This displeased the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they were left to the words of that man." In another narration: "Allah did not approve of his saying, and He left them to themselves, so they fought a fierce battle. The polytheists were routed and abandoned the women and children. Then they called out: 'O defenders of the army, remember the disgrace!' They rallied, and the Muslims were routed."

Qatadah said: "It was mentioned to us that the Tulaqa fled that day with the people, and when the people fled, they fled."

Ismail ibn Abd al-Qahir [Abd al-Aziz informed us] [[Omitted from "B".]] informed us: Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj informed us: Yahya ibn Yahya informed us: Abu Khaythamah informed us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: A man said to al-Bara' ibn Azib: "O Abu 'Imarah, did you flee on the day of Hunayn?" He said: "No, by Allah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not turn his back. But the young and light-armed of his companions went out, unarmed or with little armor, and they encountered a people who were archers, from whom no arrow fell in vain, namely Hawazin and Banu Nasr. They shot at them with a volley that almost never missed. Then they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on his white mule, with Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib leading it. He dismounted, sought help, and said: 'I am the Prophet, there is no lie. I am the son of Abd al-Muttalib.' Then he arranged them [[Narrated by Muslim in Kitab al-Jihad wa al-Siyar, Bab Ghazwat Hunayn, no. (1776): 3/1400.]]."

Muhammad ibn Isma'il [al-Bukhari] narrated it from Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, from Israil, from Abu Ishaq, and added: "No one was seen among the people that day who was more fierce than him" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Jihad, Bab man qal: khudha wa ana ibn fulan..., 6/164.]].

Zakariyya narrated it from Abu Ishaq and added: al-Bara' said: "When the fighting grew fierce, we would seek protection by him, and the bravest of us was the one who stood beside him," meaning the Prophet (ﷺ) [[Narrated by Muslim in the previous place: 3/1401.]].

Shu'bah narrated from Abu Ishaq, who said: al-Bara' said: "Hawazin were a people of archers. When we met them, we charged against them, and they were routed. The Muslims turned to the spoils, and they met us with arrows. As for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he did not flee."

Al-Kalbi said: "Around the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) there were three hundred Muslims, and the rest of the people were routed."

Others said: "On that day, there remained with the Prophet (ﷺ) none except al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith, and Ayman ibn Umm Ayman, and Ayman was killed that day before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

Ismail ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us: Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan [[1]]informed us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj said: Abu Tahir Ahmad ibn Amr ibn Sarh informed us: Abu Wahb informed us: Yunus informed us, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, who said: Kathir ibn Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib told me, saying: al-Abbas said: "I witnessed the day of Hunayn with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith and I stayed close to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and did not leave him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was on a white mule that Farwah ibn Nafathah al-Judhami had given him as a gift. When the Muslims and the disbelievers met, the Muslims turned and fled. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began to urge his mule toward the disbelievers, while I was holding the bridle of the Messenger of Allah's mule, restraining it so that it would not speed up, and Abu Sufyan was holding its stirrup. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O Abbas, call out to the companions of the Samurah (tree).' Al-Abbas, who had a loud voice, said: 'I called with the top of my voice: Where are the companions of the Samurah?' He said: 'By Allah, as soon as they heard my voice, they turned back as a cow turns to its calves, and they said: Here we are, here we are!' He said: 'They fought the disbelievers, and the call was among the Ansar: O assembly of the Ansar, O assembly of the Ansar! Then the call was limited to Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked, while on his mule, as one who stretches up toward their fighting, and said: 'Now the oven has become hot.' [[This expression is only heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Al-watis is a pit dug in the ground, in which a fire is lit, its top made small, with holes for smoke, then meat is placed in it and sealed, and it is taken out the next day, the meat cooked but not burnt, and its flesh roasted. It is used as a metaphor for the intensity of war.]] Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took some pebbles and threw them at the faces of the disbelievers, then said: 'They are routed, by the Lord of Muhammad!' I went to look, and the fighting was in its former state, as far as I could see. He said: 'By Allah, it was only that when he threw the pebbles at them, I kept seeing their edge blunted and their affair turned back' [[Narrated by Muslim in Kitab al-Jihad wa al-Siyar, Bab fi Ghazwat Hunayn, no. (1775): 3/1398-1399; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/31-32.]]."

Salamah ibn al-Akwa' said: "We fought with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at Hunayn. When they came upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he dismounted from the mule, then took a handful of dust from the earth, then faced it toward their faces and said: 'Shahat al-wujuh' (may the faces be disfigured). Not a single person whom Allah created from them was spared without his eyes being filled with dust from that handful. They turned back in flight, and Allah, mighty and majestic, routed them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divided their spoils among the Muslims" [[Narrated by Muslim in the previous place, no. (1777): 3/1402.]].

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Allah, exalted is He, reinforced His Prophet (ﷺ) with five thousand angels marked for battle" [[Attributed by al-Suyuti to Ibn Abi Hatim. al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/161.]].

It is related in a report that a man from Banu Nadr called Shajarah said to the believers after the fighting: "Where are the dappled horses and the men who wore white garments? We did not see you among them except like a mole's spot, and we were not slain except by their hands!" They informed the Prophet (ﷺ) of that, and he said: "Those were the angels."

al-Zuhri said: "It reached me that Shaybah ibn Uthman ibn Talhah [[See: Sirat Ibn Hisham: 2/444.]] said: 'On the day of Hunayn I stood behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), intending to kill him, to avenge Talhah ibn Uthman and Uthman ibn Talhah, who had both been killed on the day of Uhud. Allah informed His Messenger (ﷺ) of what was in my mind. He turned to me, struck my chest, and said: "I seek refuge for you in Allah, O Shaybah." My sinews trembled, and I looked at him, and he was dearer to me than my hearing and sight. I said: "I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah, and that Allah has informed you of what is in my mind."'"

When Allah routed the polytheists and they turned back in flight, they went on until they reached Awtas, where their families and wealth were. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a man from the Ash'ariyyin called Abu Amir and appointed him over the army of the Muslims to Awtas. He went to them, and they fought. Durayd ibn al-Simmah was killed, and Allah routed the polytheists, and the Muslims took their families captive. Their commander Malik ibn Awf al-Nasri fled and came to al-Ta'if, where he fortified himself. His wealth and family were taken among those seized. The commander of the Muslims, Abu Amir, was killed [[Sirat Ibn Hisham: 2/449, 453; Tabaqat Ibn Sa'd: 2/151-152.]].

al-Zuhri said: "Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib informed me that they took six thousand captives that day. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to al-Ta'if and besieged them for the rest of that month. When Dhu al-Qa'dah, which is a sacred month, came, he withdrew from them. He came to al-Ji'ranah, where he entered the state of ihram for a 'umrah, and he distributed there the spoils of Hunayn and Awtas, and he won over some people, among them Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, al-Harith ibn Hisham, Suhayl ibn Amr, and al-Aqra' ibn Habis, and he gave them" [[See: Imta' al-Asma' by al-Maqrizi: 1/422-423.]].

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliki informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Abu al-Yaman informed us: Shu'ayb informed us: al-Zuhri informed us: Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, informed me that some people from the Ansar said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when Allah had bestowed upon His Messenger from the wealth of Hawazin what He bestowed, and he began to give men from Quraysh a hundred camels each: "May Allah forgive the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He gives to Quraysh and leaves us, while our swords are dripping with their blood?" Anas said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was told of their saying, so he sent for the Ansar and gathered them in a leather tent, and he invited no one else with them. When they had gathered, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to them and said: 'What is this word that has reached me from you?' Their jurists said to him: 'As for the men of judgment among us, O Messenger of Allah, they said nothing. But as for some of us who were young, they said: May Allah forgive the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He gives to Quraysh and leaves the Ansar, while our swords are dripping with their blood.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'I give to men who are recent in disbelief. Are you not pleased that the people go away with the wealth, while you return to your homes with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? By Allah, what you return with is better than what they return with.' They said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah, we are pleased.' He said to them: 'You will see after me a great preference given to others, so be patient until you meet Allah and His Messenger at the Pool.'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Fard al-Khums, Bab ma kana al-Nabi (ﷺ) yu'ti al-mu'allafah, 6/250-251; and Muslim in al-Zakah, Bab i'ta' al-mu'allafah qulubuhum, no. (1059): 2/733-734.]].

Al-Baghawi cites Yunus, from Ibn Shihab: "I give to men who are recent in their disbelief, to win their hearts," and he said: "Then be patient until you meet Allah and His Messenger, for I will be at the Basin." They said: "We will be patient."[[In the narration of Muslim, in the same place cited above.]]

Abdul-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) narrated to us: Wuhayb narrated to us: Amr ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Abbad ibn Tamim, from Abdullah ibn Zayd ibn Asim, who said:

When Allah bestowed the spoils (fay') upon His Messenger (ﷺ) on the day of Hunayn, he distributed among the people, giving to those whose hearts were to be won (al-mu'allafah qulubuhum)[[Al-Mu'allafah qulubuhum: those whose hearts were to be reconciled or won over to Islam, a category of recipients of zakat.]], and he gave nothing to the Ansar. So they seemed displeased, because what had befallen the people had not befallen them. He addressed them and said: "O assembly of the Ansar! Did I not find you misguided, and Allah guided you through me? Were you not divided, and Allah united you through me? Were you not in need, and Allah made you wealthy through me?" Whenever he said something, they replied: "Allah and His Messenger are the most gracious." He said: "What prevents you from answering the Messenger of Allah? Whenever he says something, you say: 'Allah and His Messenger are the most gracious.'" He said: "Had you wished, you could have said: 'You came to us rejected and we gave you refuge, you came to us in need and we consoled you, you came in fear and we gave you security.' Are you pleased that the people should go away with sheep and camels, while you go away with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to your homes? Were it not for the migration (hijrah), I would have been a man of the Ansar. If the people were to take a valley or a mountain pass, I would take the valley of the Ansar and their pass. The Ansar are the inner garment, and the people are the outer garment. You will encounter after me a time of favoritism (athrah), so be patient until you meet me at the Basin."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter on the Battle of al-Ta'if: 8/47; by Muslim in al-Zakat, chapter on giving to those whose hearts are to be won over to Islam, no. (1061): 2/738; and by the author (al-Baghawi) in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/34.]]

Ismail ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us: Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan narrated to us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us: Muhammad ibn [folio 155a] Abi Umar al-Makki narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Umar ibn Sa'id ibn Masruq, from his father, from Ubayah ibn Rifa'ah, from Rafi' ibn Khadij (may Allah be pleased with him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, Safwan ibn Umayyah, Uyaynah ibn Hisn, and al-Aqra' ibn Habis one hundred camels each, and he gave Abbas ibn Mirdas less than that. Abbas ibn Mirdas said:

"Neither Hisn nor Habis
Surpass Mirdas in the assembly.
Will you place my share and the share of the (other) lineage
Between Uyaynah and al-Aqra'?
I was not below any one of them,
And whoever is lowered today will not be raised."

He said: So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) completed one hundred for him.[[Narrated by Muslim in the same place, no. (1060): 2/737.]]

In the hadith also: some people from Hawazin came later as Muslims and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you are the best and most generous of people, and our sons, our women, and our wealth have been taken."[[Mentioned by al-Tha'labi without a chain. Ibn Ishaq and Musa ibn Uqbah mentioned it at length in their accounts of the campaigns. See: al-Kafi al-Shaf p. (74); Fath al-Bari: 8/38.]]

Abdul-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) narrated to us: Sa'id ibn Ufayr narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to me: Aqil narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, that Marwan and al-Miswar ibn Makhramah informed him that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up when the delegation of Hawazin came to him as Muslims, and they asked him to return to them their property and their captives. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "I have with me those whom you see, and the most beloved speech to me is the most truthful. Choose one of the two groups: either the captives or the wealth." They said: "We choose our captives." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, praised Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with what is fitting for Him, and then said: "To proceed: these brothers of yours have come repentant, and I have decided to return their captives to them. Whoever among you loves to make this good for them, let him do so. And whoever wishes to remain with his share until we give it to him from the first of what Allah grants us as spoils, let him do so." The people said: "We have made it good (for them)."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 24–25 (part 1 of 2):

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to those who stayed behind from the Hijrah (migration to Madinah): ﴿If your fathers﴾. This is because when the first verse was revealed, those who had accepted Islam but had not emigrated said: "If we emigrate, our wealth will be lost, our trade will perish, our houses will be ruined, and we will sever our ties of kinship." Al-Kalbi said: "They were ten thousand, and they were then more numerous than they had ever been. The polytheists were four thousand from Hawazin and Thaqif. Then they called out: 'O defenders of the army, remember the disgrace!' They rallied, and the Muslims were routed."

Ismail ibn Abd al-Qahir [Abd al-Aziz informed us] [[Omitted from "B".]] informed us: Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj informed us: Yahya ibn Yahya informed us: Abu Khaythamah informed us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: A man said to al-Bara' ibn Azib: "O Abu 'Imarah, did you flee on the day of Hunayn?" They shot at them with a volley that almost never missed. Then they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on his white mule, with Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib leading it.
