Then he arranged them [[Narrated by Muslim in Kitab al-Jihad wa al-Siyar, Bab Ghazwat Hunayn, no. (1776): 3/1400.]]."

Muhammad ibn Isma'il [al-Bukhari] narrated it from Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, from Israil, from Abu Ishaq, and added: "No one was seen among the people that day who was more fierce than him" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Jihad, Bab man qal: khudha wa ana ibn fulan..., 6/164.]].

Zakariyya narrated it from Abu Ishaq and added: al-Bara' said: "When the fighting grew fierce, we would seek protection by him, and the bravest of us was the one who stood beside him," meaning the Prophet (ﷺ) [[Narrated by Muslim in the previous place: 3/1401.]].

Shu'bah narrated from Abu Ishaq, who said: al-Bara' said: "Hawazin were a people of archers. When we met them, we charged against them, and they were routed. The Muslims turned to the spoils, and they met us with arrows. As for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he did not flee."

Al-Kalbi said: "Around the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) there were three hundred Muslims, and the rest of the people were routed."

Others said: "On that day, there remained with the Prophet (ﷺ) none except al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith, and Ayman ibn Umm Ayman, and Ayman was killed that day before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

Ismail ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us: Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan [[1]]informed us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj said: Abu Tahir Ahmad ibn Amr ibn Sarh informed us: Abu Wahb informed us: Yunus informed us, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, who said: Kathir ibn Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib told me, saying: al-Abbas said: "I witnessed the day of Hunayn with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith and I stayed close to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and did not leave him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was on a white mule that Farwah ibn Nafathah al-Judhami had given him as a gift. When the Muslims and the disbelievers met, the Muslims turned and fled. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began to urge his mule toward the disbelievers, while I was holding the bridle of the Messenger of Allah's mule, restraining it so that it would not speed up, and Abu Sufyan was holding its stirrup. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O Abbas, call out to the companions of the Samurah (tree).' Al-Abbas, who had a loud voice, said: 'I called with the top of my voice: Where are the companions of the Samurah?' He said: 'By Allah, as soon as they heard my voice, they turned back as a cow turns to its calves, and they said: Here we are, here we are!' He said: 'They fought the disbelievers, and the call was among the Ansar: O assembly of the Ansar, O assembly of the Ansar! Then the call was limited to Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked, while on his mule, as one who stretches up toward their fighting, and said: 'Now the oven has become hot.' [[This expression is only heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Al-watis is a pit dug in the ground, in which a fire is lit, its top made small, with holes for smoke, then meat is placed in it and sealed, and it is taken out the next day, the meat cooked but not burnt, and its flesh roasted. It is used as a metaphor for the intensity of war.]] Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took some pebbles and threw them at the faces of the disbelievers, then said: 'They are routed, by the Lord of Muhammad!' I went to look, and the fighting was in its former state, as far as I could see. He said: 'By Allah, it was only that when he threw the pebbles at them, I kept seeing their edge blunted and their affair turned back' [[Narrated by Muslim in Kitab al-Jihad wa al-Siyar, Bab fi Ghazwat Hunayn, no. (1775): 3/1398-1399; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/31-32.]]."

Salamah ibn al-Akwa' said: "We fought with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at Hunayn. When they came upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he dismounted from the mule, then took a handful of dust from the earth, then faced it toward their faces and said: 'Shahat al-wujuh' (may the faces be disfigured). Not a single person whom Allah created from them was spared without his eyes being filled with dust from that handful. They turned back in flight, and Allah, mighty and majestic, routed them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) divided their spoils among the Muslims" [[Narrated by Muslim in the previous place, no. (1777): 3/1402.]].

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Allah, exalted is He, reinforced His Prophet (ﷺ) with five thousand angels marked for battle" [[Attributed by al-Suyuti to Ibn Abi Hatim. al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/161.]].

It is related in a report that a man from Banu Nadr called Shajarah said to the believers after the fighting: "Where are the dappled horses and the men who wore white garments? We did not see you among them except like a mole's spot, and we were not slain except by their hands!" They informed the Prophet (ﷺ) of that, and he said: "Those were the angels."

al-Zuhri said: "It reached me that Shaybah ibn Uthman ibn Talhah [[See: Sirat Ibn Hisham: 2/444.]] said: 'On the day of Hunayn I stood behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), intending to kill him, to avenge Talhah ibn Uthman and Uthman ibn Talhah, who had both been killed on the day of Uhud. Allah informed His Messenger (ﷺ) of what was in my mind. He turned to me, struck my chest, and said: "I seek refuge for you in Allah, O Shaybah." My sinews trembled, and I looked at him, and he was dearer to me than my hearing and sight. I said: "I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah, and that Allah has informed you of what is in my mind."'"

When Allah routed the polytheists and they turned back in flight, they went on until they reached Awtas, where their families and wealth were. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a man from the Ash'ariyyin called Abu Amir and appointed him over the army of the Muslims to Awtas. He went to them, and they fought. Durayd ibn al-Simmah was killed, and Allah routed the polytheists, and the Muslims took their families captive. Their commander Malik ibn Awf al-Nasri fled and came to al-Ta'if, where he fortified himself. His wealth and family were taken among those seized. The commander of the Muslims, Abu Amir, was killed [[Sirat Ibn Hisham: 2/449, 453; Tabaqat Ibn Sa'd: 2/151-152.]].

al-Zuhri said: "Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib informed me that they took six thousand captives that day. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to al-Ta'if and besieged them for the rest of that month. When Dhu al-Qa'dah, which is a sacred month, came, he withdrew from them. He came to al-Ji'ranah, where he entered the state of ihram for a 'umrah, and he distributed there the spoils of Hunayn and Awtas, and he won over some people, among them Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, al-Harith ibn Hisham, Suhayl ibn Amr, and al-Aqra' ibn Habis, and he gave them" [[See: Imta' al-Asma' by al-Maqrizi: 1/422-423.]].

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliki informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Abu al-Yaman informed us: Shu'ayb informed us: al-Zuhri informed us: Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, informed me that some people from the Ansar said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when Allah had bestowed upon His Messenger from the wealth of Hawazin what He bestowed, and he began to give men from Quraysh a hundred camels each: "May Allah forgive the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He gives to Quraysh and leaves us, while our swords are dripping with their blood?" Anas said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was told of their saying, so he sent for the Ansar and gathered them in a leather tent, and he invited no one else with them. When they had gathered, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to them and said: 'What is this word that has reached me from you?' Their jurists said to him: 'As for the men of judgment among us, O Messenger of Allah, they said nothing. But as for some of us who were young, they said: May Allah forgive the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He gives to Quraysh and leaves the Ansar, while our swords are dripping with their blood.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'I give to men who are recent in disbelief. Are you not pleased that the people go away with the wealth, while you return to your homes with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? By Allah, what you return with is better than what they return with.' They said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah, we are pleased.' He said to them: 'You will see after me a great preference given to others, so be patient until you meet Allah and His Messenger at the Pool.'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Fard al-Khums, Bab ma kana al-Nabi (ﷺ) yu'ti al-mu'allafah, 6/250-251; and Muslim in al-Zakah, Bab i'ta' al-mu'allafah qulubuhum, no. (1059): 2/733-734.]].

Al-Baghawi cites Yunus, from Ibn Shihab: "I give to men who are recent in their disbelief, to win their hearts," and he said: "Then be patient until you meet Allah and His Messenger, for I will be at the Basin." They said: "We will be patient."[[In the narration of Muslim, in the same place cited above.]]

Abdul-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) narrated to us: Wuhayb narrated to us: Amr ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Abbad ibn Tamim, from Abdullah ibn Zayd ibn Asim, who said:

When Allah bestowed the spoils (fay') upon His Messenger (ﷺ) on the day of Hunayn, he distributed among the people, giving to those whose hearts were to be won (al-mu'allafah qulubuhum)[[Al-Mu'allafah qulubuhum: those whose hearts were to be reconciled or won over to Islam, a category of recipients of zakat.]], and he gave nothing to the Ansar. So they seemed displeased, because what had befallen the people had not befallen them. He addressed them and said: "O assembly of the Ansar! Did I not find you misguided, and Allah guided you through me? Were you not divided, and Allah united you through me? Were you not in need, and Allah made you wealthy through me?" Whenever he said something, they replied: "Allah and His Messenger are the most gracious." He said: "What prevents you from answering the Messenger of Allah? Whenever he says something, you say: 'Allah and His Messenger are the most gracious.'" He said: "Had you wished, you could have said: 'You came to us rejected and we gave you refuge, you came to us in need and we consoled you, you came in fear and we gave you security.' Are you pleased that the people should go away with sheep and camels, while you go away with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to your homes? Were it not for the migration (hijrah), I would have been a man of the Ansar. If the people were to take a valley or a mountain pass, I would take the valley of the Ansar and their pass. The Ansar are the inner garment, and the people are the outer garment. You will encounter after me a time of favoritism (athrah), so be patient until you meet me at the Basin."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter on the Battle of al-Ta'if: 8/47; by Muslim in al-Zakat, chapter on giving to those whose hearts are to be won over to Islam, no. (1061): 2/738; and by the author (al-Baghawi) in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/34.]]

Ismail ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us: Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan narrated to us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us: Muhammad ibn [folio 155a] Abi Umar al-Makki narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Umar ibn Sa'id ibn Masruq, from his father, from Ubayah ibn Rifa'ah, from Rafi' ibn Khadij (may Allah be pleased with him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, Safwan ibn Umayyah, Uyaynah ibn Hisn, and al-Aqra' ibn Habis one hundred camels each, and he gave Abbas ibn Mirdas less than that. Abbas ibn Mirdas said:

"Neither Hisn nor Habis
Surpass Mirdas in the assembly.
Will you place my share and the share of the (other) lineage
Between Uyaynah and al-Aqra'?
I was not below any one of them,
And whoever is lowered today will not be raised."

He said: So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) completed one hundred for him.[[Narrated by Muslim in the same place, no. (1060): 2/737.]]

In the hadith also: some people from Hawazin came later as Muslims and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you are the best and most generous of people, and our sons, our women, and our wealth have been taken."[[Mentioned by al-Tha'labi without a chain. Ibn Ishaq and Musa ibn Uqbah mentioned it at length in their accounts of the campaigns. See: al-Kafi al-Shaf p. (74); Fath al-Bari: 8/38.]]

Abdul-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) narrated to us: Sa'id ibn Ufayr narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to me: Aqil narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, that Marwan and al-Miswar ibn Makhramah informed him that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up when the delegation of Hawazin came to him as Muslims, and they asked him to return to them their property and their captives. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "I have with me those whom you see, and the most beloved speech to me is the most truthful. Choose one of the two groups: either the captives or the wealth." They said: "We choose our captives." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, praised Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with what is fitting for Him, and then said: "To proceed: these brothers of yours have come repentant, and I have decided to return their captives to them. Whoever among you loves to make this good for them, let him do so. And whoever wishes to remain with his share until we give it to him from the first of what Allah grants us as spoils, let him do so." The people said: "We have made it good (for them)."

"O Messenger of Allah!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We do not know which of you gave permission in that matter, and which did not. So return until your leaders (*'urafa'*, representatives) bring your matter to us." So the people returned, and their leaders spoke with them. Then they came back to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and informed him that they had given their consent and permission. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter on Allah's saying: "And on the day of Hunayn...": 8/32-33.]]

Then Allah the Exalted revealed, concerning the story of Hunayn: ﴿Allah had already given you victory on many battlefields, and on the day of Hunayn, when your great number made you vain,﴾ until you said, "We will not be overcome today for lack of numbers." ﴿But your great number availed you nothing﴾, meaning that victory does not come through numbers. ﴿And the earth, for all its vastness, was straitened for you﴾, meaning despite its breadth and expanse. ﴿Then you turned back in flight﴾, meaning routed.

﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down hosts that you did not see, and He punished those who disbelieved; and that is the recompense of the disbelievers.﴾

﴿Then Allah sent down﴾ after the defeat, ﴿His tranquility (sakinah)﴾, meaning security and calm. It is on the pattern fa'īlah, derived from al-sukūn (stillness). ﴿upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down hosts you did not see﴾, meaning the angels. It was said: they were not for fighting, but to strike terror into the disbelievers and to encourage the Muslims, because it is related that the angels fought only on the day of Badr. ﴿And He punished those who disbelieved﴾ by killing, capture, the taking of women and children captive, and the seizure of property. ﴿That is the recompense of the disbelievers.﴾

﴿Then Allah relents after that to whom He wills﴾, guiding him to Islam. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.﴾

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, the polytheists are only impure (najas)﴾, to the end of the verse. Al-Dahhak and Abu 'Ubaydah said: najas means filth. It was also said: it means wretched. It is a verbal noun (maṣdar) in which the masculine and feminine, the dual and the plural are alike. As for al-nijs, with a kasra on the nun and a sukun on the jim, it is not used on its own; one says rijs nijs (filth, impurity). When it is used alone, it is said najis, with a fatha on the nun and a kasra on the jim. What is meant is the impurity of ruling, not the impurity of the substance; they were called najas as a reproach. Qatadah said: He named them najas because they remain in a state of major impurity (janabah) and do not bathe, and they break their minor ablution and do not perform wudu'.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque﴾. He meant preventing them from entering the Haram (the sacred precinct of Makkah), because when they enter the Haram they have approached the Sacred Mosque. By it He meant the Haram, and this is like the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque﴾ [al-Isra' 1]; by it He meant the Haram, because he was taken by night from the house of Umm Hani'.

The Shaykh, the Imam, the most Majestic said: The whole of the lands of Islam, with regard to the disbelievers, are of three categories:

The first: the Haram. It is not permissible for a disbeliever to enter it under any circumstances, whether he is a dhimmi (a protected non-Muslim subject) or a musta'man (one granted temporary safe-conduct), on the apparent meaning of this verse. If a messenger comes from the lands of the disbelievers to the Imam while the Imam is in the Haram, he is not to be permitted to enter the Haram; rather, someone is sent out to him to hear his message outside the Haram. The people of Kufa permitted a mu'ahid (one under a treaty) to enter the Haram.

The second category of the lands of Islam: the Hijaz. It is permissible for a disbeliever to enter it with permission, but he may not stay in it for longer than the length of a journey, which is three days, on account of what is related from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "If I live, God willing, I will surely expel the Jews and the Christians from the Arabian Peninsula, until I leave none in it except a Muslim." [Reported by Muslim in al-Jihad, chapter on the expulsion of Jews and Christians from the Arabian Peninsula, no. (1767): 3/1388; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/182.] Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed away and gave instructions, saying: "Expel the polytheists from the Arabian Peninsula." [Reported by al-Bukhari in the chapter on the expulsion of Jews from the Arabian Peninsula in the Book of Jizyah: 6/271, in a lengthy form; and Muslim in the chapter on bequest, on not making a bequest for one who has nothing to bequeath, no. (1637): 3/1257-1258; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/180-181.] Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, did not have leisure for this, and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, expelled them during his caliphate, and he set a term of three days for any of them who came as a merchant. The Arabian Peninsula extends in length from the farthest part of 'Adan Abyan to the fertile lands of Iraq, and in breadth from Jeddah and what lies beside it on the sea coast to the borders of Syria.

The third category: the rest of the lands of Islam. It is permissible for a disbeliever to reside in them under dhimmah (protection) and aman (safe-conduct), but they may not enter the mosques except with the permission of a Muslim.

His saying: ﴿after this year of theirs﴾, meaning the year in which Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, led the pilgrimage with the people, and 'Ali, may Allah honor his face, proclaimed the Bara'ah (the declaration of disavowal), and that was in the ninth year after the Hijrah.

His saying: ﴿And if you fear poverty﴾. That was because the people of Makkah earned their livelihood from trade, and the polytheists used to bring food to Makkah and trade there. When they were prevented from entering the Haram, they feared poverty and straitened living, and they mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so Allah the Exalted sent down: ﴿And if you fear poverty﴾, meaning destitution and want. It is said: 'āla ya'īlu ʿaylah (he became poor). ﴿Then Allah will enrich you from His bounty, if He wills. Indeed Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾

'Ikrimah said: So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, enriched them by sending down rain upon them in abundance, so their good increased. Muqatil said: The people of Jeddah, San'a' and Jarish in Yemen embraced Islam and brought great quantities of provisions to Makkah, and Allah sufficed them for what they had feared. Al-Dahhak and Qatadah said: Allah compensated them for it with the jizyah (poll tax), and enriched them thereby.

﴿Then Allah sent down﴾ after the defeat, ﴿His tranquility (sakinah)﴾, meaning security and calm. It is on the pattern fa'īlah, derived from al-sukūn (stillness). ﴿upon His Messenger and upon the believers, and sent down hosts you did not see﴾, meaning the angels. It was said: they were not for fighting, but to strike terror into the disbelievers and to encourage the Muslims, because it is related that the angels fought only on the day of Badr. ﴿And He punished those who disbelieved﴾ by killing, capture, the taking of women and children captive, and the seizure of property. ﴿That is the recompense of the disbelievers.﴾

﴿Then Allah relents after that to whom He wills﴾, guiding him to Islam. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.﴾

The first: the Haram. His saying: ﴿after this year of theirs﴾, meaning the year in which Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, led the pilgrimage with the people, and 'Ali, may Allah honor his face, proclaimed the Bara'ah (the declaration of disavowal), and that was in the ninth year after the Hijrah.

His saying: ﴿And if you fear poverty﴾. That was because the people of Makkah earned their livelihood from trade, and the polytheists used to bring food to Makkah and trade there. When they were prevented from entering the Haram, they feared poverty and straitened living, and they mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so Allah the Exalted sent down: ﴿And if you fear poverty﴾, meaning destitution and want. It is said: 'āla ya'īlu ʿaylah (he became poor). ﴿Then Allah will enrich you from His bounty, if He wills. Indeed Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾

'Ikrimah said: So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, enriched them by sending down rain upon them in abundance, so their good increased. Muqatil said: The people of Jeddah, San'a' and Jarish in Yemen embraced Islam and brought great quantities of provisions to Makkah, and Allah sufficed them for what they had feared. Al-Dahhak and Qatadah said: Allah compensated them for it with the jizyah (poll tax), and enriched them thereby.

And this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in God﴾. Mujahid said: this verse was revealed when the Messenger of God ﷺ was commanded to fight the Romans, and after its revelation he undertook the expedition of Tabuk [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 4 / 167.]].

Al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning the Jews of Qurayza and al-Nadir. He made peace with them, and this was the first jizya (poll tax on non-Muslim subjects) that the people of Islam obtained, and the first humiliation that the People of the Book suffered at the hands of the Muslims.

God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in God and not in the Last Day﴾. If it is asked: do the People of the Book not believe in God and the Last Day? It is said: they do not believe as the believers believe, for when they say "Ezra is the son of God" and "the Messiah is the son of God," that is not belief in God.

﴿and do not forbid what God and His Messenger have forbidden, and do not adopt the religion of truth﴾. That is: they do not adopt the true religion; he attributed the noun to the adjective. Qatada said: "the Truth" is God, meaning they do not adopt the religion of God, and His religion is Islam. Abu 'Ubayda said: its meaning is that they do not obey God, exalted is He, with the obedience of the people of truth.

﴿of those who were given the Scripture﴾: meaning the Jews and the Christians.

﴿until they give the jizya﴾, which is the tribute imposed upon their necks. ﴿with willing submission (ʿan yadin)﴾: meaning under compulsion and humiliation. Abu 'Ubayda said: it is said of anyone who gives something unwillingly, without good will: he gave it ʿan yadin. Ibn 'Abbas said: they give it with their own hands, and they do not send it through the hand of another. It was also said: ʿan yadin means in cash, not on credit. It was also said: ʿan yadin means by acknowledging the favour of the Muslims upon them in accepting the jizya from them. ﴿while they are humbled (ṣāghirūn)﴾: abased and subdued. ʿIkrima said: they give the jizya standing, while the collector sits. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: it is taken from him and his neck is trampled.

Al-Kalbi said: when he gives it, he is slapped on the back of the neck.

It was also said: he is seized by his beard and struck on his jaws.

It was also said: he is seized by his collar and dragged forcibly to the place of payment.

It was also said: his giving it is itself the ṣaghar (humiliation).

Al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, said: the ṣaghar is the application of the rulings of Islam over them.

The community (ummah) agreed on the permissibility of taking the jizya from the People of the Two Books, namely the Jews and the Christians, provided they are not Arabs.

They differed concerning the Arab People of the Book and concerning non-People of the Book among the unbelieving non-Arabs. Al-Shafi'i held that the jizya is based on religion, not on lineage, so it is taken from the People of the Book whether they are Arabs or non-Arabs, and it is never taken from the people of idols under any circumstances. He argued that the Prophet ﷺ took it from Ukaydir of Dumah, who was a man of the Arabs, said to be of Ghassan, and he took it from the protected people of Yemen, most of whom were Arabs.

Malik and al-Awza'i held that it is taken from all unbelievers except the apostate.

Abu Hanifa said: it is taken from the People of the Book in general, it is taken from the polytheist non-Arabs, and it is not taken from the polytheist Arabs. Abu Yusuf said: it is not taken from an Arab, whether he is a People of the Book or a polytheist, and it is taken from a non-Arab, whether he is a People of the Book or a polytheist.

As for the Magians (Majus), the Companions, may God be pleased with them, agreed on taking the jizya from them.

ʿAbd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us, ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us, Abu al-ʿAbbas al-Asamm informed us, al-Rabiʿ informed us, al-Shafiʿi informed us, Sufyan informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Dinar, that he heard Bajala say: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, did not take the jizya from the Magians until ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf testified that the Prophet ﷺ had taken it from the Magians of Hajar [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Jizya and Truce, chapter on the jizya and truce with the protected people and the belligerents: 6 / 257.]].

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us, Zahir ibn Ahmad Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us, Abu Musʿab informed us, from Malik, from Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, from his father, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab mentioned the Magians and said: "I do not know how to deal with their affair." ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf said: "I testify that I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ say: 'Treat them as you treat the People of the Book'" [[Narrated by Malik in al-Muwatta', chapter on zakat: 1 / 278; al-Shafi'i: 2 / 130 (Tartib al-Musnad); Abu ʿUbayd in al-Amwal p. 42; Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf: 3 / 224; al-Khatib in Tarikh Baghdad: 10 / 88; al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 9 / 189; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11 / 169. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr said: this hadith is munqati' (broken in its chain), but its meaning is connected through good routes. See also: Nasb al-Rayah: 3 / 448-449; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 6 / 13; Irwa' al-Ghalil: 5 / 88.]].

Regarding ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, refraining from taking the jizya from the Magians until ʿAbd al-Rahman [ibn ʿAwf testified that the Prophet ﷺ had taken it from the Magians of Hajar, is evidence that the opinion of the Companions was that it is not taken from every polytheist, but only from the People of the Book [[The words between the brackets are missing from manuscript "A".]].

They differed over whether the Magians are among the People of the Book or not. It is related from ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, that he said: "They had a Book which they studied, then in the morning the night had passed over their Book and it was lifted from among them." [[This report from ʿAli, may God be pleased with him, was narrated by al-Shafi'i in al-Musnad: 2 / 131, and in its chain is Saʿid ibn al-Marzuban, who is weak (majruh). Yahya ibn Saʿid al-Qattan said: I do not consider it lawful to narrate from him. See: Nasb al-Rayah: 3 / 449-450.]]

They agreed on the prohibition of eating the slaughtered meat of the Magians and marrying their women, unlike the People of the Two Books.

As for those from other polytheists who entered the religion of the Jews and the Christians, the matter is examined: if they entered it before the abrogation (naskh) and alteration (tabdil), they are allowed to continue under the jizya, and their marriages and slaughter are lawful. If they entered their religion after the abrogation, with the coming of Muhammad ﷺ, they are not allowed to continue under the jizya, and their marriages and slaughter are not lawful. As for one whose entry, we are doubtful, was either after the abrogation or before it, he continues under the jizya, giving precedence to preserving life, and his marriages and slaughter are not lawful, giving precedence to prohibition. Among them are the Christian Arabs of the Tanukh, Bahra', and Banu Taghlib; ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, allowed them to continue under the jizya, and said: "Their slaughtered meat is not lawful for us."

As for the amount of the jizya: its minimum is one dinar, and it is not permitted to reduce it. A dinar is accepted from the poor, the wealthy, and the middling alike, on the basis of what Abu ʿUthman Saʿid ibn Isma'il al-Dabbi informed us: Abu Muhammad ʿAbd al-Jabbar ibn Muhammad al-Jarrahi informed us, Abu al-ʿAbbas Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mahbubi narrated to us, Abu ʿIsa al-Tirmidhi narrated to us, Mahmud ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Sufyan informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu Wa'il, from Masruq, from Muʿadh ibn Jabal, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ sent me to Yemen and commanded me to take from every adult male a dinar or its equivalent in Mu'afiri garments [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Zakat, chapter on what has come concerning the zakat of cattle: 3 / 257, and he said: this is a hasan hadith. Also by Abu Dawud in Imarah, chapter on taking the jizya: 4 / 249; al-Nasa'i in Zakat: 5 / 25-26; Ibn Hibban in Mawarid al-Zam'an p. 794; Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 5 / 230, 233; al-Hakim declared it sahih: 1 / 398; and the author narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11 / 172.]]. The Prophet ﷺ commanded him to take it from every ḥālim, that is, every adult, one dinar, and he did not distinguish between the rich, the poor, and the middling. This indicates that it is not obligatory on children, and likewise not obligatory on women; it is taken only from free, sane, adult men.

Some scholars held that it is four dinars on every wealthy person, two dinars on every person of middling means, and one dinar on every poor person. This is the view of the adherents of opinion (ashab al-ra'y).

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 30:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the Jews say, "Ezra is the son of Allah," and the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of Allah."﴾ Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A group of Jews came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): Sallam ibn Mishkam, al-Nu'man ibn Awfa, Shas ibn Qays, and Malik ibn al-Sayf. They said: "How can we follow you when you have abandoned our qibla, and you do not claim that Ezra is the son of Allah?" Then Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And the Jews say, "Ezra is the son of Allah."﴾ [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 14/202, and by Ibn Ishaq in his Sirah: 1/570. al-Suyuti also attributed it, along with the other narration, to Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, and Ibn Mardawayh. al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/170-171.]]

Asim, al-Kisa'i, and Ya'qub read "'Uzayrun" (ʿUzayrun) with tanwin, while the others read it without tanwin, because it is a non-Arabic name that resembles a diminutive form. Whoever reads it with tanwin says: because it is a light (triptote) noun, its proper treatment is to be declined, even though it is non-Arabic, like Nuh, Hud, and Lut. Abu 'Ubayda preferred the tanwin and said: because this is not an attribute of his father; rather, it is like your saying "Zayd ibn al-Amir" and "Zayd ibn Ukhtina." So ʿUzayr is the subject (mubtada'), and what follows it is its predicate (khabar).

ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr said: This statement was made only by one man among the Jews named Finhas ibn ʿAzurá' [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 14/201; Ibn al-Mundhir also narrated it from Ibn Jurayj. al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/171.]].

He is the one who said: "Indeed, Allah is poor and we are rich" (Al ʿImran 181).

ʿAtiyyah al-ʿAwfi narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Jews only said "Ezra is the son of Allah" because Ezra was among them, the Torah was with them, and the Ark (al-Tabut) was among them. They neglected the Torah and acted contrary to the truth, so Allah lifted the Ark from them and caused them to forget the Torah, erasing it from their hearts. Ezra supplicated Allah and humbly implored Him to return to him what had been erased from their hearts. While he was praying, humbly beseeching Allah, a light descended from the sky and entered his body, and the Torah returned to him. He then called out to his people, saying: "O people, Allah has given me the Torah back; He has returned it to me!" The people gathered around him, and he taught them. They remained as long as Allah willed. Then the Ark descended after its removal from them. When they saw the Ark, they compared what was in it with what Ezra had been teaching them, and they found it to be identical. They said: "Ezra was given this only because he is the son of Allah."  [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 14/202-203. See also al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/171.]]

al-Kalbi said: When Bukhtansar (Nebuchadnezzar) prevailed over the Children of Israel, he killed those among them who read the Torah. Ezra was then a young boy, so he regarded him as too young and did not kill him. When the Children of Israel returned to Bayt al-Maqdis, there was no one among them who could read the Torah. Allah sent Ezra to renew the Torah for them, and it was a sign for them after one hundred years. It is said: an angel came to him with a vessel containing water and gave him to drink, and the Torah was imprinted in his chest. When he came to them, he said, "I am Ezra," but they denied him and said: "If you are as you claim, then dictate the Torah to us." So he wrote it out for them. Then a man said: "My father told me from my grandfather that the Torah had been placed in a jar and buried in a vineyard." So they went with him until they dug it up, and they compared it with what Ezra had written for them, and they found that he had not omitted a single letter from it. They said: "Allah would not have cast the Torah into the heart of a man except that he is His son." At that point the Jews said: "Ezra is the son of Allah."

As for the Christians, they said: "The Messiah is the son of Allah." The cause of this was that they had been upon the religion of Islam for eighty-one years after 'Isa, peace be upon him, was raised, praying toward the qibla and fasting Ramadan, until war broke out between them and the Jews. There was among the Jews a brave man called "Bulus" (Paul), who killed a number of the companions of 'Isa, peace be upon him. Then he said to the Jews: "If the truth is with 'Isa, then we have disbelieved in him, and the Fire is our destination. We are cheated if they enter Paradise and we enter the Fire. I will scheme and lead them astray until they enter the Fire." He had a horse called al-ʿUqab, on which he used to fight; he hamstrung his horse, showed remorse, and put dust on his head. The Christians said to him: "Who are you?" He said: "Bulus, your enemy." Then a voice called out to him from the sky: "There is no repentance for you except that you become a Christian; and you have repented." So they brought him into the church, and he entered a room, not leaving it by night or by day for a year, until he learned the Gospel. Then he came out and said: "I was called out to, that Allah has accepted your repentance." They believed him and loved him. Then he went to Bayt al-Maqdis and appointed Nestor (Nastur) over them, and taught him that 'Isa, Maryam, and God were three. Then he set out for the Romans and taught them the divinity (lahut) and humanity (nasut). He said: "'Isa was neither a human nor a body, but he is the son of Allah." He taught this to a man called "Ya'qub." Then he summoned a man called Malik and said: "God has always been and will always be, and 'Isa is God." When he had gained influence over them, he summoned these three one by one and said to each of them: "You are my chosen one, and I have seen 'Isa in a dream, and he is pleased with me." He said to each of them: "Tomorrow I will sacrifice myself, so call the people to your creed." Then he entered the altar, sacrificed himself, and said: "I do this only to please 'Isa." When the third day came, each of them called the people to his creed, and a group of people followed each of them. They disagreed and fought one another. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿And the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of Allah."﴾ ﴿That is their saying with their mouths﴾, saying with their tongues without knowledge. The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: Allah, exalted is He, did not mention any statement attached to "mouths" and "tongues" except that it was falsehood.

﴿Yudahi'una﴾: Asim read it with a kasra on the ha' and with hamza; the others read it with a damma on the ha' without hamza. Both are dialectal forms, meaning the same: it is said "dahaytuhu" and "dahha'tuhu," with the same meaning. Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "they resemble." Al-mudahat means resemblance. Mujahid said: "they conform to." al-Hasan said: "they agree with." ﴿The saying of those who disbelieved before﴾: Qatadah and al-Suddi said: the Christians resembled the saying of the Jews before them, so they said: "The Messiah is the son of Allah," just as the Jews said: "Ezra is the son of Allah." Mujahid said: they resemble the saying of the polytheists who came before, who used to say: "al-Lat, al-ʿUzza, and Manat are the daughters of Allah." al-Hasan said: He likened their disbelief to the disbelief of the disbelieving nations that passed away, as He said concerning the polytheists of the Arabs: "Thus said those before them, the like of their saying; their hearts have become alike" (al-Baqarah 118). al-Qutaybi said: He means that whoever was in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) from among the Jews and Christians was saying what the first of them had said. ﴿Allah destroy them﴾: Ibn ʿAbbas said: "May Allah curse them." Ibn Jurayj said: that is, "May Allah kill them." It was also said: it is not meant literally as fighting, but is an expression of wonder. ﴿How are they deluded?﴾: that is, they are turned away from the truth after the evidences for it have been established.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 31:

﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords﴾, meaning: their scholars and their reciters. The aḥbār (sing. ḥibr, pronounced with either a kasra or a fatḥa on the ḥāʾ; meaning "scholars") are the scholars, and the ruhbān among the Christians are the people of the monasteries (ṣawāmiʿ). If it is asked: "They did not worship the rabbis and the monks?" We say: the meaning is that they obeyed them in disobedience to Allah, and they declared lawful what they declared lawful and unlawful what they declared unlawful, so they took them as lords. It is narrated from ʿAdiyy ibn Ḥātim (raḍiyallāhu ʿanhu) that he said: I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while there was a golden cross around my neck, and he said to me: "O ʿAdiyy, throw this idol away from your neck," so I threw it away. Then I reached him while he was reciting: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah﴾, until he finished it. I said to him: "We do not worship them." He said: "Do they not make unlawful what Allah has made lawful, so you make it unlawful, and make lawful what Allah has made unlawful, so you make it lawful?" He said: I said: "Yes." He said: "That is their worship." [[Narrated by al-Ṭabarī in al-Tafsīr: 14/210. Al-Tirmidhī narrated it in abridged form in the Tafsīr of Sūrat Barāʾa: 8/492-494, and said: "This is a strange ḥadīth which we do not know except through the narration of ʿAbd al-Salām ibn Ḥarb, and Ghaṭīf ibn Aʿyan is not well known in ḥadīth." al-Suyūṭī also attributed it to Ibn Saʿd, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, al-Ṭabarānī, Abū al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqī. See: al-Durr al-Manthūr: 4/174; al-Kāfī al-Shāfī p. (75); Jāmiʿ Bayān al-ʿIlm wa-Faḍlihi by Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr p. (437).]].

ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak said:
"And has anything corrupted the religion except the kings... and the evil rabbis and their monks?"

﴿And the Messiah, son of Mary﴾, meaning: they took him as a god. ﴿Yet they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no god but Him; glory be to Him above what they associate.﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 9, verses 32–33:**

﴿They desire to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths﴾, that is, they desire to nullify the religion of Allah with their tongues and their denial of it. Al-Kalbi said: "The light is the Qur'an." That is, they desire to reject the Qur'an with their tongues through denial. ﴿But Allah refuses except to perfect His light﴾, that is, He will make His religion prevail, make His word manifest, and complete the truth with which He sent Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿Though the disbelievers dislike it.﴾

﴿It is He who sent His Messenger﴾, meaning: He who refuses except to complete His religion is the one who sent His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿with guidance﴾. It was said: with the Qur'an. And it was said: with the explanation of the obligatory duties. ﴿And the religion of truth﴾, which is Islam, ﴿that He may make it prevail﴾, that is, make it high and grant it victory, ﴿over all religion﴾, over all the other religions, ﴿though the polytheists dislike it.﴾

The commentators differed concerning the meaning of this verse. Ibn Abbas said: the pronoun refers to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that is, that He might teach him all the laws of the religion, so that he would make it prevail over them, until nothing of them is hidden from him.

Others said: the pronoun refers to the religion of truth, and its prevailing over the religions means that Allah the Exalted is not worshipped except through it. Abu Hurayrah and al-Dahhak said: this will be at the descent of Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him); no people of any religion will remain except that they enter Islam.

We have also related from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning the descent of Isa (peace be upon him), that he said: "In his time all religions will perish except Islam." [[A fragment of a hadith of Abu Hurayrah, related by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 2/437. The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said: Ahmad and Abu Dawud narrated it with a sound isnad (chain of narration) through the route of Abd al-Rahman ibn Adam from Abu Hurayrah, traced to the Prophet (marfu', i.e., attributed directly to the Prophet).]] And al-Miqdad narrated: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "No dwelling of clay or of hair will remain on the face of the earth except that Allah will cause the word of Islam to enter it, either with the honor of one who is honored or the humiliation of one who is humiliated. Either Allah will honor them and make them of its people, so it (Islam) will be honored through them, or He will humiliate them and they will submit to it." [[Related by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 6/4. Al-Haythami mentioned it from the narration of al-Miqdad and Tamim al-Dari and said: Ahmad and al-Tabarani narrated it, and the men of al-Tabarani's chain are the men of the sahih (authentic collections). Majma' al-Zawa'id: 6/14. Furthermore, in manuscript "a" the narration reads: "He honors the honored and humiliates the humiliated."]]

Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Habib informed us, Abu Ja'far Muhammad Sulayman ibn Mansur narrated to us, Abu Muslim ibn Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah al-Kajji narrated to us, Abu Asim al-Nabil narrated to us, Abd al-Hamid, that is, Ibn Ja'far, narrated to us, from al-Aswad ibn al-Ala, from Abu Salama, from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Night and day will not pass until al-Lat and al-Uzza are worshipped." She said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I did not think that would be after Allah the Exalted revealed to you: 'It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, though the polytheists dislike it.'" Then he said: "That will be what Allah wills. Then Allah the Exalted will send a pleasant wind, which will take the soul of everyone who has in his heart an atom's weight of good. Then there will remain only those in whom there is no good, and people will return to the religion of their fathers." [[Related by Muslim in al-Fitan, chapter "The Hour will not come until the tribe of Daws worships Dhu al-Khalasa," no. (2907): 4/2230; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/91–92.]]

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: The meaning of the verse is: that He may make it prevail over all religion through clear proofs.

It was also said: that He may make it prevail over the religions that surround the Prophet (ﷺ), so that He overcomes them.

Al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Allah has indeed made His Messenger (ﷺ) prevail over all religions by making clear to everyone who heard him that it is the truth, and that whatever opposes it among the religions is falsehood. He also said: And he prevailed over them in that the totality of polytheism consists of two religions: the religion of the People of the Book and the religion of the unlettered (Arab pagans). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) subdued the unlettered until they submitted to Islam, willingly and unwillingly, and he killed the People of the Book and took captives, until some of them submitted to Islam, and some of them he gave the jizya (poll tax) while in a state of humiliation, and his rule was applied to them. This is his prevailing over all religion. And Allah knows best.

﴿They desire to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths﴾, that is, they desire to nullify the religion of Allah with their tongues and their denial of it. Al-Kalbi said: "The light is the Qur'an." That is, they desire to reject the Qur'an with their tongues through denial. ﴿But Allah refuses except to perfect His light﴾, that is, He will make His religion prevail, make His word manifest, and complete the truth with which He sent Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿Though the disbelievers dislike it.﴾

﴿It is He who sent His Messenger﴾, meaning: He who refuses except to complete His religion is the one who sent His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿with guidance﴾. It was said: with the Qur'an. Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Habib informed us, Abu Ja'far Muhammad Sulayman ibn Mansur narrated to us, Abu Muslim ibn Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah al-Kajji narrated to us, Abu Asim al-Nabil narrated to us, Abd al-Hamid, that is, Ibn Ja'far, narrated to us, from al-Aswad ibn al-Ala, from Abu Salama, from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Night and day will not pass until al-Lat and al-Uzza are worshipped." She said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I did not think that would be after Allah the Exalted revealed to you: 'It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion, though the polytheists dislike it.'" Then he said: "That will be what Allah wills. Then Allah the Exalted will send a pleasant wind, which will take the soul of everyone who has in his heart an atom's weight of good. Then there will remain only those in whom there is no good, and people will return to the religion of their fathers." [[Related by Muslim in al-Fitan, chapter "The Hour will not come until the tribe of Daws worships Dhu al-Khalasa," no. (2907): 4/2230; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/91–92.]]

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: The meaning of the verse is: that He may make it prevail over all religion through clear proofs.

It was also said: that He may make it prevail over the religions that surround the Prophet (ﷺ), so that He overcomes them.

Al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Allah has indeed made His Messenger (ﷺ) prevail over all religions by making clear to everyone who heard him that it is the truth, and that whatever opposes it among the religions is falsehood. He also said: And he prevailed over them in that the totality of polytheism consists of two religions: the religion of the People of the Book and the religion of the unlettered (Arab pagans). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) subdued the unlettered until they submitted to Islam, willingly and unwillingly, and he killed the People of the Book and took captives, until some of them submitted to Islam, and some of them he gave the jizya (poll tax) while in a state of humiliation, and his rule was applied to them. This is his prevailing over all religion. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 34:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed many of the rabbis (al-ahbar) and the monks (al-ruhban)﴾ means the scholars and the reciters from among the People of the Book, ﴿consume the wealth of people unjustly﴾ [he means: they take] [[In "A": (they intend: they take).]] bribes in their judgments, and they distort the Book of Allah, and they write with their own hands books, saying, "This is from Allah," and they take for it a small price from their inferiors. These are the gains they obtain from them in exchange for altering the description of the Prophet ﷺ, fearing that if they affirmed him, those gains would be lost to them. ﴿And they hinder﴾ they turn and divert people ﴿from the way of Allah﴾, the religion of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿And those who hoard gold and silver and do not spend it in the way of Allah - give them tidings of a painful punishment.﴾ Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Every wealth whose zakat is paid is not a hoard, even if it is buried; and every wealth whose zakat is not paid is a hoard, even if it is not buried. The same is related from Ibn Abbas.

Isma'il ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us, Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us, Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi informed us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us, Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj informed us, Suwayd ibn Sa'id informed me, Hafs ibn Maysara informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, that Abu Salih ibn Dhakwan informed him that he heard Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no owner of gold or silver who does not pay its due, except that on the Day of Resurrection plates of fire will be made for him, and they will be heated in the fire of Hell, and his side, his forehead and his back will be branded with them. Whenever they cool, they will be returned to him, in a day whose length is fifty thousand years, until Allah judges between the servants, and he sees his path, either to Paradise or to the Fire. And there is no owner of camels who does not pay its due, and among its due is milking them on the day of watering, except that on the Day of Resurrection they will be laid out for him on a level plain, most abundant as they were, not one of them missing, trampling him with their hooves and biting him with their mouths. Whenever the first of them passes over him, the last of them is returned to him, in a day whose length is fifty thousand years, until He judges between the servants, and he sees his path, either to Paradise or to the Fire. And there is no owner of cattle or sheep who does not pay its due, except that on the Day of Resurrection they will be laid out for him on a level plain, not one of them missing, none of them hornless, broken-horned or maimed, goring him with their horns and trampling him with their hooves. Whenever the first of them passes over him, the last of them is returned to him, in a day whose length is fifty thousand years, until Allah judges between the servants, and he sees his path, either to Paradise or to the Fire." [[Related by Muslim in Zakat, chapter on the sin of one who withholds zakat, no. (987): 2/680-681, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/480.]]

And we have related from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever Allah gives wealth but does not pay its zakat, his wealth will be represented to him on the Day of Resurrection as a bald venomous serpent with two black spots, which will encircle him on the Day of Resurrection, seize him by his two jaws, meaning his cheeks, and then say: 'I am your wealth, I am your hoard.'" Then he recited: ﴿And let not those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty think it is better for them﴾ to the end of the verse. [[Related by al-Bukhari in Zakat, chapter on the sin of one who withholds zakat: 3/268, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/478.]]

It is also reported from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: Every wealth exceeding four thousand dirhams is a hoard, whether or not zakat has been paid from it, and what is less than that is expenditure. [[Related by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 14/219-220.]]

It has been said: What exceeds need is a hoard. Isma'il ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us, Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us, Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi informed us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us, Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj informed us, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah informed us, Waki' informed us, al-A'mash informed us, from al-Ma'rur ibn Suwayd, from Abu Dharr, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was sitting in the shade of the Ka'bah. When he saw me he said: "They are the greatest losers, by the Lord of the Ka'bah." He said: I came and sat down, but I could not remain still, so I stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be ransomed for you, who are they?" He said: "They are those with the most wealth, except for those who say: 'Like this and like this and like this,' from before him, behind him, to his right and to his left. And few are they." [[Related by al-Bukhari in Oaths, chapter on how the oath of the Prophet ﷺ was: 11/524, and Muslim in Zakat, chapter on the severity of the punishment for one who does not pay zakat, no. (990): 2/686.]]

It is also reported from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, that he used to say: Whoever leaves behind a white or red (wealth), he will be branded with it on the Day of Resurrection. [[Related by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 5/168, and al-Tabari: 14/220. Ibn Hajar also attributed it to al-Bukhari in al-Tarikh, and to Ibn Mardawayh through the route of Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Wahid al-Thaqafi from Abu al-Najib al-Shami from Abu Dharr, and from Thawban Ibn Mardawayh and al-Tabarani in Musnad al-Shamiyyin related it with different wording. See: al-Kafi al-Shaf pp. (75-76).]]

It is related from Abu Umamah who said: A man from the People of the Bench (ahl al-Suffah) died, and a dinar was found in his loincloth. The Prophet ﷺ said: "A brand." Then another died, and two dinars were found in his loincloth, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "Two brands." [[Related by Imam Ahmad: 1/101. Ibn Hajar said: Ahmad, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Ya'la, al-Tabarani and al-Tabari related it through the route of Shahr ibn Hawshab. Ibn Hibban related the second part from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud. See: al-Kafi al-Shaf p. (76).]]

The first opinion is more sound, because the verse concerns withholding zakat, not gathering lawful wealth. The Prophet ﷺ said: "How excellent is righteous wealth for a righteous man." [[Related by Imam Ahmad: 4/197, 202, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/91.]]

Mujahid related from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: When this verse was revealed, it weighed heavily on the Muslims, and they said: "None of us can leave anything for his child." So Umar mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah, and he said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not prescribe zakat except to purify with it what remains of your wealth." [[Related by Abu Dawud in Zakat, chapter on the rights of wealth: 2/250; al-Hakim authenticated it: 2/333; al-Bayhaqi: 4/83; and the author mentioned it in al-Masabih: 2/10. al-Haythami mentioned it in al-Majma': 7/30 and said: Abu Ya'la related it, and in its chain is Uthman ibn Umayr, who is weak. See also: al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/178.]]

Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, was asked about this verse, and he said: That was before zakat was revealed. When it was revealed, Allah made it a purification for wealth.

Ibn Umar also said: I would not mind if I had gold equal to Uhud, whose count I know, that I would pay its zakat and act in obedience to Allah.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿and do not spend it in the way of Allah﴾, He did not say "and do not spend them" (in dual form), though He mentioned gold and silver together. It has been said: He intended the hoards and the gold and silver themselves. It has also been said: The pronoun was returned to silver because it is the more general, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed it is difficult﴾ [al-Baqarah: 45], where the pronoun is returned to prayer because it is the more general; and as He said: ﴿And when they see a trade or amusement, they scatter toward it﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 11], where the pronoun is returned to trade because it is the more general. ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾, i.e., warn them.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 35:

﴿On the Day it will be heated up in the fire of Hellfire﴾, i.e., the fire will be made to enter upon them and it will be kindled over them, i.e., over the treasures, ﴿and their foreheads, their sides and their backs will be branded with it﴾, i.e., they will be burned with it, ﴿their foreheads﴾, i.e., the foreheads of those who hoarded them, ﴿and their sides and their backs﴾. It is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Not a dinar will be placed upon a dinar, nor a dirham upon a dirham, but his skin will be widened so that every dinar and dirham is placed in a separate place."

Abu Bakr al-Warraq was asked: "Why did He single out the foreheads, the sides and the backs for branding?" He said: "Because the wealthy owner of the hoard, when he sees the poor man, contracts his face, knits what is between his eyebrows, turns his back to him, and turns away from him with his side."

His Exalted saying: ﴿This is what you hoarded﴾, i.e., it will be said to them: "This is what you hoarded, ﴿for yourselves. So taste what you used to hoard﴾", i.e., you used to withhold the rights of Allah Exalted in your wealth. Some of the Companions said: this verse concerns the People of the Book. Most of them said: it is general, concerning both the People of the Book and the Muslims, and Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) said likewise.

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 36–37:

The words of God Most High: ﴿Indeed, the number of months﴾, meaning the number of months, ﴿with God is twelve months in the Book of God﴾. They are Muharram, Safar, Rabi' al-Awwal, Rabi' al-Thani, Jumada al-Ula, Jumada al-Akhirah, Rajab, Sha'ban, Ramadan, Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa'dah and Dhu al-Hijjah. His words ﴿in the Book of God﴾ mean in the judgement of God. It is also said: in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). Abu Ja'far recited "ithna 'ashara", "tis'ata 'ashara" and "ahada 'ashara" with the shin silent (sukun), while the common readers (al-'Amma) recited them with a fatha on the shin.

﴿The day He created the heavens and the earth﴾. What is meant by this is the lunar months (al-shuhur al-hilaliyyah), which are the months by which the Muslims reckon their fasting, their pilgrimage, their festivals and all their affairs. By the solar months the year is three hundred and sixty-five days and a quarter of a day, whereas the lunar year falls short of three hundred and sixty days by the shortfall of the crescents. Usually it amounts to three hundred and fifty-four days.

﴿Of them, four are sacred﴾. Among the months, four are sacred (hurum), and they are: Rajab, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and Muharram; one is single and three are consecutive. ﴿That is the upright religion﴾, that is, the straight reckoning.

﴿So do not wrong yourselves therein﴾. It has been said: his words "therein" refer to all the months of the year, meaning: do not wrong yourselves therein by committing sins and abandoning obedience. It has also been said: "therein" means in the sacred months. Qatadah said: righteous deeds are greater in reward in the sacred months, and wrongdoing in them is greater than wrongdoing in other months, although wrongdoing is grave in every circumstance. Ibn Abbas said: ﴿do not wrong yourselves therein﴾ means making lawful what is forbidden and raiding in them. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: do not make their lawful things unlawful, nor their unlawful things lawful, as the polytheists did, and this is the nasi' (intercalation, the postponement of the sacred months).

﴿And fight the polytheists all together﴾, all of them, in general, ﴿as they fight you all together. And know that God is with the God-fearing﴾. The scholars differed concerning the prohibition of fighting in the sacred months. One group said: it was a great prohibition, then it was abrogated (naskh, the cancellation of a ruling by a later revelation) by His words: ﴿And fight the polytheists all together﴾, as if He were saying: [fight] in them and in other than them. This is the view of Qatadah, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, al-Zuhri and Sufyan al-Thawri. They said: the Prophet (ﷺ) fought Hawazin at Hunayn and Thaqif at Ta'if, and he besieged them in Shawwal and part of Dhu al-Qa'dah. Others said: it has not been abrogated. Ibn Jurayj said: 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah swore by God: it is not lawful for people to raid in the sanctuary or in the sacred months, except if they are attacked in them; and it has not been abrogated.

The words of God Most High: ﴿The nasi' is only an increase in disbelief﴾. It has been said that it is a verbal noun (masdar) like "sa'ir" and "harib", and it has also been said that it is a passive participle (maf'ul) like "jarih" and "qatil". It derives from postponement (al-ta'khir), and from it comes "nasi'ah" in sale (deferred payment). It is said: God "ansa'a" in his term, meaning He postponed it. According to most readers it is written with a hamzah and is lengthened (mamdud). Warsh, from Nafi', through the route of al-Bukhari, recited it with a doubled ya' without a hamzah, and it has been said that its original form has a hamzah which was lightened.

It has also been said that it derives from forgetting (al-nisyan) in the sense of "the forgotten", that is, "the abandoned". The meaning of nasi' is postponing the prohibition of one month to another month. The Arabs used to hold the sacred months in high regard, and this was among the things they had retained from the religion of Abraham, peace be upon him. Their livelihood was mostly from hunting and raiding, so it was hard for them to refrain from that for three consecutive months. Sometimes they would have a war in one of the sacred months, and they disliked postponing their war, so they performed nasi', that is, they postponed the prohibition of that month to another month. They used to postpone the prohibition of Muharram to Safar, so they would forbid Safar and make Muharram lawful. When they needed to postpone the prohibition of Safar, they postponed it to Rabi', and so on, month after month, until the prohibition went round the entire year. Then Islam came, and Muharram had returned to its proper place which God, Mighty and Majestic, had set for it, and that was after a long period. So the Prophet (ﷺ) gave a sermon during his pilgrimage.

As: Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Firabri informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Salam narrated to us, Abd al-Wahid narrated to us, Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Bakrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed time has come around to its original form, the day God created the heavens and the earth. The year is twelve months, of which four are sacred: three in succession, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and Muharram, and Rajab of Mudar, which lies between Jumada and Sha'ban." He said: "Which month is this?" We said: "God and His Messenger know best." He was silent until we thought he would name it by another name. Then he said: "Is it not Dhu al-Hijjah?" We said: "Yes." He said: "Which land is this?" We said: "God and His Messenger know best." He was silent until we thought he would name it by another name. Then he said: "Is it not the sacred land?" We said: "Yes." He said: "Which day is this?" We said: "God and His Messenger know best." He was silent until we thought he would name it by another name. He said: "Is it not the day of sacrifice?" We said: "Yes." He said: "Indeed your blood and your property," Muhammad said: "I think he said: and your honour, are forbidden to you, as the sanctity of this day of yours, in this land of yours, in this month of yours. You will meet your Lord, and He will ask you about your deeds. Beware, do not turn back after me as misguided people, striking one another's necks. Let the one present convey it to the one absent, for perhaps some who are told will understand it better than some who have heard it. Have I conveyed it? Have I conveyed it?" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Adahi (The Sacrifices), chapter on whoever said: "the Adha is the day of sacrifice": 10/7–8; and Muslim in al-Qiyamah (The Resurrection), chapter on the severity of the prohibition of blood and honour, no. (1679): 3/1305; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/215–216.]]

They said: the nasi' had continued among them, so that sometimes they would perform the pilgrimage in one year in one month, and in the following year they would perform it in another month. [157/b]

Mujahid said: they used to perform the pilgrimage in every month for two years. They performed the pilgrimage in Dhu al-Hijjah for two years, then they performed it in Muharram for two years, then in Safar for two years, and likewise for the other months. The pilgrimage of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, before the Farewell Pilgrimage, coincided with the second year, in Dhu al-Qa'dah. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) performed the Farewell Pilgrimage in the following year, and his pilgrimage coincided with the prescribed month of pilgrimage, which is Dhu al-Hijjah. He stood at 'Arafah on the ninth day, and he gave the sermon on the tenth day at Mina. He informed them that the months of nasi' had been shifted by the rotation of time, and the matter had returned to what God had established as the reckoning of the months on the day God created the heavens and the earth. He commanded them to preserve it so that it would not be changed in the days to come.

They differed about who first performed the nasi'. Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, Qatadah and Mujahid said: the first to perform the nasi' were the Banu Malik ibn Kinanah, and they were three: Abu Thumamah Junadah ibn 'Awf ibn Umayyah al-Kinani. Al-Kalbi said: the first to do that was a man from the Banu Kinanah called Nu'aym ibn Tha'labah, who used to be the commander over the people at the season (of pilgrimage). When the people were about to depart, he would stand and address the people, saying: "There is no rejection of what I have decided. I am the one who is not blamed and not refused." The polytheists would say to him: "At your service." Then they would ask him to postpone for them a month in which they could raid. He would say: "Indeed Safar this year is sacred." When he said that, they would unstring their bows and remove their spearheads and arrowheads. If he said it was lawful, they would string their bows, fasten their arrowheads and raid. After Nu'aym ibn Tha'labah there was a man called Junadah ibn 'Awf, and he is the one whom the Prophet (ﷺ) witnessed.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: he was a man from the Banu Kinanah called al-Qalammas. Their poet said: "Among us is the postponer of the month, al-Qalammas." They used to do that only in Dhu al-Hijjah, when the Arabs gathered for the season.

Juwaybir said, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: the first to institute the nasi' was Amr ibn Luhayy ibn Qam'ah ibn Khindif.

Isma'il ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us, Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us, Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi informed us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan narrated to us, Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me, Jarir narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I saw Amr ibn Luhayy ibn Qam'ah ibn Khindif, the father of the Banu Ka'b, dragging his intestines in the Fire." [[Previously cited in the commentary on surah al-Ma'idah 3/108. There is nothing in the hadith that indicates that Amr ibn Luhayy was the first to institute the nasi'.]]

This, which we have mentioned, is the nasi' that God Most High mentioned when He said: ﴿The nasi' is only an increase in disbelief﴾, meaning an increase of disbelief upon their disbelief. ﴿By it those who disbelieve are led astray﴾. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs read ﴿yudallu﴾ with a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the dad, as in His words: ﴿The evil of their deeds has been made attractive to them﴾. Ya'qub read it with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the dad, and this is the reading of al-Hasan and Mujahid, with the meaning "yudillu" (they lead astray): by it those who disbelieve lead the people astray. The others read it with a fatha on the ya' and a kasra on the dad, because they themselves are the ones who go astray, according to His words: ﴿They make it lawful one year and make it unlawful another year, to conform to the number of what God has made unlawful﴾, meaning the nasi'. "Liyuwatiu" means "liyuwafiqu" (to agree), and "mu'awatah" means "muwafaqah" (agreement). The meaning of ﴿the number of what God has made unlawful﴾ is that they did not make lawful a sacred month without making in its place a lawful month unlawful, and they did not make unlawful a lawful month without making lawful in its place a sacred month, so that the sacred months would not exceed four, as God had prescribed, so that the number would agree. ﴿So they make lawful what God has made unlawful. The evil of their deeds has been made attractive to them.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: Satan made it attractive to them. ﴿And God does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾
