It derives from postponement (al-ta'khir), and from it comes "nasi'ah" in sale (deferred payment). It is said: God "ansa'a" in his term, meaning He postponed it. According to most readers it is written with a hamzah and is lengthened (mamdud). Warsh, from Nafi', through the route of al-Bukhari, recited it with a doubled ya' without a hamzah, and it has been said that its original form has a hamzah which was lightened.

It has also been said that it derives from forgetting (al-nisyan) in the sense of "the forgotten", that is, "the abandoned". The meaning of nasi' is postponing the prohibition of one month to another month. The Arabs used to hold the sacred months in high regard, and this was among the things they had retained from the religion of Abraham, peace be upon him. Their livelihood was mostly from hunting and raiding, so it was hard for them to refrain from that for three consecutive months. Sometimes they would have a war in one of the sacred months, and they disliked postponing their war, so they performed nasi', that is, they postponed the prohibition of that month to another month. They used to postpone the prohibition of Muharram to Safar, so they would forbid Safar and make Muharram lawful. When they needed to postpone the prohibition of Safar, they postponed it to Rabi', and so on, month after month, until the prohibition went round the entire year. Then Islam came, and Muharram had returned to its proper place which God, Mighty and Majestic, had set for it, and that was after a long period. So the Prophet (ﷺ) gave a sermon during his pilgrimage.

As: Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Firabri informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Bukhari narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Salam narrated to us, Abd al-Wahid narrated to us, Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Bakrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed time has come around to its original form, the day God created the heavens and the earth. The year is twelve months, of which four are sacred: three in succession, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah and Muharram, and Rajab of Mudar, which lies between Jumada and Sha'ban." He said: "Which month is this?" We said: "God and His Messenger know best." He was silent until we thought he would name it by another name. Then he said: "Is it not Dhu al-Hijjah?" We said: "Yes." He said: "Which land is this?" We said: "God and His Messenger know best." He was silent until we thought he would name it by another name. Then he said: "Is it not the sacred land?" We said: "Yes." He said: "Which day is this?" We said: "God and His Messenger know best." He was silent until we thought he would name it by another name. He said: "Is it not the day of sacrifice?" We said: "Yes." He said: "Indeed your blood and your property," Muhammad said: "I think he said: and your honour, are forbidden to you, as the sanctity of this day of yours, in this land of yours, in this month of yours. You will meet your Lord, and He will ask you about your deeds. Beware, do not turn back after me as misguided people, striking one another's necks. Let the one present convey it to the one absent, for perhaps some who are told will understand it better than some who have heard it. Have I conveyed it? Have I conveyed it?" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Adahi (The Sacrifices), chapter on whoever said: "the Adha is the day of sacrifice": 10/7–8; and Muslim in al-Qiyamah (The Resurrection), chapter on the severity of the prohibition of blood and honour, no. (1679): 3/1305; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/215–216.]]

They said: the nasi' had continued among them, so that sometimes they would perform the pilgrimage in one year in one month, and in the following year they would perform it in another month. [157/b]

Mujahid said: they used to perform the pilgrimage in every month for two years. They performed the pilgrimage in Dhu al-Hijjah for two years, then they performed it in Muharram for two years, then in Safar for two years, and likewise for the other months. The pilgrimage of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, before the Farewell Pilgrimage, coincided with the second year, in Dhu al-Qa'dah. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) performed the Farewell Pilgrimage in the following year, and his pilgrimage coincided with the prescribed month of pilgrimage, which is Dhu al-Hijjah. He stood at 'Arafah on the ninth day, and he gave the sermon on the tenth day at Mina. He informed them that the months of nasi' had been shifted by the rotation of time, and the matter had returned to what God had established as the reckoning of the months on the day God created the heavens and the earth. He commanded them to preserve it so that it would not be changed in the days to come.

They differed about who first performed the nasi'. Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, Qatadah and Mujahid said: the first to perform the nasi' were the Banu Malik ibn Kinanah, and they were three: Abu Thumamah Junadah ibn 'Awf ibn Umayyah al-Kinani. Al-Kalbi said: the first to do that was a man from the Banu Kinanah called Nu'aym ibn Tha'labah, who used to be the commander over the people at the season (of pilgrimage). When the people were about to depart, he would stand and address the people, saying: "There is no rejection of what I have decided. I am the one who is not blamed and not refused." The polytheists would say to him: "At your service." Then they would ask him to postpone for them a month in which they could raid. He would say: "Indeed Safar this year is sacred." When he said that, they would unstring their bows and remove their spearheads and arrowheads. If he said it was lawful, they would string their bows, fasten their arrowheads and raid. After Nu'aym ibn Tha'labah there was a man called Junadah ibn 'Awf, and he is the one whom the Prophet (ﷺ) witnessed.

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: he was a man from the Banu Kinanah called al-Qalammas. Their poet said: "Among us is the postponer of the month, al-Qalammas." They used to do that only in Dhu al-Hijjah, when the Arabs gathered for the season.

Juwaybir said, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: the first to institute the nasi' was Amr ibn Luhayy ibn Qam'ah ibn Khindif.

Isma'il ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us, Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us, Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi informed us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan narrated to us, Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me, Jarir narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I saw Amr ibn Luhayy ibn Qam'ah ibn Khindif, the father of the Banu Ka'b, dragging his intestines in the Fire." [[Previously cited in the commentary on surah al-Ma'idah 3/108. There is nothing in the hadith that indicates that Amr ibn Luhayy was the first to institute the nasi'.]]

This, which we have mentioned, is the nasi' that God Most High mentioned when He said: ﴿The nasi' is only an increase in disbelief﴾, meaning an increase of disbelief upon their disbelief. ﴿By it those who disbelieve are led astray﴾. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs read ﴿yudallu﴾ with a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the dad, as in His words: ﴿The evil of their deeds has been made attractive to them﴾. Ya'qub read it with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the dad, and this is the reading of al-Hasan and Mujahid, with the meaning "yudillu" (they lead astray): by it those who disbelieve lead the people astray. The others read it with a fatha on the ya' and a kasra on the dad, because they themselves are the ones who go astray, according to His words: ﴿They make it lawful one year and make it unlawful another year, to conform to the number of what God has made unlawful﴾, meaning the nasi'. "Liyuwatiu" means "liyuwafiqu" (to agree), and "mu'awatah" means "muwafaqah" (agreement). The meaning of ﴿the number of what God has made unlawful﴾ is that they did not make lawful a sacred month without making in its place a lawful month unlawful, and they did not make unlawful a lawful month without making lawful in its place a sacred month, so that the sacred months would not exceed four, as God had prescribed, so that the number would agree. ﴿So they make lawful what God has made unlawful. The evil of their deeds has been made attractive to them.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: Satan made it attractive to them. ﴿And God does not guide the disbelieving people.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 38–39:

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿O you who have believed, what is [wrong] with you that when you are told, "Go forth in the way of Allah," you adhere heavily to the earth?﴾ — the verse [in full]. It was revealed concerning the urging to the expedition of Tabuk. That was because the Prophet ﷺ, when he returned from al-Ta'if, was commanded to fight in the expedition against the Romans. And that was at a time of hardship for the people and intense heat, when the fruits had ripened and the shade was pleasant. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not intend an expedition except that he concealed it by [mentioning] something else, until that expedition came. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ undertook it in intense heat, facing a long journey, vast deserts, and a great enemy. So he made their situation clear to the Muslims so that they might prepare the equipment of their enemy. But going out was hard for them, and they were reluctant. So Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, what is [wrong] with you that when you are told﴾ [[See al-Tabari: 14/253; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi p. 283; al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/190.]] — that is, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to you: ﴿Go forth﴾, that is, set out, ﴿in the way of Allah﴾ ﴿you adhere heavily to the earth﴾, that is, you clung to your land and your dwellings. ﴿Are you satisfied with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter?﴾ — that is, with the ease and comfort of this world rather than the bounties of the Hereafter.

﴿But the enjoyment of worldly life, in comparison with the Hereafter, is but little.﴾

Then He threatened them for abandoning jihad, saying, exalted is He: ﴿If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment﴾ in the Hereafter. It was also said: it is the withholding of rain from them in this world. Najdah ibn Nufay'(Najda ibn Nufai') asked Ibn 'Abbas about this verse, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ called upon a tribe of the tribes of the Arabs to go forth, and they were reluctant towards him, so the rain was withheld from them, and that was their punishment [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 14/254-255; al-Hakim authenticated it in al-Mustadrak: 2/118; Abu Dawud narrated it in abridged form in al-Sunan: 3/367; and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 9/48. See also al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/193-194.]] ﴿and He will replace you with a different people﴾ better than you and more obedient. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: they are the sons of Persia. It was also said: they are the people of Yemen. ﴿And you will not harm Him at all﴾ by your abandoning the going forth.

﴿And Allah is over all things competent.﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 40 (part 1 of 2)**

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Unless you help him, Allah has already helped him.﴾ This is an announcement from Allah, mighty and majestic, that He Himself undertakes to support His Messenger and to make His religion victorious, whether or not people help him. He had already given him victory when his supporters were few and his enemies many, so how much more so today, when he has a multitude of numbers and equipment? ﴿When those who disbelieved expelled him﴾ from Makkah, when they schemed against him, intended to confine him, and resolved to kill him. ﴿The second of two﴾ means he was one of the two. The two were: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanh). ﴿When they were in the cave﴾, which is a hollow in Mount Thawr in Makkah. ﴿When he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us."﴾ Al-Sha'bi said: In this verse Allah rebuked all the people of the earth, except Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanh).

Abu al-Muzaffar Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Tamimi informed us: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿUthman informed us: Khaythama ibn Sulayman informed us: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Dawraqi related to us: Saʿid ibn Sulayman related to us, from ʿAli ibn Hashim, from Kathir al-Nawwa', from Jumay' ibn ʿUmayr, who said: I came to Ibn ʿUmar (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhumā) and heard him say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu Bakr (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanh): "You are my companion in the cave, and my companion at the Basin (al-Ḥawḍ)." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Manaqib, chapter on the good tidings to Abu Bakr and ʿUmar: 10/154, and he said: This is a hasan gharib ṣaḥīḥ hadith. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/82, where he said: This is a hasan gharib hadith. In its chain is Kathir ibn Isma'il or Ibn Nafi' al-Nawwa', who is weak (ḍaʿīf), of the sixth tier (according to al-Taqrib).]]

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: Whoever says that Abu Bakr was not the companion of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is a disbeliever, because he denies the explicit text (naṣṣ) of the Qur'an. As for the rest of the Companions, if one denies it, he is an innovator (mubtadiʿ), not a disbeliever.

As for His saying, mighty and majestic: ﴿Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us﴾, Abu Bakr's grief was not out of cowardice; rather it was out of concern for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: "If I am killed, I am only one man; but if you are killed, the Ummah will be destroyed." It is related that when he set out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) toward the cave, he would walk for a while in front of him and for a while behind him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "What is the matter with you, O Abu Bakr?" He said: "I remember the pursuit, so I walk behind you; then I remember the ambush, so I walk in front of you." When they reached the cave, he said: "Stay where you are, O Messenger of Allah, until I search the cave." He entered and searched it, then said: "Come down, O Messenger of Allah." He came down, and ʿUmar said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, that night was better than the family of ʿUmar." [[Attributed by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (4/197-198) to al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il, and to Ibn ʿAsakir from Ḍabba ibn Miḥṣan. Ibn Kathir said in al-Bidaya wal-Nihaya (3/180): "There is strangeness and nakārah in this context." Ibn Ishaq related it in abridged form: 1/486. Ibn Kathir said about this report: "It has interruption (inqiṭāʿ) at both its ends." He related it in full from the narration of Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi and said: "This is mursal, and we have mentioned supporting evidence for it."]]

Abu al-Muzaffar al-Tamimi informed us: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿUthman, known as Ibn Abi al-Nazar, informed us: Khaythama ibn Sulayman informed us: Abu Qilaba al-Raqqashi related to us: Hayyan ibn Hilal related to us: Hammam ibn Yahya related to us: Thabit al-Bunani related to us: Anas ibn Malik related to us that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanh) told them, saying: "I looked at the feet of the polytheists above our heads while we were in the cave, and I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if one of them looked under his feet, he would see us.' He said: 'O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two whose third is Allah?'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the virtues of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), chapter on the merits of the Muhajirun: 7/8-9; by Muslim in the virtues of the Companions, chapter on the merits of Abu Bakr (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanh), no. (2381): 4/1854; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/365.]]

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi related to us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us: al-Layth related to us, from ʿUqayl, who said: Ibn Shihab said: ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr informed me that ʿĀʾisha, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), said: "I never knew my parents except that they were adhering to the religion. No day passed over us without the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) coming to us at both ends of the day, morning and evening. Then when the Muslims were tested..." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to the Muslims: "I have been shown the land of your migration, a place of palm trees between two lava fields (lābba), and they are the two harrah (rocky tracts)." So those who migrated migrated toward Madinah, and most of those who had migrated to the land of Abyssinia returned to Madinah. Abu Bakr (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanh) prepared to go toward Madinah, but the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Wait patiently, for I hope permission will be given to me." Abu Bakr said: "Do you hope for that, may my father be your ransom?" He said: "Yes." So Abu Bakr confined himself to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in order to accompany him, and he fed two riding camels that were with him on the leaves of the samur tree, which is al-khabt (leaves beaten down for fodder), for four months.

Ibn Shihab said: ʿUrwa said: ʿĀʾisha (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhā) said: "One day, while we were sitting in the house of Abu Bakr at the height of midday, someone said to Abu Bakr: 'This is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), veiled, at an hour when he would not come to us.' Abu Bakr said: 'May my father and mother be his ransom! By Allah, he has not come at this hour except for a matter.' She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came and asked permission to enter; he was admitted and entered. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to Abu Bakr: 'Send out those who are with you.' Abu Bakr said: 'They are only your family, may my father be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Indeed I have been permitted to leave.' Abu Bakr said: 'Companionship, may my father be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Yes.' Abu Bakr said: 'Then take, may my father be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah, one of these two riding camels of mine.' The Messenger of Allah said: 'For a price.'" ʿĀʾisha (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhā) said: "We prepared them both with the utmost haste, and we made for them a provision bag (suf'ra) in a saddlebag (jirab). Asma' bint Abi Bakr cut a piece from her waistband (niṭāq) and tied it over the mouth of the saddlebag; for this she was named Dhat al-Niṭaqayn (the one of the two waistbands)." She said: "Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr went to a cave in Mount Thawr, and they stayed there three nights. ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Bakr would spend the night with them; he was a young, alert, and intelligent lad. He would leave them before dawn and be in the morning with the Quraysh in Makkah as if he had spent the night there. He would not hear any plan against them without retaining it until he brought them news of it when darkness fell. ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayra, the freedman of Abu Bakr, would graze a flock of sheep for them, and he would bring them to them when an hour of the night had passed, so they would spend the night on milk (risl), which was the milk of their flock and its fresh milk, until ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayra called to them at the first light of dawn (ghalas). He did this every night of those three nights. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr hired a man from Banu al-Dil, who was of Banu ʿAbd ibn ʿUday, as a skilled guide (hādiyan khirrītan), and al-khirrīt means one expert in guidance. He had sworn an alliance with the family of al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil al-Sahmi, and he was upon the religion of the disbelieving Quraysh. They entrusted him, so they gave him their two riding camels and arranged with him to meet them at the cave of Thawr after three nights with their two camels at dawn on the third day. ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayra and the guide set out with them, and he led them by the coastal road."

Ibn Shihab said: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Malik al-Mudlaji, who is the nephew of Suraqa ibn Malik ibn Juʿshum, informed me that his father informed him that he heard Suraqa ibn Malik ibn Juʿshum say: "Messengers of the disbelieving Quraysh came to us, offering the blood-money (diya) of each one of them, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr (raḍiya Allāhu ʿanh), to whoever killed or captured him. While I was sitting in one of the gatherings of my people, Banu Mudlij, a man from among them came and stood over us while we were sitting, and said: 'O Suraqa, I have just seen black figures on the coast; I think they are Muhammad and his companions.' Suraqa said: 'I knew that they were them, so I said to him: They are not them, but you saw so-and-so and so-and-so who set out before our eyes.' Then I remained in the gathering for a while, then I got up, entered the house, and ordered my slave girl to bring out my horse from behind a hillock and hold it for me. I took my spear and went out with it from the back of the house, and I dragged its point on the ground and lowered its upper end until I reached my horse and mounted it, and I pushed it to bring me near them. When I drew close to them, my horse stumbled and I fell from it, then I got up. I reached my hand to my quiver and drew out the arrows (al-azlam) and cast lots with them, to see whether I would harm them or not. What I disliked came out, so I mounted my horse and disobeyed the arrows; it brought me near until I heard the recitation of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while he did not turn, and Abu Bakr turned often. Then the forelegs of my horse sank into the ground until they reached the knees. I fell from it, then I urged it on and it got up, but it could hardly pull out its legs. When it stood upright, behold, there was a dust rising into the sky like smoke at the traces of its legs. I cast lots with the arrows again, and what I disliked came out. So I called out to them for safety, and they stopped. I mounted my horse and came to them. What had occurred in my heart when I encountered what I encountered of being prevented from them was that the affair of the Prophet (ﷺ) would prevail. I said to him: 'Your people have set a blood-money upon you, and I informed them of what the people intend against them, and I offered them provisions and goods.' They did not take anything from me and did not ask me for anything, except that they said: 'Conceal us.' So I asked him to write for me a document of safe-conduct, and he commanded ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayra, who wrote it on a piece of leather. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went on."

Ibn Shihab said: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) met al-Zubayr in a caravan of Muslims who were merchants returning from Syria, and al-Zubayr clothed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr in white garments. The Muslims in Madinah heard of the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) departure from Makkah, so they would go out every morning to al-Harrah and wait for him until the heat of midday drove them back. One day they returned after having waited a long time. When they had gone to their houses, a man from among the Jews climbed to the top of one of their forts for some matter he was looking at, and he saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions appearing white, the mirage carrying them along. The Jew could not contain himself and cried out at the top of his voice: "O assembly of the Arabs, this is your grandeur (jadd) for which you have been waiting!" The Muslims rushed to their weapons and met the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the edge of al-Harrah. He turned with them to the right until he alighted among Banu Amr ibn Awf, and that was on Monday in the month of Rabi' al-Awwal. Abu Bakr stood up for the people while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat silent. Those Ansar who had come and had not seen the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began greeting Abu Bakr, until the sun struck the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Then Abu Bakr came and shaded him with his cloak, and at that the people recognised the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stayed among Banu Amr ibn Awf for some ten nights, and founded the mosque that was founded upon piety (taqwa), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed in it. Then he mounted his she-camel and set off, the people walking with him, until her kneeling place was at the mosque of the Messenger (ﷺ) in Madinah, where some Muslim men were praying at that time. It was a place for drying dates, belonging to Suhayl and Sahl, two orphan boys under the guardianship of As'ad ibn Zurarah. When his she-camel knelt with him, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This, if Allah wills, is the dwelling place." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned the two boys and bargained with them over the drying-ground so that he might take it as a mosque. They said: "Rather, we give it to you, O Messenger of Allah." Then he built it as a mosque, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began carrying bricks with them in its construction, saying as he carried the bricks: "This load is not the load of Khaybar; this is more righteous, more pure, before our Lord." And he would say: "O Allah, the reward is the reward of the Hereafter, so have mercy on the Ansar and the Muhajirah." Thus he recited (tamaththala) the verse of a man from among the Muslims who was not named to me.

Ibn Shihab said: It has not reached us in the reports that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited a complete line of poetry other than these verses.

Al-Zuhri said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr entered the cave, Allah sent a pair of doves which laid eggs at the bottom of the cave's opening, and the spider until it spun a web. In the narration: a pigeon was made to perch at the mouth of the cave, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, blind their eyes to us." So the pursuers began striking right and left around the cave, saying: "If the two had entered this cave, the eggs of the dove would have been broken and the spider's web torn apart."

Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon him﴾. It was said: upon the Prophet (ﷺ). Ibn Abbas said: upon Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), for the Prophet (ﷺ) had already had tranquility upon him before. ﴿And He supported him with hosts you did not see﴾, and they were the angels, who descended turning the faces and sight of the disbelievers away from seeing him. It was also said: they cast terror into the hearts of the disbelievers until they turned back. Mujahid and al-Kalbi said: He aided him with angels on the Day of Badr; He informed that He turned away the plots of the enemies from him in the cave, then manifested His victory through the angels on the Day of Badr.

﴿And He made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest﴾: their word is shirk, and it is the lowest until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And the word of Allah is the highest﴾ until the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abbas said: it is the saying "There is no god but Allah." It was also said: the word of those who disbelieved is what they plotted among themselves in scheming to kill him, and the word of Allah is Allah's promise that He will support him. Ya'qub recited ﴿wa-kalimata Allah﴾ with a fatha on the ta', as a conjunction (ʿatf) [of the object]. ﴿And Allah is Mighty, Wise.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 41:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾. Al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, Mujahid, Qatadah and Ikrimah said: young and old. And it is reported from Ibn 'Abbas: energetic and not energetic. 'Ata' al-'Awfi said: riding and on foot. Abu Salih said: "light" means light of wealth, i.e., poor, and "heavy" means rich. Ibn Zayd said: the heavy one is the one who has property (ḍay'ah), so he is heavy, disliking to leave his property, and the light one is the one who has no property. It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "light" refers to those of ease in wealth, and "heavy" refers to those in hardship. It was also said: "light" in respect of weapons, i.e., those with little of them, and "heavy" i.e., those who have much of them. al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah said: busy and not busy. Murrah al-Hamdhani said: healthy and sick. Yaman ibn Rabab said: unmarried and married. It was also said: "light" means from your retinue and followers, and "heavy" means those who have many of them. It was also said: "light" means hastening, going out at the moment of hearing the call to arms, and "heavy" means after deliberation and preparation for it.

﴿And strive with your wealth and your persons in the way of Allah. That is better for you, if you only knew.﴾ al-Zuhri said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab went out to the military campaign though one of his eyes had been lost. He was told: "You are ill and afflicted with harm." He said: "Allah has called forth the light and the heavy. If I cannot fight, I will increase the numbers and guard the baggage."

'Ata' al-Khurasani said, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas: this verse was abrogated by His saying: ﴿It was not for the believers to go forth all together﴾ [[See: al-Nasikh wa-l-Mansukh by Ibn Salamah, p. 52; Asbab al-Nuzul pp. 283–284; Ibn Kathir: 2/360.]].

al-Suddi said: When this verse was revealed, its matter weighed heavily upon the people, so Allah the Exalted abrogated it and revealed: ﴿No blame is upon the weak or upon the sick﴾ [[Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh from al-Suddi. al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/208.]] – the verse.

Then there was revealed concerning the hypocrites who stayed behind from the expedition of Tabuk: [[Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi p. 284.]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 42–46:

﴿If it had been a near gain and an easy journey, they would have followed you.﴾ The subject of "kāna" (was) is an implied pronoun, meaning: if what you call them to had been a near gain, that is, a spoil within easy reach, ﴿and a journey of moderate length﴾, meaning near and easy, ﴿they would have followed you﴾, meaning they would have gone out with you. ﴿But the distance seemed long to them﴾, that is, the distance; al-shuqqah (the hardship) is the long journey, because it burdens a person. It was also said: al-shuqqah is the goal they aimed at. ﴿They will swear by Allah, "Had we been able, we would have gone out with you." They destroy themselves﴾, meaning by the false oath. ﴿And Allah knows that they are liars﴾ in their oaths and their faith, because they were in fact able.

﴿Allah has pardoned you﴾. ʿAmr ibn Maymun said: There were two things the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did which he had not been commanded to do: his permitting the hypocrites (to stay behind), and his taking ransom from the captives of Badr. So Allah rebuked him, as you hear.

Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah said: Look at this gentleness: He began with pardon before rebuking him for the sin.

It was also said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, honoured him and raised his station by opening the speech with a supplication for him, as a man says to one he addresses whom he holds in high regard: "May Allah pardon you, what did you do about my need? May Allah be pleased with you, why did you not visit me?" It was also said its meaning is: may Allah continue pardon for you.

﴿Why did you grant them permission﴾, that is, to stay behind from you, ﴿until those who were truthful became clear to you﴾ regarding their excuses, ﴿and you knew the liars﴾ concerning them, that is, you would know those who have no excuse. Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not know the hypocrites at that time.

﴿Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day do not ask your permission to strive with their wealth and their lives﴾, that is, they do not ask you permission to stay behind. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the God-fearing.﴾

﴿Only those ask your permission who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day, and whose hearts are in doubt﴾, that is, they doubted and were hypocritical, ﴿so in their doubt they waver﴾, bewildered.

﴿And if they had intended to go out﴾ to the campaign, ﴿they would have prepared for it﴾, that is, they would have readied for it ﴿a provision﴾, meaning readiness and strength of weapons and mounts. ﴿But Allah disliked their setting out﴾, their going forth, ﴿so He held them back﴾, meaning He prevented and restrained them from going out, ﴿and it was said: "Sit with those who sit"﴾ in your houses, ﴿meaning: with the sick and the disabled.﴾ It was also said: with the women and the children.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿and it was said﴾: meaning some of them said to others: "Sit." It was also said: it was revealed into their hearts, and they were inspired with the causes of abandonment.

The Prophet ﷺ commanded them to take part in jihad (striving in the way of God) for the expedition of Tabuk, so the Messenger of God ﷺ pitched his army at Thaniyyat al-Wada' (the Pass of Farewell). Abdullah ibn Ubayy pitched his camp at Dhu Jadda [[In "A": "Dhi Halwa". "Dhu Jadda" is the clear, well-trodden road.]], below Thaniyyat al-Wada', and his army was not smaller than the other. When the Messenger of God ﷺ set out, Abdullah ibn Ubayy stayed behind, along with those hypocrites and people of doubt who stayed behind with him. God then revealed, consoling His Prophet ﷺ [[Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 284.]]: ﴿Had they gone out with you, they would have added nothing to you but corruption﴾. "They" means the hypocrites. "With you" means among you. ﴿Nothing but corruption﴾ means ruin and evil. The meaning of corruption is spreading cowardice and weakness among the believers by exaggerating the matter. ﴿And they would have hastened between you﴾ means they would have rushed into the midst of you, sowing enmity and hatred among you through slander and carrying tales from one to another. It is also said that ﴿and they would have hastened between you﴾ means they would have rushed to do what harms you.

﴿They would have sought to cause you turmoil﴾ means they would have sought out for you what would test you. They would say: "A great host has been gathered against you," "You will certainly be defeated," "Your enemy will surely prevail over you," and the like. Al-Kalbi said: "They would have sought to cause you turmoil" means defect and evil. Al-Dahhak said: "Turmoil" is polytheism. It is said: "I sought evil or good for him (baghaytu lahu al-sharr wa al-khayr), abghihi bughaan," meaning I searched it out for him, i.e., I sought it for him.

﴿And among you are listeners to them﴾. Mujahid said: its meaning is, among you are those who love them and convey to them what they hear from you, and these are the spies. Qatadah said: its meaning is, among you are those who obey them, that is, they listen to their words and obey them.

﴿And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers﴾.

﴿They had already sought to cause turmoil before, and they had turned matters over against you﴾ means they had sought to turn your companions away from the religion and return them to disbelief, and to discourage people from you before this day, like the act of Abdullah ibn Ubayy on the day of Uhud when he withdrew from you with his companions.

﴿And they turned matters over against you﴾ means they deliberated about you and about overturning your religion, by discouraging people from you and scattering your affair. ﴿Until the truth came﴾ means victory and triumph, ﴿and the command of God prevailed﴾ means the religion of God, ﴿while they were averse﴾.

The words of God, exalted is He: ﴿And among them is one who says, "Grant me leave and do not put me to trial."﴾ It was revealed concerning Jadd ibn Qays, the hypocrite. When the Prophet ﷺ prepared for the expedition of Tabuk, he said: "O Abu Wahb, would you like to fight the Banu al-Asfar?" meaning the Romans, "you could take some of their women as concubines and servants." Jadd said: "O Messenger of God, my people know that I am a man greatly drawn to women, and I fear that if I see the women of the Banu al-Asfar I will not be able to restrain myself. Grant me leave to stay behind and do not put me to trial with them. I will help you with my wealth." Ibn Abbas said: Jadd ibn Qays made an excuse, though he had no excuse except hypocrisy, so the Prophet ﷺ turned away from him. He said: "I have granted you leave." Then God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And among them﴾ meaning among the hypocrites ﴿is one who says, "Grant me leave"﴾ to remain behind ﴿"and do not put me to trial"﴾ with the women of the Banu al-Asfar. Qatadah said: "And do not make me sinful." ﴿Surely, in trial they have fallen﴾ means they have fallen into polytheism and sin through their hypocrisy and their opposition to the command of God and the command of His Messenger. ﴿And indeed, Hell encompasses the disbelievers﴾ [enclosing them] [[In "B": "surrounding them".]] and gathering them within it.

﴿If good befalls you﴾ means victory and spoils, ﴿it distresses them﴾ means it grieves them, meaning the hypocrites. ﴿And if a misfortune strikes you﴾ means killing and defeat, ﴿they say, "We had already taken our precaution"﴾ means we had taken our precaution, that is, we had adopted caution by staying away from the campaign, ﴿before﴾ meaning before this misfortune, ﴿and they turn away﴾ and withdraw ﴿rejoicing﴾, glad at the misfortune that has befallen you.

﴿Say﴾ to them, O Muhammad, ﴿"Nothing will befall us except what God has decreed for us"﴾ meaning what He has written for us in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). ﴿He is our Protector﴾ our Helper and Guardian. Al-Kalbi said: He is more entitled to us than ourselves in death and life. ﴿And upon God let the believers rely﴾.

﴿Say, "Do you await for us anything but one of the two best outcomes?"﴾ meaning, O hypocrites, do you wait for us? Either victory and spoils, or martyrdom and forgiveness. We have related from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "God has guaranteed for whoever strives in His cause, whom nothing brings out of his house except striving in His cause, and the confirmation of His word: that He will admit him to Paradise, or return him to the dwelling from which he went out, along with the reward or spoils he has gained" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Khums, chapter on the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "The spoils have been made lawful for you," 6/220; and by Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the virtue of jihad and going out in the way of God, no. 1876, 3/1496.]].

The words of God, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And we await for you﴾ one of the two evils: ﴿that God will afflict you with a punishment from Himself﴾ and destroy you as He destroyed the earlier nations, ﴿or by our hands﴾ meaning by the hands of the believers, if you reveal what is in your hearts. ﴿So wait; indeed, we are waiting with you﴾. Al-Hasan said: "So wait" for the promises of Satan; "indeed, we are waiting" for the promises of God, the manifestation of His religion and the uprooting of those who oppose it.

﴿Say, "Spend willingly or unwillingly"﴾. This is a command with the meaning of a condition and its consequence, that is: if you spend willingly or unwillingly. It was revealed concerning Jadd ibn Qays when he asked permission to stay behind, saying, "I will help you with my wealth." It is as if he said: if you spend willingly or unwillingly, ﴿it will never be accepted from you; indeed, you have been a defiantly disobedient people﴾, that is, because you were.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 55–57:

﴿So let not their wealth nor their children impress you.﴾ Al-i'jab (being impressed) is delight in something one marvels at. He says: do not be pleased with the wealth and children We have bestowed upon them, for when a servant is under istidraj (gradual lead-on) from Allah, Allah increases his wealth and his children. ﴿Allah only intends to punish them through them in the life of this world.﴾ If it is asked: how can there be punishment through wealth and children when they enjoy them in the life of this world?

It is said: Mujahid and Qatadah said there is an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the verse, its meaning being: ﴿So let not their wealth nor their children impress you in the life of this world; Allah only intends to punish them through them in the Hereafter.﴾

It is also said: the punishment is through the calamities that befall their wealth and children.

Al-Hasan said: He punishes them through them in this world by taking the zakat from them and by spending in the way of Allah. It is also said: He punishes them through the toil in gathering it, the anxiety in guarding it, the reluctance in spending it, and the regret over leaving it to those who will not praise them, and then they come before a King who will not excuse them.

﴿And their souls depart,⁠﻿ meaning: they exit, ﴿while they are disbelievers,⁠﻿ meaning: they die upon disbelief.

﴿And they swear by Allah that they are indeed of you,⁠﻿ meaning: upon your religion, ﴿but they are not of you; rather they are a people who are fearful⁠﻿ [they fear that they will reveal what they are upon]. [[Omitted from "A".]]

﴿If they could find a refuge⁠﻿ — a shelter, a fortress, and a stronghold. ʿAtaʾ said: a place of escape. It is also said: a people among whom they would feel secure.

﴿Or caves⁠﻿ — hollows in the mountains, plural of maghara, which is the place where one goes in and hides, i.e., conceals himself. ʿAtaʾ said: tunnels.

﴿Or a place of entry⁠﻿ — the place of entering into it; the original form is mudtakhal (muftaʿal), from adkhala, yudkhilu. Mujahid said: a place of safety. Qatadah said: a burrow. Al-Kalbi said: a tunnel in the earth like the tunnel of the jerboa. Al-Hasan said: a way into which they could enter, contrary to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. It is also read: ﴿madkhalan⁠﻿ with a fatha on the mim and a light dal, and Ya'qub read it this way. ﴿They would turn away to it⁠﻿ — they would flee to it, running from you, ﴿rushing headlong⁠﻿ — hastening in aversion and flight, nothing turning their faces back. The meaning of the verse is: if they found a way of escape from you and a place of refuge, they would part from you.
