Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 58:

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And among them are those who find fault with you concerning the charities﴾ [the verse]. It was revealed concerning Dhu'l-Khuwaysira al-Tamimi, whose name was Hurqus ibn Zuhayr, the origin of the Kharijites (al-Khawarij, the seceders).

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) related to us: Abu'l-Yaman related to us: Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman informed me that Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "While we were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he was distributing a distribution among us, Dhu'l-Khuwaysira came to him, and he was a man from the Banu Tamim, and he said: 'O Messenger of Allah, be just!' He said: 'Woe to you! Who will be just if I am not just? You have failed and lost if I am not just.'" Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "O Messenger of Allah, permit me to deal with him, and I will strike his neck." He said to him: "Leave him, for he has companions, such that one of you will belittle his prayer in comparison with their prayer, and his fasting in comparison with their fasting. They recite the Qur'an but it does not go past their collarbones. They pass through the religion as an arrow passes through the game. One looks at its blade and finds nothing on it, then looks at its feathers and finds nothing on them, then looks at its shaft, which is its wood, and finds nothing on it, then looks at its fletching and finds nothing on it, having outrun the dung and the blood. Their sign is a black man, one of whose arms is like the breast of a woman, or like a lump of flesh that jiggles. They will emerge at a time of division among the people." Abu Sa'id said: "I bear witness that I heard this hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I bear witness that Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) fought them while I was with him. He commanded concerning that man, and he was sought and found, and he was brought until I looked at him according to the description of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) which he had described." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Manaqib, chapter on the signs of prophethood in Islam: 6/617-618, and Muslim in al-Zakat, chapter on mentioning the fighting of the Kharijites and their attributes, no. (1064), 2/744-745. And the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 10/224.]

al-Kalbi said: A man from the hypocrites, called Abu'l-Jawwaz [in B: Dhu'l-Hawwat], said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "You did not divide equally," so Allah the Exalted revealed [Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. 286]: ﴿And among them are those who find fault with you concerning the charities﴾, i.e., they criticize you regarding its affairs and its distribution, and they slander you concerning it. It is said: lamazahu and hamazahu, meaning he found fault with him. The meaning is that the hypocrites used to say that Muhammad gives only to whom he loves. Ya'qub read ﴿yalmizuka﴾ wherever it occurs. Mujahid said: "yalmizuka" means yarwuzuka, meaning: he tests you.

﴿If they are given from it, they are pleased, and if they are not given from it, behold, they become angry﴾. It was said: if they are given much, they rejoice, and if they are given little, they become angry.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 59–60 (part 1 of 2):**

﴿Had they been content with what Allah and His Messenger had given them﴾, that is, had they been satisfied with what Allah and His Messenger had apportioned to them, ﴿and said: "Allah is sufficient for us"﴾, meaning Allah suffices us, ﴿"Allah will give us of His bounty, and His Messenger too"﴾, meaning what we need, ﴿"indeed we turn to Allah in hope"﴾, that He may expand His bounty upon us and make us independent of charity and of other people's wealth. The answer to "law" (lau, "if") is omitted, meaning: it would have been better for them and more beneficial to them.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Charity is only for the poor and the needy﴾, and the verse. In this verse Allah, the Exalted, specifies the recipients of the sadaqat (the obligatory charities, zakat) and makes them eight categories.

It is related from Ziyad ibn al-Harith al-Suda'i, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and pledged allegiance to him. A man came to him and said: "Give me from the charity." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Indeed Allah was not pleased to leave the judgment concerning the charities to a prophet or to anyone else, until He Himself judged concerning them and divided them into eight portions. So if you are one of those portions, I will give you your due."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in az-Zakat, chapter "Who is to be given from the charity": 2/230-231; ad-Daraqutni in az-Zakat 2/137; and al-Bayhaqi in as-Sunan: 4/174. al-Mundhiri said: "In its chain is Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad al-Afriqi, about whom more than one has spoken."]]

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿for the poor and the needy﴾. So the first category of the charity is the fuqara' (the poor), and the second is the masakin (the needy).

The scholars differed concerning the description of the faqir (poor) and the miskin (needy). Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ikrimah and al-Zuhri said: the faqir is the one who does not ask, and the miskin is the one who asks.

Ibn Umar said: "He is not poor who gathers a dirham to a dirham and a date to a date. Rather, the poor one is he who has purified his soul and his clothing and has no means at all; the ignorant person considers them rich because of their restraint."

Qatadah said: "The faqir is the needy one who is disabled, and the miskin is the able-bodied needy one."

It is related from Ikrimah that he said: "The fuqara' are from among the Muslims, and the masakin are from among the People of the Book."

Al-Shafi'i said: "The faqir is one who has no property and no trade that suits him, whether he is disabled or not. The miskin is one who has property or a trade but it does not suffice him, whether he asks or does not ask." So according to him the miskin is in a better condition than the faqir, because Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿As for the boat, it belonged to poor men﴾ (Surah al-Kahf 18:79). He affirmed for them ownership together with the name of "miskin."

According to the companions of opinion (the Hanafis), the faqir is in a better condition than the miskin.

Al-Qutaybi said: "The faqir is the one who has the means of subsistence, and the miskin is the one who has nothing at all."

It was also said: "The faqir is one who has a dwelling and a servant, and the miskin is one who owns nothing." They said: "Everyone who is in need of something is 'muftaqir' (in need) of it, even if he is independent of others." Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿You are the poor in need of Allah﴾ (Surah Fatir 35:15). And the miskin is one in need of everything. Do you not see how He urged feeding him, and made the expiation food for him? And there is no poverty greater than the need to satisfy hunger.

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: "The fuqara' are the Muhajirun (emigrants), and the masakin are those Muslims who did not emigrate."

In sum: faqr (poverty) and maskana (neediness) are two expressions for need and weakness of condition. The faqir is the needy one whom need has broken to the back, and the miskin is the one whose self has become weak and has become still from striving to seek sustenance.

Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal narrated to us: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm narrated to us: al-Rabi' narrated to us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Sufyan ibn Uyayna informed us, from Hisham, that is Ibn Urwa, from his father, from Ubayd Allah ibn Adi ibn al-Khiyar: that two men informed him that they came to the Messenger of Allah and asked him about the charity [so he looked at them and considered them][[What is between the brackets is from Musnad al-Shafi'i.]], and he said: "If you wish, I will give you, but there is no share in it for a rich person, nor for a strong earner."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in az-Zakat, chapter "Concerning who is given from the charity": 2/233; an-Nasa'i in az-Zakat, chapter "Asking by one who is rich and earns": 5/99-100; ash-Shafi'i in al-Musnad: 1/244; at-Tahawi in Sharh Ma'ani al-Athar: 2/15; and al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/81. Imam Ahmad said: "How excellent a hadith!" See al-Talkhis al-Habir: 3/108.]]

They differed concerning the limit of wealth which prevents one from taking charity. The majority said: its limit is that one has what suffices him and his dependents for a year; this is the view of Malik and al-Shafi'i.

The companions of opinion (Hanafis) said: its limit is that one owns two hundred dirhams.

Some people said: whoever owns fifty dirhams, charity is not lawful for him, on the basis of what we have narrated from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever asks people while he has what suffices him will come on the Day of Resurrection with his asking being scratches, or scrapes, or gashes on his face." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what suffices him?" He said: "Fifty dirhams, or their value in gold."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in az-Zakat, chapter "Who is given from the charity and the limit of wealth": 2/226; at-Tirmidhi in az-Zakat, chapter "What has been reported about who is lawfully given zakat": 3/313-314, and he said: "A good hadith; Shu'bah has spoken about Hakim ibn Jubayr because of this hadith." Also narrated by an-Nasa'i in az-Zakat, chapter "The limit of wealth": 5/97; Ibn Majah in az-Zakat, chapter "Who asks while having sufficient means," no. (1840): 1/589; and al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/83.]] This is the view of al-Thawri, Ibn al-Mubarak, Ahmad and Ishaq. They said: it is not permissible for a man to be given more than fifty dirhams from zakat. It was also said: forty dirhams, on the basis of what is reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever asks while he has an uqiyya (ounce) or its equivalent, has asked insistently."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in az-Zakat, chapter "Who is given from the charity": 2/228-229; an-Nasa'i in az-Zakat, chapter "If he does not have dirhams but has their equivalent": 5/98-99; and al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/84.]]

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and the workers who collect it﴾. These are the sa'in (collectors) who take charge of receiving the charities from their owners and placing them where they belong. They are given from the wealth of the charity, whether they are poor or rich, and they are given the equivalent wage of their work.

Al-Dahhak and Mujahid said: "They have one-eighth of the charity."

﴿And those whose hearts are to be reconciled﴾. The fourth category of those entitled to charity is: al-mu'allafa qulubuhum (those whose hearts are to be reconciled). They are of two kinds: a kind who are Muslims, and a kind who are disbelievers.

As for the Muslims, they are of two types. One type entered Islam while their intention in it was weak, so the Prophet ﷺ would give them in order to reconcile their hearts, as he gave Uyayna ibn Badr, al-Aqra' ibn Habis, and al-Abbas ibn Mirdas. The other type embraced Islam with a strong intention and were nobles among their people, such as Adi ibn Hatim and al-Zibriqan ibn Badr. The Prophet ﷺ would give them in order to win over their people and to encourage their like to embrace Islam. These may be given by the imam from one-fifth of the one-fifth (khums al-khums) of the spoils of war and of the fay', the share of the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ used to give them from that and did not give them from the charities.

The second kind of Muslim mu'allafa: a group of Muslims stationed opposite a group of disbelievers in a remote place (mutanat, "far away") which the armies of the Muslims cannot reach except with great expense, and they do not fight, either because of the weakness of their intention or the weakness of their condition. So the imam may give them from the share of the warriors (ghuzat) from the wealth of charity. It was said: from the share of the mu'allafa. Among them are also a group opposite a company of those who withhold zakat, who take zakat from them and carry it to the imam; the imam gives them from the share of the mu'allafa from the charities. It was said: from the share of "in the way of Allah."

It is narrated that Adi ibn Hatim came to Abu Bakr al-Siddiq with three hundred camels from the charities of his people, and Abu Bakr gave him thirty camels from them.

As for the disbelievers among the mu'allafa: they are those whose evil is feared from them, or whose Islam is hoped for. The imam may wish to give this one out of fear of his evil, or to give that one to encourage him toward Islam. The Prophet ﷺ used to give them from one-fifth of the one-fifth, as he gave Safwan ibn Umayya because of what he saw of his inclination to Islam. But today, Allah has honored Islam, and to Him be praise, and has made it sufficient that men should be won over through it; so no polytheist is to be given to win him over in any way. Many people of knowledge have said this: that the mu'allafa category has ended and its share has lapsed. This was related from Ikrimah, and it is the view of al-Sha'bi, and Malik, al-Thawri, the companions of opinion, and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh held it too.

Others said: their share remains, which is related from al-Hasan, and it is the view of al-Zuhri, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali, and Abu Thawr. Ahmad said: they are to be given if the Muslims are in need of that.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and for the captives (fi al-riqab)﴾. The fifth category is: al-riqab (captives/slaves), namely the mukatabun (slaves who have contracted to buy their freedom). They have a share of the charity. This is the view of most jurists, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Nakha'i, al-Zuhri, al-Layth ibn Sa'd and al-Shafi'i held it. A group said: the share of the riqab is used to buy slaves who are then freed. This is the view of al-Hasan, and Malik, Ahmad and Ishaq held it too.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and the debtors﴾. The sixth category is: al-gharimun (debtors). They are of two kinds. One kind incurred debts for themselves in what is not disobedience to Allah; they are given from the charity if they do not have wealth sufficient to pay their debts. If they have enough to pay, they are not given. The other kind incurred debts for what is good and for reconciling people; they are given from the wealth of charity to pay their debts, even if they are rich.

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata' ibn Yasar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Charity is not lawful for a rich person except for five: for one who fights in the way of Allah, or for a debtor, or for a man who bought it with his own wealth, or for a man who has a poor neighbour who gives charity to the poor and the poor man gives a gift to the rich man, or for a worker who collects it."[[Narrated as mursal (with a broken chain): Malik in al-Muwatta', Kitab az-Zakat, chapter "Taking charity and who is permitted to take it": 1/268; and Abu Dawud in az-Zakat, chapter "Who is permitted to take charity while being rich": 2/234-235.]]

It was narrated by Ma'mar, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet ﷺ, connected (muttasilan), with the same meaning.[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in the same place, and Ibn Majah in az-Zakat, no. (1841): 1/590. And al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/89.]]

As for one whose debt was incurred in disobedience, he is not to be given anything.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and in the way of Allah﴾. By this are meant the warriors (ghuzat). They have a share of the charity; they are given when they wish to go out to fight, and what they need for the matter of fighting: provisions, clothing, weapons, and mounts, even if they are rich. Nothing from it is given for the Hajj according to most people of knowledge.

A group said: it is permissible to spend the share of "in the way of Allah" on the Hajj. This is related from Ibn Abbas, and it is the view of al-Hasan, Ahmad and Ishaq.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and the wayfarer﴾. The eighth category is: ibn al-sabil (the wayfarer). Whoever intends a lawful journey and does not have what will carry him across the distance is given from the charity an amount sufficient to cross that distance, whether or not he has wealth in the city to which he is moving.

Qatadah said: "Ibn al-sabil is the guest."

The jurists of Iraq said: "Ibn al-sabil is the pilgrim who has been cut off."

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿an obligation﴾, that is, obligatory, ﴿from Allah﴾. It is in the accusative as an absolute (qat') or it is said: as a verbal noun (masdar), meaning: Allah has prescribed these things as an obligation.

ALLAH is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

The jurists differed concerning the manner of distributing the zakat (ṣadaqāt), and concerning the permissibility of giving it to only some of the categories:

A group held that it is not permissible to give all of it to some of them while the other categories are present. This is the view of ʿIkrimah, and it is also the position of al-Shafiʿi, who said: The zakat of each type of property must be distributed among those present from the six categories whose shares are fixed, in equal portions, because the share of al-Muallafah (those whose hearts are to be reconciled) has lapsed, and the share of the administrator (ʿamil) is when he distributes it himself. Then the share of each category must not be given to fewer than three of them if three or more of them are present. If there is a difference among those three, it is permissible. If only one person of some category is found, that category's share is given to him, provided it does not exceed the limit of entitlement. If his need is met and something remains, he returns it to the rest.

Another group held that if the whole amount is given to one category of these categories, or to one person from among them, it is permissible. Allah the Exalted named these eight categories only to inform that zakat is not to be taken out of these categories, not as an obligation to divide it among all of them. This is the view of ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbas, and Saʿid ibn Jubayr and ʿAtaʾ also said so. Sufyan al-Thawri and the Companions of opinion (Ashab al-Ra'y) adopted it, and Ahmad also said so, saying: It is permissible to place it in one category, though distributing it is better.

Ibrahim said: If the wealth is large enough to allow division, he divides it among the categories; if it is small, it is permissible to place it in one category.

Malik said: He should seek out the place of need among them, and give precedence to the most deserving, from among the people of need and hardship. If he sees the need among the poor in one year to be greater, he gives them precedence; and if in another year he sees the need among another category, he shifts it to them.

Whoever is given anything of the zakat must not be given more than the measure of his entitlement. So the poor man is not given more than the measure of his sufficiency. When the least degree of wealth (ghina) is attained, he is not given after that. If he is a craftsman but does not have the tools of his craft, he is given an amount with which he can acquire the tools of his craft. The worker (ʿamil) is not given more than the wage of his work. The mukatab (slave seeking manumission by purchase) is given an amount by which he can be freed. The debtor (gharim) is given an amount equal to his debt. The one fighting in the cause of Allah (ghazi) is given an amount equal to his expenses for going, returning, and staying in his campaign, and what he needs of a horse and weapons. The wayfarer (ibn al-sabil) is given an amount equal to reaching his destination or his place of return.

They differed concerning transferring zakat from the land of the wealth to another place, while the eligible recipients are present there. Most people of knowledge disliked it, on account of what Abu ʿUthman Saʿid ibn Ismaʿil al-Dabbi informed us: Abu Muhammad ʿAbd al-Jabbar ibn Muhammad al-Jarrahi informed us: Abu al-ʿAbbas Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mahbubi narrated to us: Abu ʿIsa al-Tirmidhi narrated to us: Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Waki narrated to us: Zakariyya ibn Ishaq al-Makki narrated to us: Yahya ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Sayfi narrated to us from Abu Maʿbad, from Ibn ʿAbbas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Muʿadh to Yemen and said: "You are going to a people who are People of the Book, so invite them to testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. If they obey you in that, then inform them that Allah has enjoined upon them five prayers in the day and night. If they obey you in that, then inform them that Allah has enjoined upon them a charity (ṣadaqah) taken from their wealthy and returned to their poor. If they obey you in that, then beware of the choicest of their property, and beware of the supplication of the oppressed, for there is no barrier between it and Allah." [Narrated by the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) and mentioned previously.]

This indicates that the zakat of the wealthy of each people is returned to the poor of that same people.

They agreed that if it is transported from one land to another, it is discharged though disliked, and the obligation is lifted from the one liable, except what is reported from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz (may Allah be pleased with him) that he returned a charity that had been carried from Khurasan to Syria to its place in Khurasan.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 59–60 (part 1 of 2):**

﴿Had they been content with what Allah and His Messenger had given them﴾, that is, had they been satisfied with what Allah and His Messenger had apportioned to them, ﴿and said: "Allah is sufficient for us"﴾, meaning Allah suffices us, ﴿"Allah will give us of His bounty, and His Messenger too"﴾, meaning what we need, ﴿"indeed we turn to Allah in hope"﴾, that He may expand His bounty upon us and make us independent of charity and of other people's wealth. The answer to "law" (lau, "if") is omitted, meaning: it would have been better for them and more beneficial to them.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Charity is only for the poor and the needy﴾, and the verse. In this verse Allah, the Exalted, specifies the recipients of the sadaqat (the obligatory charities, zakat) and makes them eight categories.

It is related from Ziyad ibn al-Harith al-Suda'i, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and pledged allegiance to him. A man came to him and said: "Give me from the charity." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Indeed Allah was not pleased to leave the judgment concerning the charities to a prophet or to anyone else, until He Himself judged concerning them and divided them into eight portions. So if you are one of those portions, I will give you your due."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in az-Zakat, chapter "Who is to be given from the charity": 2/230-231; ad-Daraqutni in az-Zakat 2/137; and al-Bayhaqi in as-Sunan: 4/174. al-Mundhiri said: "In its chain is Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad al-Afriqi, about whom more than one has spoken."]]

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿for the poor and the needy﴾. So the first category of the charity is the fuqara' (the poor), and the second is the masakin (the needy).

The scholars differed concerning the description of the faqir (poor) and the miskin (needy). Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ikrimah and al-Zuhri said: the faqir is the one who does not ask, and the miskin is the one who asks.

Ibn Umar said: "He is not poor who gathers a dirham to a dirham and a date to a date. Rather, the poor one is he who has purified his soul and his clothing and has no means at all; the ignorant person considers them rich because of their restraint."

Qatadah said: "The faqir is the needy one who is disabled, and the miskin is the able-bodied needy one."

It is related from Ikrimah that he said: "The fuqara' are from among the Muslims, and the masakin are from among the People of the Book."

Al-Shafi'i said: "The faqir is one who has no property and no trade that suits him, whether he is disabled or not. The miskin is one who has property or a trade but it does not suffice him, whether he asks or does not ask." So according to him the miskin is in a better condition than the faqir, because Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿As for the boat, it belonged to poor men﴾ (Surah al-Kahf 18:79). He affirmed for them ownership together with the name of "miskin."

According to the companions of opinion (the Hanafis), the faqir is in a better condition than the miskin.

Al-Qutaybi said: "The faqir is the one who has the means of subsistence, and the miskin is the one who has nothing at all."

It was also said: "The faqir is one who has a dwelling and a servant, and the miskin is one who owns nothing." They said: "Everyone who is in need of something is 'muftaqir' (in need) of it, even if he is independent of others." Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿You are the poor in need of Allah﴾ (Surah Fatir 35:15). And the miskin is one in need of everything. Do you not see how He urged feeding him, and made the expiation food for him? And there is no poverty greater than the need to satisfy hunger.

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: "The fuqara' are the Muhajirun (emigrants), and the masakin are those Muslims who did not emigrate."

In sum: faqr (poverty) and maskana (neediness) are two expressions for need and weakness of condition. The faqir is the needy one whom need has broken to the back, and the miskin is the one whose self has become weak and has become still from striving to seek sustenance.

Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal narrated to us: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm narrated to us: al-Rabi' narrated to us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Sufyan ibn Uyayna informed us, from Hisham, that is Ibn Urwa, from his father, from Ubayd Allah ibn Adi ibn al-Khiyar: that two men informed him that they came to the Messenger of Allah and asked him about the charity [so he looked at them and considered them][[What is between the brackets is from Musnad al-Shafi'i.]], and he said: "If you wish, I will give you, but there is no share in it for a rich person, nor for a strong earner."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in az-Zakat, chapter "Concerning who is given from the charity": 2/233; an-Nasa'i in az-Zakat, chapter "Asking by one who is rich and earns": 5/99-100; ash-Shafi'i in al-Musnad: 1/244; at-Tahawi in Sharh Ma'ani al-Athar: 2/15; and al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/81. Imam Ahmad said: "How excellent a hadith!" See al-Talkhis al-Habir: 3/108.]]

They differed concerning the limit of wealth which prevents one from taking charity. The majority said: its limit is that one has what suffices him and his dependents for a year; this is the view of Malik and al-Shafi'i.

The companions of opinion (Hanafis) said: its limit is that one owns two hundred dirhams.

Some people said: whoever owns fifty dirhams, charity is not lawful for him, on the basis of what we have narrated from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever asks people while he has what suffices him will come on the Day of Resurrection with his asking being scratches, or scrapes, or gashes on his face." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what suffices him?" He said: "Fifty dirhams, or their value in gold."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in az-Zakat, chapter "Who is given from the charity and the limit of wealth": 2/226; at-Tirmidhi in az-Zakat, chapter "What has been reported about who is lawfully given zakat": 3/313-314, and he said: "A good hadith; Shu'bah has spoken about Hakim ibn Jubayr because of this hadith." Also narrated by an-Nasa'i in az-Zakat, chapter "The limit of wealth": 5/97; Ibn Majah in az-Zakat, chapter "Who asks while having sufficient means," no. (1840): 1/589; and al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/83.]] This is the view of al-Thawri, Ibn al-Mubarak, Ahmad and Ishaq. They said: it is not permissible for a man to be given more than fifty dirhams from zakat. It was also said: forty dirhams, on the basis of what is reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever asks while he has an uqiyya (ounce) or its equivalent, has asked insistently."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in az-Zakat, chapter "Who is given from the charity": 2/228-229; an-Nasa'i in az-Zakat, chapter "If he does not have dirhams but has their equivalent": 5/98-99; and al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/84.]]

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and the workers who collect it﴾. These are the sa'in (collectors) who take charge of receiving the charities from their owners and placing them where they belong. They are given from the wealth of the charity, whether they are poor or rich, and they are given the equivalent wage of their work.

Al-Dahhak and Mujahid said: "They have one-eighth of the charity."

﴿And those whose hearts are to be reconciled﴾. The fourth category of those entitled to charity is: al-mu'allafa qulubuhum (those whose hearts are to be reconciled). They are of two kinds: a kind who are Muslims, and a kind who are disbelievers.

As for the Muslims, they are of two types. One type entered Islam while their intention in it was weak, so the Prophet ﷺ would give them in order to reconcile their hearts, as he gave Uyayna ibn Badr, al-Aqra' ibn Habis, and al-Abbas ibn Mirdas. The other type embraced Islam with a strong intention and were nobles among their people, such as Adi ibn Hatim and al-Zibriqan ibn Badr. The Prophet ﷺ would give them in order to win over their people and to encourage their like to embrace Islam. These may be given by the imam from one-fifth of the one-fifth (khums al-khums) of the spoils of war and of the fay', the share of the Prophet ﷺ, and the Prophet ﷺ used to give them from that and did not give them from the charities.

The second kind of Muslim mu'allafa: a group of Muslims stationed opposite a group of disbelievers in a remote place (mutanat, "far away") which the armies of the Muslims cannot reach except with great expense, and they do not fight, either because of the weakness of their intention or the weakness of their condition. So the imam may give them from the share of the warriors (ghuzat) from the wealth of charity. It was said: from the share of the mu'allafa. Among them are also a group opposite a company of those who withhold zakat, who take zakat from them and carry it to the imam; the imam gives them from the share of the mu'allafa from the charities. It was said: from the share of "in the way of Allah."

It is narrated that Adi ibn Hatim came to Abu Bakr al-Siddiq with three hundred camels from the charities of his people, and Abu Bakr gave him thirty camels from them.

As for the disbelievers among the mu'allafa: they are those whose evil is feared from them, or whose Islam is hoped for. The imam may wish to give this one out of fear of his evil, or to give that one to encourage him toward Islam. The Prophet ﷺ used to give them from one-fifth of the one-fifth, as he gave Safwan ibn Umayya because of what he saw of his inclination to Islam. But today, Allah has honored Islam, and to Him be praise, and has made it sufficient that men should be won over through it; so no polytheist is to be given to win him over in any way. Many people of knowledge have said this: that the mu'allafa category has ended and its share has lapsed. This was related from Ikrimah, and it is the view of al-Sha'bi, and Malik, al-Thawri, the companions of opinion, and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh held it too.

Others said: their share remains, which is related from al-Hasan, and it is the view of al-Zuhri, Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali, and Abu Thawr. Ahmad said: they are to be given if the Muslims are in need of that.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and for the captives (fi al-riqab)﴾. The fifth category is: al-riqab (captives/slaves), namely the mukatabun (slaves who have contracted to buy their freedom). They have a share of the charity. This is the view of most jurists, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Nakha'i, al-Zuhri, al-Layth ibn Sa'd and al-Shafi'i held it. A group said: the share of the riqab is used to buy slaves who are then freed. This is the view of al-Hasan, and Malik, Ahmad and Ishaq held it too.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and the debtors﴾. The sixth category is: al-gharimun (debtors). They are of two kinds. One kind incurred debts for themselves in what is not disobedience to Allah; they are given from the charity if they do not have wealth sufficient to pay their debts. If they have enough to pay, they are not given. The other kind incurred debts for what is good and for reconciling people; they are given from the wealth of charity to pay their debts, even if they are rich.

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata' ibn Yasar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Charity is not lawful for a rich person except for five: for one who fights in the way of Allah, or for a debtor, or for a man who bought it with his own wealth, or for a man who has a poor neighbour who gives charity to the poor and the poor man gives a gift to the rich man, or for a worker who collects it."[[Narrated as mursal (with a broken chain): Malik in al-Muwatta', Kitab az-Zakat, chapter "Taking charity and who is permitted to take it": 1/268; and Abu Dawud in az-Zakat, chapter "Who is permitted to take charity while being rich": 2/234-235.]]

It was narrated by Ma'mar, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet ﷺ, connected (muttasilan), with the same meaning.[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in the same place, and Ibn Majah in az-Zakat, no. (1841): 1/590. And al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/89.]]

As for one whose debt was incurred in disobedience, he is not to be given anything.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and in the way of Allah﴾. By this are meant the warriors (ghuzat). They have a share of the charity; they are given when they wish to go out to fight, and what they need for the matter of fighting: provisions, clothing, weapons, and mounts, even if they are rich. Nothing from it is given for the Hajj according to most people of knowledge.

A group said: it is permissible to spend the share of "in the way of Allah" on the Hajj. This is related from Ibn Abbas, and it is the view of al-Hasan, Ahmad and Ishaq.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and the wayfarer﴾. The eighth category is: ibn al-sabil (the wayfarer). Whoever intends a lawful journey and does not have what will carry him across the distance is given from the charity an amount sufficient to cross that distance, whether or not he has wealth in the city to which he is moving.

Qatadah said: "Ibn al-sabil is the guest."

The jurists of Iraq said: "Ibn al-sabil is the pilgrim who has been cut off."

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿an obligation﴾, that is, obligatory, ﴿from Allah﴾. It is in the accusative as an absolute (qat') or it is said: as a verbal noun (masdar), meaning: Allah has prescribed these things as an obligation.

ALLAH is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

The jurists differed concerning the manner of distributing the zakat (ṣadaqāt), and concerning the permissibility of giving it to only some of the categories:

A group held that it is not permissible to give all of it to some of them while the other categories are present. This is the view of ʿIkrimah, and it is also the position of al-Shafiʿi, who said: The zakat of each type of property must be distributed among those present from the six categories whose shares are fixed, in equal portions, because the share of al-Muallafah (those whose hearts are to be reconciled) has lapsed, and the share of the administrator (ʿamil) is when he distributes it himself. Then the share of each category must not be given to fewer than three of them if three or more of them are present. If there is a difference among those three, it is permissible. If only one person of some category is found, that category's share is given to him, provided it does not exceed the limit of entitlement. If his need is met and something remains, he returns it to the rest.

Another group held that if the whole amount is given to one category of these categories, or to one person from among them, it is permissible. Allah the Exalted named these eight categories only to inform that zakat is not to be taken out of these categories, not as an obligation to divide it among all of them. This is the view of ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbas, and Saʿid ibn Jubayr and ʿAtaʾ also said so. Sufyan al-Thawri and the Companions of opinion (Ashab al-Ra'y) adopted it, and Ahmad also said so, saying: It is permissible to place it in one category, though distributing it is better.

Ibrahim said: If the wealth is large enough to allow division, he divides it among the categories; if it is small, it is permissible to place it in one category.

Malik said: He should seek out the place of need among them, and give precedence to the most deserving, from among the people of need and hardship. If he sees the need among the poor in one year to be greater, he gives them precedence; and if in another year he sees the need among another category, he shifts it to them.

Whoever is given anything of the zakat must not be given more than the measure of his entitlement. So the poor man is not given more than the measure of his sufficiency. When the least degree of wealth (ghina) is attained, he is not given after that. If he is a craftsman but does not have the tools of his craft, he is given an amount with which he can acquire the tools of his craft. The worker (ʿamil) is not given more than the wage of his work. The mukatab (slave seeking manumission by purchase) is given an amount by which he can be freed. The debtor (gharim) is given an amount equal to his debt. The one fighting in the cause of Allah (ghazi) is given an amount equal to his expenses for going, returning, and staying in his campaign, and what he needs of a horse and weapons. The wayfarer (ibn al-sabil) is given an amount equal to reaching his destination or his place of return.

They differed concerning transferring zakat from the land of the wealth to another place, while the eligible recipients are present there. Most people of knowledge disliked it, on account of what Abu ʿUthman Saʿid ibn Ismaʿil al-Dabbi informed us: Abu Muhammad ʿAbd al-Jabbar ibn Muhammad al-Jarrahi informed us: Abu al-ʿAbbas Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mahbubi narrated to us: Abu ʿIsa al-Tirmidhi narrated to us: Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Waki narrated to us: Zakariyya ibn Ishaq al-Makki narrated to us: Yahya ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Sayfi narrated to us from Abu Maʿbad, from Ibn ʿAbbas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Muʿadh to Yemen and said: "You are going to a people who are People of the Book, so invite them to testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. If they obey you in that, then inform them that Allah has enjoined upon them five prayers in the day and night. If they obey you in that, then inform them that Allah has enjoined upon them a charity (ṣadaqah) taken from their wealthy and returned to their poor. If they obey you in that, then beware of the choicest of their property, and beware of the supplication of the oppressed, for there is no barrier between it and Allah." [Narrated by the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) and mentioned previously.]

This indicates that the zakat of the wealthy of each people is returned to the poor of that same people.

They agreed that if it is transported from one land to another, it is discharged though disliked, and the obligation is lifted from the one liable, except what is reported from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz (may Allah be pleased with him) that he returned a charity that had been carried from Khurasan to Syria to its place in Khurasan.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 61:

﴿And among them are those who harm the Prophet and say, "He is an ear."﴾ It was revealed concerning a group of hypocrites who used to harm the Prophet ﷺ and say what was not fitting. Some of them said, "Do not do this, for we fear that what you say will reach him and befall us." Al-Jullas ibn Suwayd, one of them, said, "Rather, we will say whatever we wish, then come to him and deny what we said, and swear, and he will believe us in what we say, for Muhammad is only an ear." [Al-Wahidi, Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 286; Ibn Hisham, Sirah, 1/521.] That is, "an ear that hears." It is said: "So-and-so is an ear and an udhunah" on the pattern of fu'ulah, when he hears everything said to him and accepts it. Its root is from adhina, ya'dhanu, udhunan, meaning he listened. It was also said: "He is an udhun," meaning: possessor of a hearing ear.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: It was revealed concerning a man among the hypocrites called Nabtal ibn al-Harith. He was a man with a small, ugly face, disheveled hair, red eyes, dark-blotched cheeks, and a deformed appearance. The Prophet ﷺ had said: "Whoever wishes to look at the devil, let him look at Nabtal ibn al-Harith." He used to convey the Prophet's ﷺ words to the hypocrites. He was told, "Do not do this," and he said, "Muhammad is only an ear; whoever speaks to him, he believes him. So we say whatever we wish, then we come to him and swear by Allah, and he believes us." Then Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. [Narrated by Ibn Ishaq without a complete chain; see al-Tabari, 14/324; Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 286; al-Durr al-Manthur, 4/227.]

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: an ear of good for you.﴾ The majority read it with the genitive construction (idafah), meaning: a listener to what is good and right for you, not a listener to evil and corruption. Al-A'mash and al-Burjumi, from Abu Bakr, read ﴿an ear of good for you﴾ with both words in the nominative and with tanwin, meaning: that he hears from you and believes you is better for you than that he should deny you and not accept your word. Then He refuted them, saying: ﴿He believes in Allah﴾, that is: No, rather he believes in Allah, ﴿and believes the believers﴾, that is: he trusts the believers and accepts from them, not from the hypocrites. It is said: amintuhu and amintu lahu, with the same meaning: I believed him (sadaqtuhu).

﴿And mercy﴾: Hamzah read "wa-rahmatin" in the genitive, on the sense of "an ear of good for you and an ear of mercy." The others read "wa-rahmatun" in the nominative, meaning: he is an ear of good, and he is mercy ﴿for those of you who believe﴾, because he was the cause of the faith of the believers.

﴿And those who harm the Messenger of Allah, for them is a painful punishment.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 62–64:

﴿They swear to Allah to you in order to please you﴾. Qatadah and al-Suddi said: A group of hypocrites gathered, among them al-Jullas ibn Suwayd and Wadi'ah ibn Thabit, and they spoke ill of the Prophet (ﷺ). They said: "If what Muhammad says is true, then we are worse than donkeys." Near them was a youth from the Ansar called Amir ibn Qays, and they belittled him and spoke these words. The youth became angry and said: "By Allah, what Muhammad says is true, and you are worse than donkeys." He then went to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned them and questioned them, and they swore that Amir was a liar. Amir swore that they were liars, and the Prophet (ﷺ) believed them. Amir began to supplicate and say: "O Allah, make the truthful one truthful and the liar a liar." Then Allah the Exalted revealed this verse [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/228; Asbab al-Nuzul p. 287; al-Tabari: 14/329.]].

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning a band of hypocrites who stayed behind from the expedition of Tabuk. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned, they came to him apologising and swearing oaths. So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse: ﴿They swear to Allah to you in order to please you, but Allah and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him, if they are believers﴾.

﴿Do they not know that whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger﴾, that is, opposes Allah and His Messenger by being on one side while Allah and His Messenger are on the other, ﴿then indeed for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein. That is the great disgrace﴾, that is, the great exposure.

﴿The hypocrites fear﴾, that is, the hypocrites are apprehensive, ﴿that there will be sent down upon them﴾, that is, sent down upon the believers, ﴿a surah informing them of what is in their hearts﴾, that is, of what is in the hearts of the hypocrites of envy and enmity towards the believers. They used to speak among themselves in secret, and they feared the exposure that would come by the descent of the Qur'an concerning them.

Qatadah said: This surah is called al-Fadihah (the Exposer), al-Muba'thirah (the Disclosing), and al-Muthirah (the Stirring), for it stirred up their disgraces and their faults.

Abdullah ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Allah the Exalted revealed the mention of seventy men of the hypocrites by their names and their fathers' names, then He abrogated the mention of the names out of mercy to the believers, lest some of them reproach others, because their children were believers.

﴿Say: Mock on; indeed Allah will bring out﴾, that is, will make manifest, ﴿what you fear﴾.

Ibn Kaysan said: This verse was revealed concerning twelve men of the hypocrites who lay in wait for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the steep pass when he returned from the expedition of Tabuk, to assassinate him when he ascended it. With them was a Muslim man who concealed their intention from them. They disguised themselves against him on a dark night. Jibril informed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of what they had plotted, and commanded him to send someone to strike the faces of their mounts. Ammar ibn Yasir was leading the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) mount, and Hudhayfah was driving it behind him. He said to Hudhayfah: "Strike the faces of their mounts." So he struck them until he drove them back. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) dismounted, he said to Hudhayfah: "Whom did you recognise from the people?" He said: "I did not recognise any of them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "They were so-and-so and so-and-so," and he named them all. Hudhayfah said: "Will you not send someone to them to kill them?" He said: "I dislike that the Arabs should say, when he prevailed over his companions, he began to kill them. Rather, Allah will suffice us against them with the Dubaylah" [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/244.]].

Ismail ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us: Abd al-Ghafir ibn Isa informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan narrated to us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu Nadrah, from Qays ibn Ubad, who said: We said to Ammar: "Tell us about your fighting: is it an opinion you formed, and opinion may err and be correct, or a covenant the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made with you?" He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made no covenant with us that he did not make with all the people. And he said: 'Indeed, in my Ummah'" (Shu'bah said: "I think he said: Hudhayfah narrated to me that he said: 'in my Ummah'") "are twelve hypocrites who will not enter Paradise nor smell its fragrance until the camel passes through the eye of the needle. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 62–64:

﴿They swear to Allah to you in order to please you﴾. Qatadah and al-Suddi said: A group of hypocrites gathered, among them al-Jullas ibn Suwayd and Wadi'ah ibn Thabit, and they spoke ill of the Prophet (ﷺ). Qatadah said: This surah is called al-Fadihah (the Exposer), al-Muba'thirah (the Disclosing), and al-Muthirah (the Stirring), for it stirred up their disgraces and their faults.

Abdullah ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Allah the Exalted revealed the mention of seventy men of the hypocrites by their names and their fathers' names, then He abrogated the mention of the names out of mercy to the believers, lest some of them reproach others, because their children were believers.

Ibn Kaysan said: This verse was revealed concerning twelve men of the hypocrites who lay in wait for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the steep pass when he returned from the expedition of Tabuk, to assassinate him when he ascended it. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 65:

Allah's words: ﴿And if you ask them, they will surely say, "We were only conversing and playing around."﴾ etc. The occasion of the revelation of this verse, according to al-Kalbi, Muqatil and Qatadah, was that the Prophet (ﷺ) was traveling on the expedition of Tabuk, and before him were three hypocrites: two of them were mocking the Qur'an and the Messenger, and the third was laughing.

It was said: they used to say, "Muhammad claims that he will defeat the Romans and conquer their cities! How far-fetched that is!"

And it was said: they used to say, "Muhammad claims that a Qur'an has been revealed concerning our companions who stayed behind in Medina, but it is only his own saying and speech." So Allah informed His Prophet (ﷺ) of that, and he said, "Hold the riders back for me." He summoned them and said to them, "You said such-and-such." They replied, "We were only conversing and playing around," meaning: we were talking and engaging in speech the way travelers do to cut short the road with conversation and play.

Ibn Umar said: "I saw ʿAbdullah ibn Ubayy running in front of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while the stones were striking him, and he was saying, 'We were only conversing and playing around,' while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was saying, '﻿Was it Allah, His signs and His Messenger that you were mocking?' He paid no attention to him and did not add to it."[[Note: In both manuscripts it reads "Qala Umar." The correct reading is "Ibn Umar."]] [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari 14/333-334; Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi p. 288; al-Durr al-Manthur 4/230-231.]]

Allah's words: ﴿Say﴾, i.e., say, O Muhammad, ﴿"Was it Allah, His signs [i.e., His Book] and His Messenger that you were mocking?"﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 66:

﴿Do not make excuses; you have disbelieved after your belief.﴾ If it is asked: how does He say, "you have disbelieved after your belief," when they were not believers?

It is said: its meaning is: you manifested disbelief after you had manifested belief.

﴿If We pardon one faction of you﴾, meaning: if We forgive a faction of you. By "faction" He meant one person. ﴿We will punish another faction because they were criminals﴾, for their mockery. ʿAsim recited "naʿfu" with the nun, with a fatha on it and a damma on the fa', and "nuʿaddhib" with the nun and a kasra on the dhal, with "ṭāʾifatan" in the accusative (nuṣiba). The others recited "yuʿfa" with the ya' and a damma on it and a fatha on the fa', and "tuʿaddhab" with the ta' and a fatha on the dhal, and "ṭāʾifun" in the nominative (rufiʿa) as a passive construction (ʿalā ghayri tasmiyat al-fāʿil, i.e., the passive voice, with the subject not named).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: the one who was pardoned was a single man, Makhshiy ibn Humayyir al-Ashja'i. It is said he was the one who used to laugh and not join in the plotting, and he would walk apart from them and disapprove of some of what he heard. When this verse was revealed, he repented of his hypocrisy and said: "O Allah, I keep hearing a verse recited about which I am concerned, by which the skins shiver and the hearts pound [[wajiba qalbuhu yajibu wajiban: it fluttered and was agitated.]]. O Allah, make my death a killing in Your way, so that no one can say, 'We washed him, we shrouded him, we buried him.'" So he was struck down on the day of al-Yamama, and none of the Muslims was known to have been killed there except him, and his fall was recognized [[Sirat Ibn Hisham: 2/525. In it: Makhshin ibn Humayyir, and it is said: Makhshiy.]].

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 9, verses 67–72:**

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The hypocrite men and the hypocrite women are of one another﴾. That is, they follow one religion. It was also said: their affair is one, in that they unite in hypocrisy. ﴿They enjoin what is evil﴾, that is, polytheism and disobedience. ﴿And they forbid what is good﴾, that is, faith and obedience. ﴿And they close their hands﴾, that is, they withhold them from charity and spending in the way of Allah, and they do not extend them with good. ﴿They have forgotten Allah, so He has forgotten them﴾, that is, they abandoned the obedience of Allah, so Allah abandoned them from His guidance and success in this world, and from His mercy in the Hereafter, and left them in His punishment. ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites are the defiantly disobedient﴾.

﴿Allah has promised the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women and the disbelievers the fire of Hell, wherein they will abide. It is sufficient for them. And Allah has cursed them, and for them is an enduring punishment﴾. ﴿It is sufficient for them﴾, that is, it is their adequate recompense for their disbelief. ﴿And Allah has cursed them﴾, that is, He has removed them far from His mercy. ﴿And for them is an enduring punishment﴾, that is, a lasting one.

﴿Like those before you﴾: that is, you have done the same as those before you, by deviating from the command of Allah, so you have been cursed as they were cursed. ﴿They were greater than you in strength﴾ in force and in defence, ﴿and more abundant in wealth and children, and they enjoyed their share﴾, meaning they enjoyed, or benefited from, their share (khalaq) of this world, by following their desires, and they were content with it in place of the Hereafter. ﴿So you have enjoyed your share﴾, O disbelievers and hypocrites, ﴿as those before you enjoyed their share﴾, and you have followed their path. ﴿And you have plunged﴾ into falsehood, and into lying against Allah the Exalted, and denying His messengers, and mocking the believers. ﴿As they plunged﴾, that is, as they plunged. It was also said: "as the one who plunged" means "as those who plunged". This is because "alladhi" (the one who) is a defective noun, like "ma" and "man", which is used for the singular and the plural. Its parallel is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Like the example of one who kindled a fire﴾, then He said: ﴿Allah took away their light﴾ [al-Baqarah: 17].

﴿Those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and those are the losers﴾. That is, just as their deeds became worthless and they lost, so too your deeds have become worthless and you have lost.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz informed us: Abu Umar al-San'ani from Yemen informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "You will certainly follow the ways of those before you, span by span and cubit by cubit, to the extent that if they entered the hole of a lizard, you would follow them." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, the Jews and the Christians?" He said: "Who else?" In a narration of Abu Hurayrah: "Are the people anyone other than them?" And Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "You are the nations most similar to the Children of Israel in manner and conduct; you follow their deeds exactly, step by step, but I do not know whether you will worship the calf or not." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-I'tisam, chapter on the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "You will certainly follow the ways of those who were before you…" 13/300, and Muslim in al-'Ilm, chapter on following the ways of the Jews and Christians, no. (2669): 4/2054, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/392.]

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Has there not come to them the news﴾, meaning the hypocrites, ﴿of those before them﴾, ﴿the news﴾ being information, ﴿of those before them when they disobeyed Our messengers and opposed Our command, how We punished and destroyed them?﴾ Then He mentioned them, saying: ﴿The people of Noah﴾, who were destroyed by the flood; ﴿and 'Ad﴾, who were destroyed by the wind; ﴿and Thamud﴾, by the earthquake; ﴿and the people of Abraham﴾, by the removal of blessings and the destruction of Nimrod; ﴿and the companions of Madyan﴾, meaning the people of Shu'ayb, who were destroyed by the punishment of the Day of the Cloud; ﴿and the overturned cities﴾, the cities that were turned over, whose highest parts We made their lowest, and they were the people of Lot. ﴿Their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾, so they denied them and disobeyed them, as you have done, O company of disbelievers, so beware of hastening the retribution. ﴿Allah would not have wronged them, but they were wronging themselves﴾.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The believing men and the believing women are allies of one another﴾, in religion, in unity of word, in support and in aid.

﴿They enjoin what is good﴾, that is, faith, obedience and goodness, ﴿and forbid what is evil﴾, that is, polytheism, disobedience and whatever is not recognised in the Sharia. ﴿They establish prayer﴾, the obligatory prayer, ﴿and give zakat, and obey Allah and His Messenger. Those – Allah will have mercy upon them. Indeed, Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾.

﴿Allah has promised the believing men and the believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide, and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence﴾, meaning pleasant residences. ﴿In gardens of Eden﴾, that is, gardens of eternity and permanence. It is said: "adana bi-l-makan" means he settled in the place.

Ibn Mas'ud said: It is the central part of Paradise, that is, its middle.

Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As said: In Paradise there is a palace called "Adn", around which are towers and meadows. It has five thousand doors, and no one enters it except a prophet, a truthful one (siddiq), or a martyr.

Al-Hasan said: It is a palace of gold, which no one enters except a prophet, a truthful one, a martyr, or a just judge.

Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib said: "Adn" is a river in Paradise, [its gardens] on both its banks.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: "Adn" is the highest rank in Paradise. In it is the spring of Tasnim, and the gardens surround it, encircling it. It has been covered since the time Allah created it until its people, the prophets, the truthful ones, the martyrs and the righteous, and whomever Allah wills, enter it. In it are palaces of pearls, rubies and gold. A pleasant wind blows from beneath the Throne and enters upon them with heaps of white, pure musk.

﴿And the pleasure of Allah is greater﴾, that is, Allah's pleasure with them is greater than all of that. ﴿That is the great attainment﴾. We have related from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to the people of Paradise: 'O people of Paradise, are you pleased?' They say: 'Our Lord, and why would we not be pleased, when You have given us what You have not given anyone of Your creation?' He says: 'Shall I not give you something better than that?' They say: 'Our Lord, and what is better than that?' He says: 'I shall make My pleasure descend upon you, and I shall never be angry with you after it, ever.'" [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Tawhid, chapter on the speech of the Lord with the people of Paradise: 13/487, and also in al-Riqaq; and Muslim in al-Jannah, chapter on the descent of pleasure upon the people of Paradise, no. (2829): 4/2176; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/231–232.]

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz informed us: Abu Umar al-San'ani from Yemen informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "You will certainly follow the ways of those before you, span by span and cubit by cubit, to the extent that if they entered the hole of a lizard, you would follow them." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, the Jews and the Christians?" He said: "Who else?" In a narration of Abu Hurayrah: "Are the people anyone other than them?" And Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "You are the nations most similar to the Children of Israel in manner and conduct; you follow their deeds exactly, step by step, but I do not know whether you will worship the calf or not." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-I'tisam, chapter on the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "You will certainly follow the ways of those who were before you…" 13/300, and Muslim in al-'Ilm, chapter on following the ways of the Jews and Christians, no. (2669): 4/2054, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/392.]

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Has there not come to them the news﴾, meaning the hypocrites, ﴿of those before them﴾, ﴿the news﴾ being information, ﴿of those before them when they disobeyed Our messengers and opposed Our command, how We punished and destroyed them?﴾ Then He mentioned them, saying: ﴿The people of Noah﴾, who were destroyed by the flood; ﴿and 'Ad﴾, who were destroyed by the wind; ﴿and Thamud﴾, by the earthquake; ﴿and the people of Abraham﴾, by the removal of blessings and the destruction of Nimrod; ﴿and the companions of Madyan﴾, meaning the people of Shu'ayb, who were destroyed by the punishment of the Day of the Cloud; ﴿and the overturned cities﴾, the cities that were turned over, whose highest parts We made their lowest, and they were the people of Lot. ﴿Their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾, so they denied them and disobeyed them, as you have done, O company of disbelievers, so beware of hastening the retribution. ﴿Allah would not have wronged them, but they were wronging themselves﴾.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The believing men and the believing women are allies of one another﴾, in religion, in unity of word, in support and in aid.

﴿They enjoin what is good﴾, that is, faith, obedience and goodness, ﴿and forbid what is evil﴾, that is, polytheism, disobedience and whatever is not recognised in the Sharia. ﴿They establish prayer﴾, the obligatory prayer, ﴿and give zakat, and obey Allah and His Messenger. Those – Allah will have mercy upon them. Indeed, Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾.

﴿Allah has promised the believing men and the believing women gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide, and pleasant dwellings in gardens of perpetual residence﴾, meaning pleasant residences. ﴿In gardens of Eden﴾, that is, gardens of eternity and permanence. It is said: "adana bi-l-makan" means he settled in the place.

Ibn Mas'ud said: It is the central part of Paradise, that is, its middle.

Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As said: In Paradise there is a palace called "Adn", around which are towers and meadows. It has five thousand doors, and no one enters it except a prophet, a truthful one (siddiq), or a martyr.

Al-Hasan said: It is a palace of gold, which no one enters except a prophet, a truthful one, a martyr, or a just judge.

Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib said: "Adn" is a river in Paradise, [its gardens] on both its banks.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: "Adn" is the highest rank in Paradise. In it is the spring of Tasnim, and the gardens surround it, encircling it. It has been covered since the time Allah created it until its people, the prophets, the truthful ones, the martyrs and the righteous, and whomever Allah wills, enter it. In it are palaces of pearls, rubies and gold. A pleasant wind blows from beneath the Throne and enters upon them with heaps of white, pure musk.

﴿And the pleasure of Allah is greater﴾, that is, Allah's pleasure with them is greater than all of that. ﴿That is the great attainment﴾. We have related from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to the people of Paradise: 'O people of Paradise, are you pleased?' They say: 'Our Lord, and why would we not be pleased, when You have given us what You have not given anyone of Your creation?' He says: 'Shall I not give you something better than that?' They say: 'Our Lord, and what is better than that?' He says: 'I shall make My pleasure descend upon you, and I shall never be angry with you after it, ever.'" [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Tawhid, chapter on the speech of the Lord with the people of Paradise: 13/487, and also in al-Riqaq; and Muslim in al-Jannah, chapter on the descent of pleasure upon the people of Paradise, no. (2829): 4/2176; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/231–232.]

"O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers" with the sword and killing, "and the hypocrites." They differed concerning the manner of striving against the hypocrites. Ibn Mas'ud said: with the hand, and if he cannot, then with the tongue, and if he cannot, then with the heart. And he said: "Meet the hypocrites only with a frowning face" [[Narrated by al-Tabari from Ibn Mas'ud: 14/358. "Frowning face" (wajh mukfahirr): a face that is stern and withdrawn, with no cheerfulness, no brightness and no openness.]]. Ibn 'Abbas said: with the tongue, and by abandoning gentleness. Al-Dahhak said: by harshness of speech. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: by carrying out the prescribed punishments upon them.

"And be harsh with them. Their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination" in the Hereafter. 'Ata' said: this verse abrogated (naskh) everything of pardon and forgiveness.

"They swear by Allah that they did not say..." Ibn 'Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting in the shade of a room, and he said: "A man will come to you who looks at you with the eyes of a devil; when he comes, do not speak to him." Not long after, a blue-eyed man appeared, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called him and said: "Why do you and your companions revile me?" The man went off and brought his companions, and they swore by Allah that they had not said it. So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed this verse [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 14/363; Shaykh Shakir authenticated its chain. al-Suyuti attributed it additionally to al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh. al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/241.]].

Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning al-Jullas ibn Suwayd. The reason was that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave a sermon one day at Tabuk, mentioning the hypocrites, calling them filth and denouncing them. Al-Jullas said: "If Muhammad is truthful, then we are worse than donkeys." 'Amir ibn Qays heard him and said: "Indeed, Muhammad is truthful, and you are worse than donkeys." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned to Madinah, 'Amir ibn Qays came to him and informed him of what al-Jullas had said. Al-Jullas said: "He lied about me, O Messenger of Allah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered them both to swear beside the pulpit. After 'Asr, al-Jullas stood by the pulpit and swore by Allah, besides whom there is no god, that he had not said it, and that 'Amir had lied about him. Then 'Amir stood and swore by Allah, besides whom there is no god, that he had indeed said it and had not lied about him. Then he raised his hands to the sky and said: "O Allah, send down to Your Prophet the confirmation of the truthful one among us." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers said: "Amen." Before they separated, Jibril (peace be upon him) descended with this verse, until he reached: "So if they repent, it is better for them." Al-Jullas stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I hear that Allah, mighty and majestic, has offered me repentance. 'Amir ibn Qays has spoken the truth in what he said; I said it, and I seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) accepted that from him, and his repentance was made good.

"And they have indeed uttered the word of disbelief and disbelieved after their Islam" — that is, they openly displayed disbelief after openly displaying faith and Islam. It was said: it is cursing the Prophet (ﷺ). It was said: the word of disbelief is the statement of al-Jullas: "If Muhammad is truthful, then we are worse than donkeys." It was also said: the word of disbelief is their saying, "If we return to Madinah, the mightier will surely expel the meaner from it" [al-Munafiqun: 8]; and that story will come in its place in Surat al-Munafiqun. "And they resolved upon what they did not attain." Mujahid said: the hypocrites resolved to kill the Muslim who heard their saying, "We are worse than donkeys," so that he would not spread it.

It was also said: they were twelve men from among the hypocrites who stood at the mountain pass on the road to Tabuk to assassinate the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Jibril (peace be upon him) came and commanded him to send someone to them who would strike the faces of their mounts, so he sent Hudhayfah for that purpose.

Al-Suddi said: They said, "When we reach Madinah, we will place a crown on the head of 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy," but they did not reach it.

"And they found fault" — they disliked and disapproved of and denied them, "except that Allah and His Messenger enriched them from His bounty." This was because the client (mawla) of al-Jullas was killed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered his blood-money of twelve thousand dirhams to be paid, and so he became rich. Al-Kalbi said: Before the arrival of the Prophet (ﷺ) they were in hardship of livelihood; when the Prophet (ﷺ) came to them, they became rich through the spoils of war.

"So if they repent" from their hypocrisy and disbelief, "it will be better for them; but if they turn away," turning away from faith, "Allah will punish them with a painful punishment in this world" with humiliation, "and in the Hereafter" — that is, in the Hereafter, with the Fire. "And they will have no protector or helper on earth."

"O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers" with the sword and killing, "and the hypocrites." They differed concerning the manner of striving against the hypocrites. Ibn Mas'ud said: with the hand, and if he cannot, then with the tongue, and if he cannot, then with the heart. And he said: "Meet the hypocrites only with a frowning face" [[Narrated by al-Tabari from Ibn Mas'ud: 14/358. "Frowning face" (wajh mukfahirr): a face that is stern and withdrawn, with no cheerfulness, no brightness and no openness.]]. Ibn 'Abbas said: with the tongue, and by abandoning gentleness. Al-Dahhak said: by harshness of speech. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: by carrying out the prescribed punishments upon them.

"And be harsh with them. Their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination" in the Hereafter. 'Ata' said: this verse abrogated (naskh) everything of pardon and forgiveness.

"They swear by Allah that they did not say..." Not long after, a blue-eyed man appeared, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called him and said: "Why do you and your companions revile me?" The man went off and brought his companions, and they swore by Allah that they had not said it. So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed this verse [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 14/363; Shaykh Shakir authenticated its chain. al-Suyuti attributed it additionally to al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn Mardawayh. al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/241.]].
