"And they will have no protector or helper on earth."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 75:

The Most High said: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity"﴾ – the verse. Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us; Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi related to us; Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Asfahani informed us; Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Samarqandi related to us; Muhammad ibn Nasr related to us; Abu al-Azhar Ahmad ibn al-Azhar related to me; Marwan ibn Muhammad ibn Sho'ayb related to us; Mu'an [[In "A" (Mu'adh), with a dhal.]] ibn Rifa'ah related to us, from 'Ali ibn Yazid [[In the original: (Zayd), which is an error.]], from al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Umamah al-Bahili, who said: Tha'labah ibn Hatib al-Ansari came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, invoke Allah to grant me wealth." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Woe to you, O Tha'labah! A little that you can give thanks for is better than a lot that you cannot bear." Then he came to him again after that and said: "O Messenger of Allah, invoke Allah to grant me wealth." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you not have in the Messenger of Allah a good example? By Him in whose hand my soul is, if I wished that mountains would move with me as gold and silver, they would have moved." Then he came to him again after that and said: "O Messenger of Allah, invoke Allah to grant me wealth. By Him who sent you with the truth, if Allah grants me wealth, I will surely give to every one with a right his right." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, grant Tha'labah wealth."

He said: So he acquired sheep, and they multiplied as worms multiply. The city became too cramped for him, so he withdrew from it and settled in one of its valleys, and they kept multiplying like worms. He used to pray Dhuhr and 'Asr with the Prophet (ﷺ), and he prayed the rest of the prayers with his sheep. Then they increased and multiplied until he was far from the city, so he attended only Friday prayer. Then they increased and multiplied again, and he moved further away, until he attended neither Friday prayer nor congregational prayer. Whenever it was Friday, he would go out to meet people and ask them about the news. One day the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned him and said: "What has Tha'labah done?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, Tha'labah has acquired sheep that no valley can contain." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Woe to Tha'labah! Woe to Tha'labah! Woe to Tha'labah!" Then Allah revealed the verse of the sadaqat (obligatory charities), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a man from Banu Sulaym and a man from Juhaynah, and wrote for them the ages of the sadaqah (the prescribed ages of camels for zakat) and how they should take it. He said to them: "Go to Tha'labah ibn Hatib, and [so-and-so], a man from Banu Sulaym, and take their sadaqat." So the two of them set out until they came to Tha'labah, asked him for the sadaqah, and read to him the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: "This is nothing but jizyah (poll tax); this is nothing but a sister of the jizyah. Go on until you finish, then return to me." So they departed. The Sulami heard of them, looked at the best-aged camels he had, set them aside for the sadaqah, and then went out to meet them with them. When they saw them, they said: "This is not required of you." He said: "Take it, for my soul is content with that." So they passed by the people and took the sadaqat, then returned to Tha'labah. He said: "Show me your letter," and he read it, then said: "This is nothing but a sister of the jizyah. Go away until I see my opinion."

He said: They came back, and when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw them before they spoke to him, he said: "Woe to Tha'labah! Woe to Tha'labah!" Then he prayed good for the Sulami. They informed him of what Tha'labah had done, and Allah the Most High revealed concerning him: ﴿And among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity"﴾ – the verse, up to His saying: ﴿and because they used to lie﴾. A man from among the relatives of Tha'labah was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), heard that, went out until he reached him, and said: "Woe to you, O Tha'labah! Allah has revealed about you such and such." So Tha'labah went out until he came to the Prophet (ﷺ), asked him to accept his sadaqah, and he said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has forbidden me to accept your sadaqah." So he began throwing dust on his head. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is your deed; I commanded you, but you did not obey me." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) refused to accept his sadaqah, he returned to his home. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed away. Then he came to Abu Bakr and said: "Accept my sadaqah." Abu Bakr said: "Since the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not accept it from you, why should I accept it?" So Abu Bakr died without accepting it. When 'Umar became caliph, he came to him and said: "Accept my sadaqah." He said: "The Messenger of Allah did not accept it from you, nor did Abu Bakr. Shall I accept it from you?" So he did not accept it. When 'Uthman became caliph, he came to him, but he did not accept it from him, and Tha'labah died during the caliphate of 'Uthman [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 14/370–372; al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, pp. 290–292; and Ibn al-Athir in Usd al-Ghabah: 1/284–285, where he pointed out that it is narrated through Ibn Mandah, Abu Nu'aym and Ibn 'Abd al-Barr in al-Isti'ab 10/210. Al-Haythami attributed it to al-Tabarani and said: "In it is 'Ali ibn Yazid al-Alhani, who is abandoned (matruk)." Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr: 4/246, and al-Haythami in al-Majma': 7/21, to al-Hasan ibn Sufyan, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu al-Shaykh, al-'Askari in al-Amthal, Ibn Mardawayh, Abu Nu'aym in Ma'rifat al-Sahabah, and Ibn 'Asakir. Ma'an ibn Rifa'ah al-Sulami: weak in narration; 'Ali ibn Yazid: utterly weak. So the report is weak. Ibn Hajar said of it: "This isnad is very weak." Shaykh Mahmud Shakir said: "It is weak in every respect; it has no corroborating report from another source, and some of its narrators are severely weak." As for whether the verse refers to Tha'labah ibn Hatib, there is room for examination, for he was one of the people of Badr. It is established that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "No one who witnessed Badr and Hudaybiyah will enter the Fire," and he (ﷺ) related from his Lord, blessed and exalted, that He said to the people of Badr: "Do what you wish, for I have forgiven you." How could one of such standing be followed by hypocrisy in his heart, and have such verses revealed about him? Tha'labah ibn Hatib, may Allah be pleased with him, who witnessed Badr, was killed in the Battle of Uhud, whereas this narration says he died during the reign of 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him. Thus it is confirmed that he is not the Badri Tha'labah ibn Hatib. See: al-Kafi al-Shafi, p. 77; al-Isabah: 1/401; al-Hawi lil-Fatawa: 2/183.]].

Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Qatadah said: Tha'labah came to a gathering of the Ansar and called them to witness: "If Allah grants me of His bounty, I will give to every one with a right his right, I will give charity from it, maintain the ties of kinship, and show kindness to my relatives." Then a paternal cousin of his died and left him wealth, but he did not fulfill what he had said. So Allah the Most High revealed this verse [[See: al-Tabari: 14/373–374; al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/247.]].

Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: It was revealed concerning Tha'labah ibn Hatib and Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, both from Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf. They went out before a seated assembly and said: "By Allah, if Allah grants us wealth, we will surely give charity." When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, granted them wealth, they became stingy with it [[al-Tabari: 14/374–375.]]. So His saying, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿And among them﴾ means: the hypocrites, ﴿are those who made a covenant with Allah: "If He gives us of His bounty, we will surely give charity"﴾ and we will surely pay Allah's right from it.

﴿And we will surely be among the righteous﴾ – we will act by the deeds of the people of righteousness in it, such as maintaining the ties of kinship and spending for good causes.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 76–79:

"فَلَمَّا آتَاهُمْ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ بَخِلُوا بِهِ وَتَوَلَّوْا وَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ" ("But when He gave them of His bounty, they became miserly with it and turned away while they were averse.")

﴿فَأَعْقَبَهُم﴾ ("So He caused them to follow") means ﴿فَأَخَلَفَهُمْ﴾ ("He made them to fail/break faith"). ﴿نِفَاقًا فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ ("hypocrisy in their hearts") means that the outcome of their affair was hypocrisy. It is said: "A'qaba fulanan nadamatan" when the outcome of his affair becomes that (regret). It was also said: "'Aqabahum bi-nifaqi qulubihim" ("He recompensed them with the hypocrisy of their hearts"). It is said: "'Aqabtuhu" and "A'qabtuhu" with the same meaning.

﴿إِلَى يَوْمِ يَلْقَوْنَهُ﴾ ("until the day they meet Him") means He deprived them of repentance until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿بِمَا أَخْلَفُوا اللَّهَ مَا وَعَدُوهُ وَبِمَا كَانُوا يَكْذِبُونَ﴾ ("because they broke with Allah what they had promised Him, and because they used to lie").

Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Kharaqi informed us: Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah al-Taysafuni narrated to us: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar al-Jawhari narrated to us: Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Kushmihani narrated to us: 'Ali ibn Hajar narrated to us: Isma'il ibn Ja'far informed us: Abu Suhayl Nafi' ibn Malik informed us, from his father, from Abu Hurayra, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The sign of the hypocrite is three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when he is entrusted he betrays." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Iman, chapter "Signs of the Hypocrite": 1/89, and by Muslim in al-Iman, chapter "Characteristics of the Hypocrite," no. (59): 1/78. The author (al-Baghawi) also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/72.]]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ سِرَّهُمْ وَنَجْوَاهُمْ﴾ ("Did they not know that Allah knows their secret and their private conversation?") means what they conceal in their hearts and what they confide to one another. ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ﴾ ("and that Allah is the Knower of the unseen").

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَلْمِزُونَ الْمُطَّوِّعِينَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فِي الصَّدَقَاتِ﴾ ("Those who criticize the volunteers among the believers concerning the charities") – the verse.

The exegetes (ahl al-tafsir) said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) urged giving in charity, so 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf came with four thousand dirhams and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I had eight thousand. I have brought you four thousand, so place it in the way of Allah, and I have kept four thousand for my dependants." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah bless you in what you gave and in what you kept." So Allah blessed his wealth, to the extent that when he died he left two wives, and an eighth of his wealth came to them, amounting to one hundred and sixty thousand dirhams. On that day 'Asim ibn 'Adi al-'Ajlani also gave in charity one hundred wasq of dates. Abu 'Aqil al-Ansari, whose name was al-Habbab, came with one sa' of dates and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I spent my night drawing water with a rope until I earned two sa's of dates. I kept one for my family and brought you the other." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered him to scatter it into the charity. The hypocrites then criticized them, saying: "'Abd al-Rahman and 'Asim gave only for show, and Allah and His Messenger are certainly not in need of Abu 'Aqil's sa'. He only wanted to make himself known so that he would be given from the charity." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: [[See al-Tabari: 14/383–388; al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/249–250.]]

Al-Qutaybi said: al-juhd with a ḍamma means capacity, and with a fatḥa means hardship.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 76–79:

"فَلَمَّا آتَاهُمْ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ بَخِلُوا بِهِ وَتَوَلَّوْا وَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ" ("But when He gave them of His bounty, they became miserly with it and turned away while they were averse.")

﴿فَأَعْقَبَهُم﴾ ("So He caused them to follow") means ﴿فَأَخَلَفَهُمْ﴾ ("He made them to fail/break faith"). ﴿نِفَاقًا فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ ("hypocrisy in their hearts") means that the outcome of their affair was hypocrisy. It is said: "A'qaba fulanan nadamatan" when the outcome of his affair becomes that (regret). ﴿إِلَى يَوْمِ يَلْقَوْنَهُ﴾ ("until the day they meet Him") means He deprived them of repentance until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿بِمَا أَخْلَفُوا اللَّهَ مَا وَعَدُوهُ وَبِمَا كَانُوا يَكْذِبُونَ﴾ ("because they broke with Allah what they had promised Him, and because they used to lie").

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 80–83:

﴿Ask forgiveness for them, or do not ask forgiveness for them﴾. Its wording is an imperative, but its meaning is a statement. Its implied sense is: whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them, ﴿Allah will never forgive them﴾.

﴿If you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will never forgive them﴾. The mention of the number seventy is for emphasis in despair of forgiveness, though there was hope for it.

Al-Dahhak said: When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has given me permission, so I will surely add to the seventy, perhaps Allah will forgive them." Then Allah revealed to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them﴾ [[al-Tabari: 14/395; al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/253.]].

﴿That is because they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people﴾.

﴿Those who were left behind rejoiced﴾ at staying behind from the expedition of Tabuk. The word al-mukhallaf (those left behind) means those who were left behind. ﴿In their seat﴾, i.e., by their sitting [at home], ﴿contrary to the Messenger of Allah﴾. Abu 'Ubaydah said: i.e., after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It was also said: it was opposition to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he set out and they remained behind. ﴿And they disliked striving with their wealth and their lives in the way of Allah, and they said: "Do not go forth in the heat."﴾ The expedition of Tabuk took place in intense heat. ﴿Say: "The Fire of Hell is more intense in heat, if only they understood."﴾ — i.e., if only they knew. Thus it is also in the codex of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.

﴿So let them laugh a little﴾ in this world, ﴿and let them weep much﴾ in the Hereafter. Its implied sense is: so let them laugh a little, for they will weep much, ﴿as a recompense for what they used to earn﴾.

Al-Imam Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us: al-Sayyid Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-'Alawi informed us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Husayn al-Sharqi informed us, 'Abdullah ibn Hashim narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us from Musa ibn Anas, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with them, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much." [[Recorded by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, chapter on the saying of the Exalted: "Do not ask about things which, if made apparent to you, would distress you": 8/280; Muslim in Fada'il, chapter on his honour (ﷺ), no. (2359): 4/1832; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/368-369.]].

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Tawbah informed us, Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Harith narrated to us, [Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn] [[What is between the brackets is missing from "A".]] Ya'qub al-Kisai narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Mahmud narrated to us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn 'Abdullah al-Khallal narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us from Imran ibn Zayd al-Ta'labi, Yazid al-Raqashi narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "O people, weep. If you cannot, then feign weeping, for the people of the Fire weep in the Fire until their tears flow down their faces like streams; then the tears cease and blood flows, so the eyes become sore. If ships were sailed in it, they would sail."* [[Al-Haythami said: Abu Ya'la narrated it, and Yazid al-Raqashi is among its weakest narrators, though he has been deemed trustworthy despite his weakness. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 84–90:

﴿And do not pray over any of them who has died, ever, nor stand at his grave﴾ — the (remainder of the) verse. The people of tafsir said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul sent (a message) to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was ill. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon him, he said to him: "Has the love of the Jews destroyed you?" He replied: "O Messenger of Allah, I did not send for you so that you would reproach me. I only sent for you so that you would ask forgiveness for me." He also asked him to shroud him in his shirt and to pray over him.

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who said: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us, who said: al-Layth related to me, from ʿUqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with them), that he said: When ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul died, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was summoned to pray over him. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, I leapt toward him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, will you pray over Ibn Ubayy ibn Salul when he said on such and such a day such and such?" I enumerated his statement to him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) smiled and said: "Step back from me, O ʿUmar." When I persisted against him, he said: "I was given a choice and I chose. If I knew that if I added beyond seventy he would be forgiven, I would add beyond them." He said: So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed over him, then departed, and did not remain but a little until the two verses of Bara'a were revealed: ﴿And do not pray over any of them who has died, ever, nor stand at his grave﴾ up to his saying: ﴿and they are defiantly disobedient﴾. He said: Afterwards I was amazed at my boldness toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that day, and Allah and His Messenger know best.

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi, who said: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf reported to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, who said: ʿAli ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, who said: Sufyan narrated to us. ʿAmr said: I heard Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy after he had been placed in his grave, so he commanded that he be brought out. He placed him on his knees, blew into his mouth from his saliva, and dressed him in his shirt. So Allah knows best. And he had clothed ʿAbbas in a shirt.

Sufyan said: Harun said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had two shirts. Ibn ʿAbd Allah said: O Messenger of Allah, dress my father in your shirt that is next to your skin.

It is narrated from Jabir, who said: When the Day of Badr came, al-ʿAbbas was brought in and he had no garment on him. They found the shirt of ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy fitting him, so the Prophet (ﷺ) clothed him in it. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) removed his shirt that he had put on ʿAbd Allah. Ibn ʿUyayna said: He had a favour (yad) with the Prophet (ﷺ), so he wanted to repay him.

It is narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) was addressed about what he had done for ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, and he (ﷺ) said: "What does my shirt and my prayer avail him before Allah at all? By Allah, I used to hope that a thousand of his people would become Muslim by it." And it is narrated that a thousand of his people did become Muslim because of it, when they saw him seeking blessing through the shirt of the Prophet (ﷺ).

His saying: ﴿And do not pray over any of them who has died, ever, nor stand at his grave﴾ — and do not stand over him, nor take charge of his burial; from the expression: "So-and-so stood up to the matter of so-and-so," meaning when he takes care of his affair for him.

﴿Indeed they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and died while they were defiantly disobedient﴾. So the Prophet (ﷺ) never afterwards prayed over a hypocrite, nor stood at his grave, until he was taken (in death).

His exalted saying: ﴿And do not let their wealth or their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them through them in this world, and that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers﴾.

﴿And when a surah is sent down (saying): Believe in Allah and strive along with His Messenger, those of wealth among them ask your leave, and say: Leave us, that we may be with those who sit (at home)﴾ — those of wealth and ease among them, (who remained) in sitting (at home). ﴿And they said: Leave us, we will be with those who remain behind﴾ in their dwellings.

﴿They are content to be with the women who stay behind (khawalif)﴾ — meaning the women. It was also said: with the lowly and base of the people. It is said: "So-and-so is the khalifa of his people" when he is beneath them.

﴿And a seal is set upon their hearts, so they do not understand﴾.

﴿But the Messenger and those who believed with him strove with their wealth and their selves; for them are the good things (al-khayrat)﴾ — meaning the good deeds. It was also said: the beautiful maidens in Paradise. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Therein are good (khayrat) and beautiful (women)﴾, the plural of khayra. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas that the meaning of al-khayr is known only to Allah, as the Exalted One said: "No soul knows what is hidden for them of the comfort of the eyes" [al-Sajda: 17].

﴿And those are the successful﴾.

His exalted saying: ﴿And those who make excuses among the Bedouins came seeking permission﴾ — the verse. Ya'qub and Mujahid read ﴿al-Mu'dhirun﴾ with a light pronunciation, meaning those who go to extremes in making excuses. It is said in the proverb: "He who warns has indeed given excuse," i.e., he who gives warning has made his excuse thoroughly. The others read "al-Mu'ajjirun"/"al-Mu'ʿadhdhirun" with emphasis, meaning those who fall short; it is said ʿadhdhara, meaning he fell short. Al-Farra' said: al-Mu'adhdhirun are al-Mu'tadhirun, the tāʾ being assimilated into the dhāl and the vowel of the tāʾ transferred to the ʿayn.

Al-Dahhak said: al-Mu'adhdhirun were the kin of ʿAmir ibn al-Tufayl, who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) defending themselves, and said: "O Prophet of Allah, if we go out with you, the Tayy Bedouins will raid our wives, our children and our livestock." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Allah has informed me of your news, and Allah will suffice us from you."

Ibn ʿAbbas said: They are those who stayed behind with an excuse, by the permission of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

﴿And those who lied to Allah and His Messenger sat (at home)﴾ — meaning the hypocrites.

Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAla' said: Both groups were blameworthy: a people who fabricated excuses falsely, and they are those whom Allah the Exalted meant by His saying: ﴿And the excuse-makers came﴾; and a people who stayed behind without fabricating any excuse, sitting out of boldness toward Allah the Exalted, and they are the hypocrites, whom Allah threatened with His saying: ﴿A painful punishment will befall those of them who disbelieved﴾.

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who said: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, who said: Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us, who said: al-Layth related to me, from ʿUqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with them), that he said: When ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul died, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was summoned to pray over him. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, I leapt toward him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, will you pray over Ibn Ubayy ibn Salul when he said on such and such a day such and such?" I enumerated his statement to him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) smiled and said: "Step back from me, O ʿUmar." When I persisted against him, he said: "I was given a choice and I chose. If I knew that if I added beyond seventy he would be forgiven, I would add beyond them." He said: So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed over him, then departed, and did not remain but a little until the two verses of Bara'a were revealed: ﴿And do not pray over any of them who has died, ever, nor stand at his grave﴾ up to his saying: ﴿and they are defiantly disobedient﴾. He said: Afterwards I was amazed at my boldness toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that day, and Allah and His Messenger know best.

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi, who said: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf reported to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, who said: ʿAli ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, who said: Sufyan narrated to us. ʿAmr said: I heard Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy after he had been placed in his grave, so he commanded that he be brought out. He placed him on his knees, blew into his mouth from his saliva, and dressed him in his shirt. So Allah knows best. And he had clothed ʿAbbas in a shirt.

Sufyan said: Harun said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had two shirts. Ibn ʿAbd Allah said: O Messenger of Allah, dress my father in your shirt that is next to your skin.

It is narrated from Jabir, who said: When the Day of Badr came, al-ʿAbbas was brought in and he had no garment on him. They found the shirt of ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy fitting him, so the Prophet (ﷺ) clothed him in it. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) removed his shirt that he had put on ʿAbd Allah. Ibn ʿUyayna said: He had a favour (yad) with the Prophet (ﷺ), so he wanted to repay him.

It is narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) was addressed about what he had done for ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, and he (ﷺ) said: "What does my shirt and my prayer avail him before Allah at all? By Allah, I used to hope that a thousand of his people would become Muslim by it." And it is narrated that a thousand of his people did become Muslim because of it, when they saw him seeking blessing through the shirt of the Prophet (ﷺ).

His saying: ﴿And do not pray over any of them who has died, ever, nor stand at his grave﴾ — and do not stand over him, nor take charge of his burial; from the expression: "So-and-so stood up to the matter of so-and-so," meaning when he takes care of his affair for him.

﴿Indeed they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and died while they were defiantly disobedient﴾. So the Prophet (ﷺ) never afterwards prayed over a hypocrite, nor stood at his grave, until he was taken (in death).

His exalted saying: ﴿And do not let their wealth or their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them through them in this world, and that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers﴾.

﴿And when a surah is sent down (saying): Believe in Allah and strive along with His Messenger, those of wealth among them ask your leave, and say: Leave us, that we may be with those who sit (at home)﴾ — those of wealth and ease among them, (who remained) in sitting (at home). ﴿And they said: Leave us, we will be with those who remain behind﴾ in their dwellings.

﴿They are content to be with the women who stay behind (khawalif)﴾ — meaning the women. It was also said: with the lowly and base of the people. It is said: "So-and-so is the khalifa of his people" when he is beneath them.

﴿And a seal is set upon their hearts, so they do not understand﴾.

﴿But the Messenger and those who believed with him strove with their wealth and their selves; for them are the good things (al-khayrat)﴾ — meaning the good deeds. It was also said: the beautiful maidens in Paradise. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Therein are good (khayrat) and beautiful (women)﴾, the plural of khayra. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas that the meaning of al-khayr is known only to Allah, as the Exalted One said: "No soul knows what is hidden for them of the comfort of the eyes" [al-Sajda: 17].

﴿And those are the successful﴾.

His exalted saying: ﴿And those who make excuses among the Bedouins came seeking permission﴾ — the verse. Ya'qub and Mujahid read ﴿al-Mu'dhirun﴾ with a light pronunciation, meaning those who go to extremes in making excuses. It is said in the proverb: "He who warns has indeed given excuse," i.e., he who gives warning has made his excuse thoroughly. The others read "al-Mu'ajjirun"/"al-Mu'ʿadhdhirun" with emphasis, meaning those who fall short; it is said ʿadhdhara, meaning he fell short. Al-Farra' said: al-Mu'adhdhirun are al-Mu'tadhirun, the tāʾ being assimilated into the dhāl and the vowel of the tāʾ transferred to the ʿayn.

Al-Dahhak said: al-Mu'adhdhirun were the kin of ʿAmir ibn al-Tufayl, who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) defending themselves, and said: "O Prophet of Allah, if we go out with you, the Tayy Bedouins will raid our wives, our children and our livestock." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Allah has informed me of your news, and Allah will suffice us from you."

Ibn ʿAbbas said: They are those who stayed behind with an excuse, by the permission of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 91–92:

Then He mentioned those who have an excuse, so He, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿There is no blame upon the weak﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: That means the chronically ill, the elderly, and the infirm. It was also said: They are the children; and it was said: the women. ﴿Nor upon the sick, nor upon those who find nothing to spend﴾, meaning the poor, ﴿there is no blame (haraj)﴾, meaning sin (ma'thum). It was also said: it means constriction in staying behind from the raid, ﴿when they are sincere toward Allah and His Messenger﴾ in their absence, and they make their faith and their deeds sincerely for Allah and pledge allegiance to the Messenger.

﴿There is no route against the good-doers﴾, that is, no path to punishment, ﴿and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Qatadah said: It was revealed concerning 'A'idh ibn 'Amr and his companions. [[See: al-Tabari: 14/420.]]

And al-Dahhak said: It was revealed concerning 'Abd Allah ibn Umm Maktum, and he was blind. [[Compare with al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/262.]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Nor upon those who, when they come to you that you might give them mounts﴾. Its meaning: there is no path (of blame) against the former ones, nor against these who came to you, and they were seven men known as "the weepers": Ma'qil ibn Yasar, Sakhr ibn Khansa', 'Abd Allah ibn Ka'b al-Ansari, 'Ulbah [[In the original: (‘Ulayyah). In the printed edition: (‘Ablah). The correction is from al-Rawd al-Anf by al-Suhayli: 2/321.]] ibn Zayd al-Ansari, Salim ibn 'Umayr, Tha'labah ibn Ghanamah [[In manuscript "A": (‘Uthmah).]], and 'Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal al-Muzani. They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, indeed Allah has called us to go out with you, so carry us." [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 14/423. See also: Sirah of Ibn Hisham: 2/518; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi p. 296; Imta' al-Asma' of al-Maqrizi: 1/448.]]

They differed concerning His saying ﴿that He might carry them﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: they asked him to carry them on beasts of burden.

It was also said: they asked him to carry them on patched leather shoes and sandals so that they could fight with him. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I do not find anything to carry you on." So they turned away while they were weeping. This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They turned away while their eyes overflowed with tears from grief that they could not find what to spend﴾.

But if you are pleased with them, indeed Allah is not pleased with the defiantly disobedient people﴾ [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 4/89-90.]].

﴿The blame [al-sabil, here: the punishment]﴾ is only ﴿against those who ask your permission﴾ to stay behind, ﴿while they are wealthy. They were content to be with the ones left behind [al-khawalif]﴾, meaning the women and the children. ﴿And Allah has sealed their hearts, so they do not know﴾.

﴿They will make excuses to you when you return to them﴾. It is related that the hypocrites who stayed behind from the expedition [ghazwa] of Tabuk numbered about eighty-some men. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned, they came making excuses based on falsehood. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say, "Do not make excuses; we will never believe you. Allah has already informed us of your news"﴾, meaning, we will not believe you. ﴿And Allah will see your deeds, and so will His Messenger﴾ in the future: will you repent of your hypocrisy, or will you persist in it? ﴿Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do﴾.

﴿They will swear by Allah to you when you return to them﴾, when you turn back to them from your military campaign, ﴿so that you may turn away from them﴾, that you may overlook them and not rebuke them. ﴿So turn away from them﴾, leave them alone and to what they have chosen for themselves of hypocrisy. ﴿Indeed, they are impure [rijs]﴾, meaning filthy; that is, their deeds are ugly. ﴿And their refuge is Hell﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿as recompense for what they used to earn﴾.

Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed concerning Jadd ibn Qays, Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, and their companions, and they were eighty men of the hypocrites. The Prophet (ﷺ), when he arrived at Madinah, said: "Do not sit with them, and do not speak with them" [[See the narration from Ibn Abbas in full in: al-Tabari: 14/426-427. The saying of the Prophet (ﷺ), "Do not sit with them ...", was attributed by al-Suyuti to Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/266.]].

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning Abd Allah ibn Ubayy, who swore to the Prophet (ﷺ) by Allah, there is no god but He, that he would never stay behind from him after that, and he asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to be pleased with him. So Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed this verse, and there was also revealed: ﴿They swear to you that you may be pleased with them. But if you are pleased with them, indeed Allah is not pleased with the defiantly disobedient people﴾ [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 4/89-90.]].

**The Bedouin Arabs** (ahl al-badw, the people of the desert) **are more intense in disbelief and hypocrisy** than the people of the settled towns, **and more likely** (ajda, more fitting and more deserving) **not to know the limits of what Allah has sent down to His Messenger**. That is because they are far from hearing the Qur'an and from knowing the sunan (the Prophetic practices and traditions). **Allah is All-Knowing** of what is in the hearts of His creatures, **All-Wise** in what He has made obligatory of His obligations.

**And among the Bedouin is one who takes what he spends as a loss (maghram).** Ata said: he does not hope for any reward for giving, nor does he fear any punishment for withholding. He spends only out of fear or for show. The maghram is taking on an obligation that is not imposed.

**And he waits (yatarabbasu) for you, for the reversals (al-dawa'ir)**, meaning the turns of time, which sometimes come with good and sometimes with evil. Yaman ibn Ri'ab said: it means that time turns against you, so the Messenger dies and the polytheists prevail. **The evil turn is upon them**: calamity and grief revolve around them, and they see nothing concerning Muhammad and his religion except what displeases them.

Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read **"dā'irat al-sū'"** here and in Surat al-Fath with a damma on the sin (al-sū'), meaning harm, calamity and what is disliked. The others read it with a fatha on the sin, as a verbal noun (masdar). It was also said that with the fatha it means apostasy and corruption, and with the damma it means harm and what is disliked.

**And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.** It was revealed concerning the Bedouin of Asad, Ghatafan and Tamim. [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 297; al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/266.]]

Then he made an exception, saying:

**And among the Bedouin is one who believes in Allah and the Last Day.** Mujahid said: they are the Banu Muqarrin of Muzaynah. Al-Kalbi said: Aslam, Ghifar and Juhaynah.

Abu Sa'id Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Tahiri informed us: my grandfather Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Bazzar informed us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Zakariyya al-Adhrifi informed us: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Dabari informed us: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Aslam, Ghifar, and some of Juhaynah and Muzaynah are better with Allah on the Day of Resurrection than Tamim, Asad ibn Khuzaymah, Hawazin and Ghatafan." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Manaqib, chapter on the mention of Aslam...: 6/543; and Muslim in Fada'il al-Sahabah, chapter on the virtues of Ghifar, no. (2521): 4/1955; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/65.]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 100:**

﴿And the foremost, the first of the Muhajirun and the Ansar﴾, and so on. Ya'qub read ﴿wal-sabiqun﴾ with the *raf'* (nominative) vowel, as a conjunction (*'atf*) on his earlier phrase "wal-sabiqun" (the foremost).

The scholars differed about the "foremost first" (al-sabiqun al-awwalun). Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Qatadah, Ibn Sirin and a group said: they are those who prayed towards both qiblahs.

'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: they are the people of Badr.

al-Sha'bi said: they are those who witnessed the Pledge of al-Ridwan (*Bay'at al-Ridwan*, the Pledge of Good Pleasure), and the Pledge of al-Ridwan took place at al-Hudaybiyah.

They differed about who was the first to believe in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) after his wife Khadijah, although they agreed that she was the first to believe in the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Some said: the first to believe and pray was 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him). This is the view of Jabir, and Mujahid and Ibn Ishaq also held it; he embraced Islam at the age of ten.

Some said: the first to believe after Khadijah was Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him). This is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and al-Sha'bi.

Some said: the first to embrace Islam was Zayd ibn Harithah. This is the view of al-Zuhri and 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali used to reconcile these views, saying: the first man to embrace Islam was Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him); among women, Khadijah; among boys, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him); and among slaves, Zayd ibn Harithah.

Ibn Ishaq said: When Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) embraced Islam, he made his Islam known, called people to Allah and to His Messenger. He was a beloved, easygoing man, the most knowledgeable of the Quraysh in their genealogies and in what had happened among them. He was a merchant of good character and kindness, and the men of his people would come to him and keep his company for many matters, because of his knowledge and his good companionship. He began to invite to Islam those of his people whom he trusted. Through him, so I have been told, there embraced Islam: 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and Talhah ibn 'Ubayd Allah. He brought them to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when they had responded to him, and they embraced Islam and prayed. These eight men were the ones who were first to embrace Islam [[See: Ibn Hisham, al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah: 1/249-252 (al-Halabi edition).]]. Then people followed one another into Islam.

As for the foremost of the Ansar, they are those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of 'Aqabah. They were six in the First 'Aqabah and seventy in the Second, and those who believed when Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr came to them to teach them the Qur'an. A great multitude embraced Islam with him, along with a group of women and children.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And the foremost, the first of the Muhajirun﴾: those who emigrated from their people and kin and left their homelands.

﴿and the Ansar﴾: that is, and from the Ansar, who are those who supported the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) against his enemies from the people of Madinah and sheltered his companions. ﴿And those who followed them in goodness﴾: it was said they are the rest of the Muhajirun and Ansar apart from the foremost first.

It was also said: they are those who followed their path in faith, emigration or support until the Day of Resurrection.

'Ata' said: they are those who mention the Muhajirun and the Ansar with mercy and supplication.

Abu Sakhr Humayd ibn Ziyad said: I went to Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and said to him: "What is your view about the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" He said: "All the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) are in Paradise, the good-doers among them and the wrongdoers among them." I said: "From where do you say this?" He said: "O man, recite the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿And the foremost, the first of the Muhajirun and the Ansar﴾," up to His saying: ﴿Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him﴾. And He said: ﴿And those who followed them in goodness﴾; He made a condition for the Followers (*tabi'un*), which is that they follow them in their good deeds and not in their bad deeds."

Abu Sakhr said: "It is as if I had never recited this verse at all" [[Attributed by al-Suyuti in al-Durr (4/272) to Abu al-Shaykh and Ibn 'Asakir.]].

We have related that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not revile my companions. By Him in whose hand is my soul, if one of you were to spend gold equal to Mount Uhud, it would not reach the *mudd* of one of them, nor even half of it" [[Related by al-Bukhari in Fada'il al-Sahabah, chapter on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) "If I were to take a close friend...": 7/21; and by Muslim in Fada'il al-Sahabah, chapter on the prohibition of reviling the Companions, no. (2541): 4/1967-1968; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 14/69.]].

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gathered them in the reward, saying: ﴿Allah is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him, and He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. Ibn Kathir read ﴿min tahtiha al-anhar﴾ (with *min*, "from beneath it"), and it is likewise in the codices of the people of Makkah. ﴿Abiding therein forever. That is the great achievement.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 101:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among those around you of the Bedouins are hypocrites﴾, and they are from Muzayna, Juhayna, Ashja', Aslam and Ghifar, whose dwellings were around Madinah. He says: among these Bedouins are hypocrites. ﴿And among the people of Madinah﴾, i.e., and among the people of Madinah, from al-Aws and al-Khazraj, there are a people who are hypocrites. ﴿They have become accustomed to hypocrisy﴾, i.e., they have been trained in hypocrisy. It is said: "So-and-so rebelled (tamarrada) against his Lord," meaning he became insolent (ʿataa), and "he persisted (marada) in his disobedience," meaning he was trained in it, remained steadfast upon it and made it a habit. From this derive al-murid (the rebellious one) and al-marid (the obstinate, insolent one). Ibn Ishaq said: they clung to it and refused anything other than it.

Ibn Zayd said: they persisted in it and did not repent.

﴿You do not know them﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿We know them. We will punish them twice﴾. They differed concerning these two punishments.

al-Kalbi and al-Suddi said: The Prophet ﷺ stood delivering a sermon on Friday and said: "Go out, O so-and-so, for you are a hypocrite. Go out, O so-and-so." He expelled some people from the mosque and exposed them; this is the first punishment. The second is the punishment of the grave. [[Narrated by al-Tabari through the narration of al-Suddi from Abu Malik from Ibn Abbas: 14/441-442. al-Haythami attributed it also to al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, and said: in its chain is al-Husayn ibn Amr ibn Muhammad al-Anqazi, who is weak. See: Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/34.]]

Mujahid said: the first is killing and captivity, and the second is the punishment of the grave. He also has another narration: they were punished with hunger twice.

Qatadah said: the first is the ad-Dubaylah (a festering abscess) in this world, and the punishment of the grave.

Ibn Zayd said: the first is the calamities in their wealth and children in this world, and the other is the punishment of the Hereafter.

From Ibn Abbas: the first is the enforcement of the prescribed punishments upon them, and the other is the punishment of the grave.

Ibn Ishaq said: it is what enters upon them of the rage at Islam and their entering into it without sincere intention, then the punishment of the grave.

It is also said: one of them is the angels striking their faces and their backs at the taking of their souls, and the other is the punishment of the grave.

It is also said: the first is the burning of their mosque, the Masjid al-Dirar, and the other is their being burned with the Fire of Hell. [[See these sayings in: al-Tabari: 14/441-445; al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/274. al-Tabari, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "The most correct of these sayings in my view is to say: Allah informed that He will punish those who have become accustomed to hypocrisy twice, and He has not given us any evidence by which we can know the nature of those two punishments. It is possible that some of what we have mentioned from those who spoke is what we were informed of. We have no knowledge of which is which. However, in His saying, exalted is He: 'Then they will be returned to a great punishment,' there is evidence that the punishment in both instances occurs before they enter the Fire. And the more likely of the two is that one of them is in the grave."]]

﴿Then they will be returned to a great punishment﴾, i.e., to the punishment of Hell, wherein they will abide forever.

"And others" — that is, from the people of Madinah, or from among the Bedouins, others [acknowledged their sins]. This does not refer to the hypocrites. ﴿Confessed﴾ means acknowledged, ﴿their sins﴾; ﴿they had mixed a righteous deed﴾, which is their acknowledgment of their sins and their repentance, ﴿and another wrong deed﴾, meaning with another wrong deed. The waw has been placed in the position of the ba', as one says: "I mixed the water and the milk," meaning "with the milk."

The wrong deed is their staying behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

The righteous deed is their remorse and their tying themselves to the pillars. It is also said: it is their military campaigns with the Prophet (ﷺ).

﴿It may be that Allah will turn to them in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ This verse was revealed concerning a people who stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the Battle of Tabuk, then they regretted that and said: "We remain in the shade with the women, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions are in jihad and hardship!" When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) drew near to Madinah, they said: "By Allah, we will bind ourselves to the pillars and not release ourselves until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the one who releases us and pardons us." So they tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned, he passed by them and saw them, and said: "Who are these?" They said: "These are the ones who stayed behind from you. They pledged to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that they would not release themselves until you release them and are pleased with them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "And I swear by Allah, I will not release them nor pardon them until I am commanded to release them. They turned away from me and stayed behind from the expedition with the Muslims!" Then Allah revealed this verse, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent to them, released them and pardoned them. When they were released, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is our wealth that kept us back from you, so give charity from it, purify us and ask forgiveness for us." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have not been commanded to take anything from your wealth," so Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity﴾, the verse [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 14/447-450; Asbab al-Nuzul pp. (297-298).]].

They differed on the number of these repentant ones. It was narrated from ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: they were ten, among them Abu Lubabah. ʿAtiyyah narrated from him that they were five, one of them being Abu Lubabah. Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Zayd ibn Aslam said: they were eight. Al-Dahhak and Qatadah said: they were seven. And they all said: one of them was Abu Lubabah [[See these reports in: al-Tabari: 14/447-450; al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/275 and following.]].

Some people said: it was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah specifically. They differed about his sin. Mujahid said: it was revealed concerning Abu Lubabah when he said to the Banu Qurayzah: "If you come down under his judgment, it is slaughter," and he pointed to his throat [[al-Tabari: 14/451-452.]].

Al-Zuhri said: it was revealed concerning his staying behind from the expedition to Tabuk, so he tied himself to a pillar and said: "By Allah, I will not free myself nor taste food or drink until I die or Allah turns to me in forgiveness!" He remained for seven days without tasting food or drink until he fell unconscious. Then Allah revealed this verse, and it was said to him: "Allah has accepted your repentance!" He said: "By Allah, I will not free myself until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is the one who frees me." The Prophet (ﷺ) came and untied him with his own hand. Then Abu Lubabah said: "O Messenger of Allah, part of my repentance is that I abandon the house of my people where I committed the sin, and that I strip myself of all my wealth as charity to Allah and to His Messenger." He said: "A third will suffice you, O Abu Lubabah" [[al-Tabari: 14/452.]].

They all said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took a third of their wealth and left two-thirds, because Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Take from their wealth﴾ and did not say: "Take their wealth." Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: these were other than the three who were left behind.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 103:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity (sadaqah) that purifies them﴾ by it from their sins, ﴿and causes them to grow by it﴾, that is, raises them from the stations of the hypocrites to the stations of the sincere. It was also said: it increases their wealth. ﴿And pray for them﴾, that is, supplicate for them and seek forgiveness for them. It was also said: it is the words of the collector [to the giver] [[Addition from the printed edition, required by the context.]] when he takes the charity from him: "May God reward you for what you have given, and bless you in what you have kept." And prayer (al-salah) in the language means supplication (al-du'a').

﴿Indeed your prayer﴾: Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "ṣalātaka" in the singular, with the "t" vowelled with a fatha here. In Surah Hud they read "aṣalātuka", and in Surah al-Mu'minun "ʿalā ṣalātihim", [all of them in the singular] [[Addition from the printed edition, required by the context.]]. Hafs agreed with them here and in Surah Hud. The others read them in the plural, and they vowel the "t" with a kasra here.

﴿A comfort for them﴾: that is, your supplication is a mercy for them. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas. It was also said: reassurance for them and tranquillity for them, that God, mighty and majestic, has accepted from them. Abu ʿUbaydah said: a steadying of their hearts.

﴿And God is Hearing, Knowing﴾.

They differed concerning whether it is obligatory for the leader (imam) to supplicate when taking the charity. Some of them said: it is obligatory. Some said: it is recommended. Some said: it is obligatory for the obligatory charity and recommended for voluntary charity. It was also said: it is obligatory upon the leader, and it is recommended for the poor person to supplicate for the giver.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il [al-Bukhari] narrated to us, Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Amr ibn Murrah, who said: I heard Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa, who was one of the companions of the tree [of the Pledge of al-Ridwan], say: When the people of the Prophet (ﷺ) brought him charity, he would say: "O God, send blessings upon them." My father came to him with his charity, and he said: "O God, send blessings upon the family of Abi Awfa." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Zakah, chapter on the imam's prayer and supplication for the giver of charity: 3/361; and Muslim in al-Zakah, chapter on supplicating for one who brings charity, no. 1078: 2/756-757; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/485.]]

Ibn Kaysan said: this does not apply to obligatory charity; it is only in the charity of expiation for an oath.

ʿIkrimah said: it is the obligatory charity. When the repentance of these people was revealed, those among the laggards who had not repented said: "These were with us yesterday, yet they are not spoken to nor sat with. What is wrong with them?"

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verses 104–106:

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Do they not know that it is Allah who accepts repentance from His servants and takes the charities?﴾ That is, accepts them. ﴿And that Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾

Abdul-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us: Abdul-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Asamm narrated to us: al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman narrated to us: al-Shafi'i narrated to us: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ibn 'Ajlan, from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I heard Abu al-Qasim (ﷺ) say: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, no servant gives a charity from lawful earnings—and Allah accepts only what is good, and nothing good ascends to heaven—except that it is placed in the hand of the Most Merciful (ar-Rahman), exalted and majestic is He, and He nurtures it for him just as one of you nurtures his foal, until a morsel will come on the Day of Resurrection and it will be like a great mountain." Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, Allah is He who accepts repentance from His servants and takes the charities.﴾ [[Narrated by al-Shafi'i with a good chain: al-Musnad 1/220; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 6/131; al-Hakim authenticated it according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, 2/335. The essential meaning of the hadith is established in the Two Sahihs and elsewhere from Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him). See the note of Shaykh Shakir on al-Tabari: 6/18–20.]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And say, "Work, for Allah will see your deeds, and His Messenger and the believers. And you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do."﴾ Mujahid said: This is a warning to them. It was said: The seeing of the Prophet (ﷺ) is by Allah's informing him, and the seeing of the believers is by Allah placing love in their hearts for the people of righteousness and hatred for the people of corruption.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And others are deferred until the command of Allah—either He will punish them or He will accept their repentance. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾ The people of Medina and Kufa, except Abu Bakr, read "murja'un" without a hamza, while the others read it with a hamza. Al-irja' means postponement; murja'un means those who are delayed. "For the command of Allah" means for the judgment of Allah, exalted and majestic is He, concerning them. They are the three whose story comes later: Ka'b ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayyah, and Murarah ibn al-Rabi'. They did not exert themselves in repentance and apology as Abu Lubabah did. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) held them in abeyance for fifty nights and forbade the people from speaking to them [[In "A" (mukhalatatihim).]] and associating with them, until distress overwhelmed them and the earth, despite its vastness, became constricted for them. They had been among the people of Badr. So some people began to say, "They are destroyed," while others said, "Perhaps Allah will forgive them." Thus they were left in suspense concerning the command of Allah [not knowing] [[Addition from "B".]] whether He would punish them or have mercy upon them, until their repentance was revealed after fifty nights [[See: al-Tabari: 14/466; Asbab al-Nuzul p. 298.]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 107:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who took﴾. The people of Madinah and Syria read "alladhina" without the waw, and it is so in their codices. The others read "wa-alladhina" with the waw.

﴿a mosque for harm﴾. This verse was revealed concerning a group of the hypocrites who built a mosque by which they would harm the Mosque of Quba'. They were twelve men from among the people of hypocrisy: Wadi'ah ibn Thabit, Judham ibn Khalid, from whose house this mosque was taken out, Tha'labah ibn Hatib, Jariyah ibn 'Amir and his two sons Mujammi' and Zayd, Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, 'Abbad ibn Hanif, brother of Sahl ibn Hanif, Abu Habibah ibn al-Az'ar, Nabtal ibn al-Harith, Bijad ibn 'Uthman, and a man called Bakhraj. [[In "A": (Bakhdaj) and in "B": "Bakhraj"; the one adopted is from al-Tabari: 14/469, 471, with the annotation of Shaykh Mahmud Shakir.]] They built this mosque for harm, meaning causing harm to the believers, ﴿and disbelief﴾ in Allah and His Messenger, ﴿and division among the believers﴾. This is because they all used to pray in the Mosque of Quba', so they built the mosque of harm so that some of them would pray in it, which would lead to dissension and the scattering of the word. Mujammi' ibn Jariyah used to lead them in prayer.

When they finished its construction, they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was preparing for Tabuk and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have built a mosque for the sick, the needy, and on rainy and wintry nights, and we wish that you would come to us, pray in it for us, and invoke blessing for us." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: "I am on the point of a journey, and if we return, Allah willing, we will come to you and pray for you in it." [[For the story of the Mosque of Harm, see: al-Tabari: 14/468-475; Asbab al-Nuzul pp. (298-300); Sirah of Ibn Hisham: 2/530; al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/482 onward. Al-Albani weakened it in his takhrij of "Fiqh al-Sirah" of al-Ghazali p. (427). Ibn Hajar said: al-Tha'labi mentioned it without a chain... In the context of al-Tabari: that the Prophet ﷺ sent Malik ibn al-Dukhshum and Ma'n ibn 'Adi. He did not mention Wahshi and 'Amir ibn al-Sakan. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through the route of Ibn Ishaq, who said: al-Zuhri mentioned from Ibn Akimah al-Laythi from the nephew of Rahm that he heard Abu Rahm al-Ghifari, and he mentioned something similar. As for their having built it because of Abu 'Amir the monk: Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through the route of 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both. See: al-Kafi al-Shafi p. (81).]].

﴿and in preparation for those who had warred against Allah and His Messenger previously﴾, that is, waiting and preparing for the one who had warred against Allah and His Messenger. It is said: "arsadtu lahu" means "I prepared for him." This refers to Abu 'Amir the monk, and Abu 'Amir was a man from among them. He is the father of Handhalah, "the washed of the angels," and he had become a monk in the Pre-Islamic period, became Christian, and wore woollen garments. When the Prophet ﷺ came to Madinah, Abu 'Amir said to him: "What is this that you have brought?" He said: "I have brought the Hanifiyyah, the religion of Ibrahim." Abu 'Amir said: "We are upon it." The Prophet ﷺ said: "You are not upon it." He said: "Yes, but you have introduced into the Hanifiyyah what is not part of it." The Prophet ﷺ said: "I have not done so, rather I have brought it white and pure." Abu 'Amir said: "May Allah cause the liar among us to die, an exile, solitary, a stranger." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Amin." And he named him Abu 'Amir the Fasiq (the Depraved).

When the Day of Uhud came, Abu 'Amir said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "I do not find a people fighting you except that I will fight you alongside them." He continued to fight him until the Day of Hunayn. When Hawazin was defeated, he despaired and fled to Syria, and he sent to the hypocrites: "Prepare with whatever strength and weapons you can, and build me a mosque, for I am going to Caesar, king of the Romans, and will bring an army of Romans, and expel Muhammad and his companions." So they built the Mosque of Harm beside the Mosque of Quba'. That is the meaning of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and in preparation for those who had warred against Allah and His Messenger﴾, namely Abu 'Amir the Fasiq, so that he might pray in it when he returned from Syria.

His saying: ﴿previously﴾ refers back to Abu 'Amir, meaning: who had warred against Allah and His Messenger previously, that is, before the building of the Mosque of Harm.

﴿And they will surely swear, "We intended nothing but good"﴾, that is, what we intended by its construction, ﴿except the best﴾, meaning except the good deed, which is kindness to the Muslims and providing ease for the weak and those unable to travel to the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

﴿And Allah testifies that they are indeed liars﴾ in their saying and their oath. It is narrated that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned from Tabuk and stopped at Dhu Awan, a place near Madinah, they came to him and asked him to come to their mosque. He called for his shirt to wear it and go to them, but the Qur'an was revealed to him and Allah informed him of the matter of the Mosque of Harm and what they had planned. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then called Malik ibn al-Dukhshum, Ma'n ibn 'Adi, 'Amir ibn al-Sakan, and Wahshi, the slayer of Hamzah, and said to them: "Go to this mosque whose people are wrongdoers, demolish it and burn it." They set out quickly until they came to Banu Salim ibn 'Awf, who were the kin of Malik ibn al-Dukhshum. Malik said: "Wait for me until I bring you fire from my family." He entered his household, took a palm frond, and kindled fire in it. Then they went out running until they entered the mosque, in which its people were present, and they burned it and demolished it, and its people dispersed from it. The Prophet ﷺ ordered that it be made a dunghill where carrion, filth, and refuse would be thrown. Abu 'Amir the monk died in Syria, solitary, alone, a stranger.

It is also narrated that the Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, who had built the Mosque of Quba', came to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab during his caliphate, asking him to permit Mujammi' ibn Harithah to lead them in prayer in their mosque. He said: "No, and not a blessing of the eye. Is he not the imam of the Mosque of Harm?" Mujammi' said to him: "O Commander of the Believers, do not hasten against me. By Allah, I prayed in it, and I do not know what they concealed in it. Had I known, I would not have prayed with them in it. I was a young man who recited the Qur'an, and they were elders who did not recite the Qur'an, so I prayed, and I thought only that they were seeking nearness to Allah, the Exalted, and I did not know what was in their hearts." 'Umar excused him, believed him, and commanded him to lead the prayer in the Mosque of Quba'.

'Ata' said: When Allah granted 'Umar the conquest of the cities, he commanded the Muslims to build mosques, and he commanded them not to build in their city two mosques, one of which would harm the other.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 108:

Allah's words: ﴿Do not stand in it ever.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "Do not pray in it." Allah forbade His Prophet ﷺ from praying in the Masjid al-Dirar (the mosque of harm).

﴿Surely a mosque founded upon piety﴾: the lam is the lam of inception (lam al-ibtida'). It has also been said that it is the lam of oath, its implied meaning being: "By Allah, surely a mosque founded..." That is, its foundation was laid upon piety (al-taqwa), ﴿from the first day﴾, meaning from the first day it was built and its foundation was laid, ﴿is more worthy that you stand in it﴾, that is, to pray.

They differed concerning the mosque that was founded upon piety. Ibn 'Umar, Zayd ibn Thabit, and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: it is the Mosque of Madinah, the Mosque of the Messenger ﷺ. The evidence for this is:

What Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Qahir informed us: 'Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi related to us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan related to us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj related to us: Muhammad ibn Hatim related to us: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, from Humayd al-Kharrat, who said: I heard Abu Salamah 'Abd al-Rahman say: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'id passed by me, and he said: I said to him: How did you hear your father mention the mosque that was founded upon piety? He said: My father said: I entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the house of one of his wives, and I said: O Messenger of Allah, which of the two mosques is the one founded upon piety? He said: He took a handful of pebbles and struck them against the ground, then said: It is this mosque of yours, the Mosque of Madinah. He said: I said: I bear witness that I heard your father mention it in exactly this way. [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Hajj, chapter on the explanation that the mosque founded upon piety is the Mosque of the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah, no. (1398): 2 / 1015.]]

And Abu al-Hasan al-Shirazi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Khubayb ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Hafs ibn 'Asim, from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Between my house and my pulpit is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and my pulpit is upon my Basin." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the virtue of prayer in the Mosques of Makkah and Madinah, chapter on the virtue of what is between the grave and the pulpit: 3 / 70, and Muslim in al-Hajj, chapter on what is between the grave and the pulpit being a garden from the gardens of Paradise, no. (1391): 2 / 1011. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2 / 338.]]

And a people went to the view that it is the Mosque of Quba, which is the narration of 'Atiyyah from Ibn 'Abbas, and the saying of 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr [and Sa'id ibn Jubayr] [[Omitted in manuscript "A".]] and Qatadah:

'Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us: Musa ibn Isma'il related to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muslim related to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Prophet ﷺ used to come to the Mosque of Quba every Saturday, walking and riding, and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar used to do the same. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari, in the previous place: 3 / 69, and Muslim in al-Hajj, chapter on the virtue of the Mosque of Quba, no. (1399): 2 / 1016-1017.]]

Nafi' added from Ibn 'Umar, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "and he would pray in it two rak'ahs." [[In the narration of Muslim, in the previous place.]]

Allah's words: ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves﴾, from minor impurities (al-ahdath), major impurities (al-janabat) and najasat (physical filth). 'Ata' said: They used to cleanse themselves with water and did not sleep at night in a state of janabah.

Abu Tahir 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Qashani informed us: Abu 'Umar al-Qasim ibn Ja'far ibn 'Abd al-Wahid al-Hashimi informed us: Abu 'Ali Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn 'Amr al-Lu'lu'i informed us: Abu Dawud Sulayman ibn al-Ash'ath al-Sijistani related to us: Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' informed us: Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham related to us, from Yunus ibn al-Harith, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Maymunah, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "This verse was revealed concerning the people of Quba": ﴿In it are men who love to purify themselves﴾, and he said: "They used to cleanse themselves with water, so this verse was revealed concerning them." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in Tahara, chapter on istinja' with water: 1 / 39, and al-Tirmidhi in the tafsir of Surat al-Tawbah: 8 / 503, and he said: this is a gharib hadith from this route, and on the subject there are reports from Abu Ayyub, Anas ibn Malik, and Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Salam. Ibn Majah also narrated it in Tahara, chapter on istinja' with water, no. (357). Al-Albani authenticated it in Sahih Ibn Majah, no. (286). See: Talkhis al-Habir: 1 / 112-113; Khulasat al-Badr al-Munir by Ibn al-Mulaqqin: 1 / 50.]]

﴿And Allah loves those who purify themselves﴾, i.e., those who keep themselves pure.

﴿Is one who founded his building﴾ Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read "ussisa" with a damma on the hamza and a kasra on the sin, and "bunyanuhu" with a raised nun in both, in the passive form (ghayr tasmiyat al-fa'il, the form without naming the agent). The others read "assasa" with a fatha on the hamza and the sin, and "bunyanahu" with a nasb (accusative) on the nun, in the active form (tasmiyat al-fa'il, the form naming the agent).

﴿upon piety from Allah and approval, better﴾ That is: upon seeking piety and the approval of Allah the Exalted is better. ﴿Or one who founded his building upon the edge﴾ upon the brink, ﴿of a crumbling bank﴾. Abu 'Amr, Hamzah and Abu Bakr read "jurfin" with a sukun on the ra', while the rest read it with a damma on the ra'. Both are dialectal variants (lughatan). It is the well that has not been lined with stone. Abu 'Ubaydah said: it is the pit, and what the torrent tears away from the valleys, so that it becomes hollowed out (yanjarif bil-ma'), and is left weak and crumbling. ﴿Crumbling (hari)﴾ means hA'ir, the one that collapses. It is said: haara yahuru, so he is ha'ir; then it is inverted and said as hari, like shakin and sha'ik, and 'aqin and 'a'iq. It is also said that it derives from yuhar, when something collapses, and its meaning is that which falls, part of it following upon part, as sand and any soft thing crumbles.

﴿So it collapsed with him﴾ that is, it fell with its builder ﴿into the fire of Hell﴾. He means that building this mosque of harm is like building on the brink of Hell, so that it collapses with its people into it. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: He means that hypocrisy has led them to the Fire.

﴿And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾. Qatadah said: By Allah, they did not cease until it fell into the Fire. It was mentioned to us that a pit was dug in it, and smoke was seen rising from it. Jabir ibn 'Abdullah said: I saw smoke rising from the Mosque of Harm. [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 14/495, and authenticated by al-Hakim: 4/596, and al-Dhahabi agreed. al-Suyuti added its attribution to Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh. al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/292. Ibn Hajar attributed it in al-Matalib al-'Aliyah: 3/340 to Musaddad, with an addition.]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 9, verses 110–111:**

﴿The building which they have built will never cease to be a source of doubt in their hearts﴾, that is, doubt and hypocrisy. They think that they were doing good in building it, just as the calf was made beloved to the people of Musa (Moses). This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both. Al-Kalbi said: it is regret and remorse, because they regretted having built it. Al-Suddi said: the demolition of their building will continue to be a source of doubt, resentment and rage in their hearts.

﴿Unless their hearts are cut to pieces﴾, that is, their hearts are split apart so that they die. Ibn 'Amir, Abu Ja'far, Hamzah and Hafs read "tuqatta'a" with a fathah on the ta', meaning "tataqatta'a" (their hearts are cut to pieces). The others read it with a dammah. Ya'qub alone read "ila an" lightly, as a limit (ghayah), and "tuqta'a" with a dammah on the ta' and lightly, from qat' (cutting). The explanation of al-Dahhak and Qatadah supports this: they will remain in doubt about it until they die, and then they will become certain.

﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾.

The statement of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties﴾, to the end of the verse. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: When the Ansar pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the Night of 'Aqabah in Makkah, and they were seventy persons, 'Abdullah ibn Rawahah said: "O Messenger of Allah, stipulate for your Lord and for yourself whatever you wish."

He said: "I stipulate for my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, that you worship Him and do not associate anything with Him, and I stipulate for myself that you protect me from what you protect yourselves and your properties from."

They said: "And if we do that, what will we have?"

He said: "Paradise."

They said: "The sale is profitable; we will neither cancel it (la nuqilu) nor seek its cancellation (wa la nastaqilu)."[[Aqalahu al-bay' yuqiluhu iqalatan and taqayala al-bay'an: if the two parties dissolve the sale, the goods return to their owner and the price to the buyer, when one or both have regretted it. Al-iqalah may be used in a pledge and covenant. Istiqalah: to ask him to cancel it for you.]] Then this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in return for that they will have Paradise﴾.[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 14/499. See also: al-Kafi al-Shaf p. (81); Asbab al-Nuzul p. (300).]]

Al-A'mash read "bil-jannah" (with the definite article attached as a preposition: "with Paradise").

﴿They fight in the way of Allah, so they kill and are killed﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "fa-yuqtalun" (so they are killed), with the object placed before the subject, meaning that some of them kill others, and the rest are killed. The others read it with the subject placed first.

﴿A promise [binding] upon Him in truth﴾, that is: the reward of Paradise for them is a promise and a truth ﴿in the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an﴾. That is, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, promised them this promise and clarified it in these Books. It has also been said: this indicates that all the adherents of the religions were commanded to fight for the reward of Paradise. Then He congratulated them, saying: ﴿And who is more faithful to his covenant than Allah? So rejoice in your transaction which you have made. That is the great achievement﴾, that is, be glad. 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, made a pledge with you and made both transactions yours."

Qatadah said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, bargained with them and raised the price for them.[["Thamantu al-rajul fi al-mabi'": when I haggled with him over its price, discussed it with him, and bargained with him over its sale and purchase. See al-Tabari: 14/499.]]

Al-Hasan said: Listen to a profitable bargain by which Allah has made a pact with every believer. He also said: Allah has given you the world, so buy Paradise with part of it.

Then He described them, saying: ﴿Those who repent﴾. Al-Farra' said: it is begun in the nominative (marfu') because the verse is complete and the speech has ended. Al-Zajjaj said: "al-ta'ibun" is in the nominative as the subject of a new sentence, and its predicate is implied. The meaning is: "Those who repent, to the end of the verse, also have Paradise." That is, whoever does not fight, without being stubborn or intending to abandon jihad (because some Muslims suffice for others in jihad), [whoever has this description]¹ also has Paradise. This is the better view: it is as if He promised Paradise to all the believers, as He said: "And to each Allah has promised the best" (al-Nisa' 95). Whoever makes it a continuation of the first view, the promise of Paradise is specific to those who fight and are described by this attribute.²

[[¹ The words between the brackets are in manuscript "b".]]
[[² In manuscript "b": "the attributes" (al-sifat).]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 112:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿the repentant ones﴾, meaning those who repented from polytheism (shirk) and disassociated themselves from hypocrisy (nifaq). ﴿The worshippers﴾, meaning the obedient ones who devoted their worship sincerely to Allah, mighty and majestic. ﴿The praisers﴾, meaning those who praise Allah in every state, in ease and in hardship.

We have also related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "The first to be called to Paradise on the Day of Resurrection are those who praise Allah in ease and in hardship." [[Narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 1/502, who declared it sound according to the conditions of Muslim; and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah: 5/69. Al-Haythami said: "al-Tabarani narrated it in three chains, and in one of them is Qays ibn al-Rabi'. Shu'bah, al-Thawri and others declared him trustworthy, while Yahya al-Qattan and others declared him weak. The rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih. al-Bazzar narrated it in similar wording with a good chain." Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/95. The author also narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/50, and its chain includes Habib ibn Abi Thabit, who is a mudallis and narrated it with 'an'anah.]]

﴿The travelers (al-sa'ihun)﴾: Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: they are the fasting ones. [[Related both as a marfu' and mawquf report. The mawquf one is sound. See: al-Tabari: 14/502-504; al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/297-298; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/393.]]

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: the fasting person was only called "sa'ih" (traveler) because he abstains from all pleasures: food, drink, and marriage.

'Ata' said: "the travelers" are the warriors who fight in the cause of Allah. It is related from 'Uthman ibn Maz'un, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, permit me to travel (siyahah)." He said: "The travel (siyahah) of my ummah is jihad in the cause of Allah." [[A weak hadith narrated by al-Tabarani, in whose chain is Mu'alla ibn Hilal, who is abandoned (matruk). The author narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/370-371. Abu Dawud narrated it in the Book of Jihad through the route of Abu Umamah, in whose chain is Rushdin ibn Sa'd.
