Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 121:

Allah's words: ﴿And they do not spend an expenditure﴾, i.e., in the way of Allah, ﴿small or great﴾, ﴿not even the cord [[al-'ilaqah: that from which a sword or the like is hung.]] of a whip﴾, ﴿and they do not cross a valley﴾, i.e., they do not pass over a valley in their journey, whether advancing or retreating.

﴿except that it is written for them﴾, meaning: their traces and their steps, ﴿that Allah may reward them with the best of what they used to do﴾. It was narrated from Khuraym ibn Fatik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever spends an expenditure in the way of Allah, it is written for him seven hundred times [the reward]" [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Fada'il al-Jihad, chapter on what has come concerning the virtue of spending in the way of Allah: 5/254, and he said: this is a hasan hadith. Also by al-Nasa'i in al-Jihad, chapter on the virtue of spending in the way of Allah, 6/49. Ibn Hibban (396) in al-Mawarid and al-Hakim (2/872) declared it authentic. Al-Albani, in his commentary on al-Mishkat, said: its chain is authentic.]].

Ismail ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us, Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us, Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi informed us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan narrated to us, Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali narrated to us, Jarir informed us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Amr al-Shaybani, from Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari, who said: A man came with a bridled she-camel and said: "This is for the way of Allah." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "For you, on its account on the Day of Resurrection, there will be seven hundred she-camels, all of them bridled" [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the virtue of charity in the way of Allah, no. (1892): 3/1505, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/359.]].

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Abu Ma'mar narrated to us, Abd al-Warith narrated to us, al-Husayn [narrated to me Yahya ibn Abi Kathir] [[What is between the brackets is missing from "A".]] narrated to me Abu Salamah, narrated to me Busr ibn Sa'id, narrated to me Zayd ibn Khalid, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever equips a warrior in the way of Allah has indeed fought, and whoever takes care of the family of a warrior in the way of Allah with good has indeed fought" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Jihad, chapter: the virtue of one who equips a warrior or looks after his family with good: 6/49, and Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the virtue of aiding the warrior in the way of Allah... via Bukayr ibn al-Ashajj from Busr ibn Sa'id from Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, no. (1895): 3/1507, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 10/359.]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 122:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿It is not for the believers to go forth all together﴾, to the end of the verse. Ibn 'Abbas, in the narration of al-Kalbi, said: When God, may He be exalted and glorified, revealed the faults of the hypocrites during the expedition of Tabuk, the Prophet ﷺ would dispatch the expeditionary detachments (sarayا), and the Muslims would all go forth together to the military campaign and leave the Prophet ﷺ alone, so God, may He be exalted and glorified, revealed this verse. [[Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. 304.]] This is a negation in the sense of a prohibition.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Why did not a party from every group among them go forth﴾, meaning: Why did not a group from every tribe go forth to the campaign [while a group remained with the Messenger of God ﷺ]? [[Omitted in manuscript "A".]] ﴿that they might gain understanding in the religion﴾, meaning the group that remained behind, who would learn the Qur'an, the Sunnah, the obligatory duties and the rulings. When the detachments returned, they would inform them of what had been revealed after they left, so the detachments would remain and learn what had been revealed after them, and other detachments would be dispatched. This is His saying: ﴿and that they may warn their people﴾, and inform them of the Qur'an and warn them with it, ﴿when they return to them, that they may beware﴾, by not acting contrary to it.

Al-Hasan said: This understanding (tafaqquh) and warning refers to the group that goes forth, and its meaning is: Why did not a group go forth so that they might gain insight (li-yatabassaru) through what God shows them of victory over the polytheists and the support of the religion, and so that they might warn their people among the unbelievers when they return to them from jihad, informing them of God's support of His Messenger ﷺ and the believers, that they may beware of opposing the Prophet ﷺ, lest there befall them what befell their companions among the unbelievers. [[This is the meaning which Imam al-Tabari preferred and articulated soundly: al-Tafsir: 14/573-574.]]

Al-Kalbi also said: It has another aspect, namely that some clans of Banu Asad from Khuzaymah were struck by a severe year of drought, so they came with their families until they alighted in Medina, and they fouled its roads with excrement and raised its prices. So there was revealed His saying: ﴿It is not for the believers to go forth all together; why did not a party from every group among them go forth﴾, meaning: It was not for them to go forth all together, but rather a party from every tribe should go forth so that they might gain understanding in the religion. [[See: al-Tabari: 14/569; al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/323.]]

Mujahid said: It was revealed concerning people who went out into the desert seeking good from its inhabitants, and they obtained some kindness from them and called whomever they found among the people to guidance. The people said to them: "We see you only as having left your companion and come to us," so they felt a distress in themselves over that, and they all came back from the desert until they entered upon the Prophet ﷺ, and God revealed this verse, meaning: Why did not a party from every group go forth so that they might gain understanding in the religion and hear what had been revealed after them, and that they might warn their people, meaning all the people, when they return to them and call them to God, that they may beware of the punishment and vengeance of God. A party remained, seeking good. [[al-Tabari: 14/566.]]

We were informed by Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Kharaqi, who said: Abu al-Hasan al-Taysafuni informed us, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar al-Jawhari narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Kushmihani narrated to us, who said: 'Ali ibn Hajar narrated to us, who said: Isma'il ibn Ja'far narrated to us, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Sa'id ibn Abi Hind narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Whomever God wills good for, He gives him understanding in the religion." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Knowledge, chapter "Whomever God wills good for, He gives him understanding in the religion": 1/164, and in Virtues; and by Muslim in Zakah, chapter on the prohibition of asking, no. (1037): 2/718; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/385.]]

We were informed by 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib, who said: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal narrated to us, who said: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm narrated to us, who said: al-Rabi' informed us, who said: al-Shafi'i informed us, who said: Sufyan related to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "You will find people to be mines, like mines of gold and silver; the best of them in the Jahiliyyah are the best of them in Islam when they gain understanding." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Virtues, chapter on His saying, "O mankind, indeed We created you from male and female": 6/525-526; by Muslim in the Virtues of the Companions, chapter on the best of people, no. (2526): 4/1958; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/286.]]

Al-Fiqh (jurisprudence, i.e., knowledge of the rulings of the religion) is divided into fard 'ayn (individual obligation) and fard kifayah (collective obligation). The individual obligation is like knowledge of purification, prayer and fasting, which every accountable person must know. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim." [[In "B": "and Muslimah". The hadith is narrated by Ibn Majah in the Introduction, chapter on the virtue of scholars and urging the seeking of knowledge, no. (224): 1/81. He said in the Zawa'id: its isnad is weak because of the weakness of Hafs ibn Sulayman. It is attributed in Kanz al-'Ummal: 10/130-131 to Ibn 'Adi, al-Bayhaqi, al-Tabarani and al-Khatib. The hadith has been related through many routes from a number of Companions, and each route is not free of weakness, but their multiplicity strengthens the hadith; therefore al-Mizzi and Ibn al-Qattan graded it hasan, and al-Suyuti declared it sahih li-ghayrihi and mentioned it among the mutawatir hadiths. Al-Sakhawi said in al-Maqasid al-Hasanah: some authors added to this hadith "and Muslimah", which has no mention in any of its routes, although its meaning is sound. See: Tamyiz al-Tayyib min al-Khabith of Ibn al-Dayba': p. 116; Kashf al-Khafa': 2/56-57; Nazm al-Mutanathir of al-Kittani: pp. 35-37.]] Likewise, every act of worship that the Law has made obligatory upon each individual requires knowledge of it, such as knowledge of zakah if one has property, and knowledge of hajj if it is obligatory upon him.

As for fard kifayah, it is that one learns until he reaches the degree of ijtihad and the rank of issuing fatwa. If the people of a town abstain from learning it, they all sin; and if one person from each town rises and learns it, the obligation falls from the others, and it is incumbent upon them to follow him (taqlid) in what befalls them of events. Abu Umamah, may God be pleased with him, related that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "The superiority of the scholar over the worshipper is like my superiority over the least of you." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Knowledge, chapter on what has come concerning the virtue of jurisprudence over worship: 7/456-457, and he said: this is a hasan, gharib, sahih hadith. al-Darimi narrated it from Makhul as a mursal with a hasan isnad in the Introduction, chapter on whoever said: knowledge is fear and piety of God: 1/88, and he also narrated it from al-Hasan as marfu' in the chapter on the virtue of knowledge and the scholar: 1/97-98. Also by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/278, and Ibn 'Abd al-Barr in Jami' Bayan al-'Ilm: 1/46. See: al-Albani's commentary on al-Mishkat: 1/74-75.]]

And from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "One jurist is more severe upon the Devil than a thousand worshippers." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Knowledge, chapter on what has come concerning the virtue of jurisprudence over worship: 7/450, and he said: this is a gharib hadith, and we do not know it except from this route; and by Ibn Majah in the Introduction, chapter on the virtue of scholars and urging the seeking of knowledge, no. (222): 1/81. In its isnad is Rawh ibn Junah, who is very weak, accused of fabrication. Ibn 'Abd al-Barr narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas, and also from Abu Hurayrah, in Jami' Bayan al-'Ilm: 1/52-53. In it is Yazid ibn 'Ayyash, who is a liar. See: al-Albani's commentary on al-Mishkat: 1/75, and Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/278.]]

al-Shafi'i said: Seeking knowledge is more excellent than voluntary prayer.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 9, verse 123:

The words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿O you who have believed, fight those adjacent to you of the disbelievers﴾ to the end of the verse. They were commanded to fight those nearest to them in dwelling and kinship, the nearer and then the nearer. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: such as the Banu Qurayzah, the Nadir, Khaybar, and the like.

It was also said: He meant by them the Byzantines (al-Rum), because they were the inhabitants of al-Sham, and al-Sham [was] [[omitted from "a".]] closer to Madinah than Iraq. ﴿And let them find in you harshness﴾: severity and zeal. Al-Hasan said: patience in striving against them. ﴿And know that Allah is with the muttaqun (the God-conscious)﴾ through help and support.

The Quranic verse on the words of God, "And when a surah is revealed, some of them say, 'Which of you has had its faith increased by this?'" means: certainty. The hypocrites used to say this mockingly. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith﴾, in certainty and affirmation, ﴿and they rejoice﴾, they are glad at the revelation of the Quran.

﴿And as for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, doubt and hypocrisy, ﴿it has added to them defilement upon their defilement﴾, meaning disbelief upon their disbelief. So each time a surah is revealed, they deny it, and their disbelief increases because of it.

Mujahid said: this verse is an indication that faith increases and decreases.

Umar used to take the hand of a man or two of his companions and say: "Come, so that we may increase in faith."

Ali ibn Abi Talib said: Faith begins as a white speck (lumtah) [[In al-Nihayah by Ibn al-Athir: "yabda'" (begins) a lumtah. The lumtah, with a dammah on the lam, is like a spot, of whiteness.]] in the heart. Whenever faith grows in magnitude, that whiteness increases until the whole heart becomes white. Hypocrisy likewise begins as a black speck in the heart, and whenever hypocrisy increases, that blackness increases until the whole heart becomes black. By Allah, if you were to split open the heart of a believer, you would find it white, and if you were to split open the heart of a hypocrite, you would find it black. [[Narrated by Abu Ubayd in Gharib al-Hadith: 3/460, and by Ibn al-Mubarak in al-Zuhd, Khushaysh in al-Istiqamah, al-Bayhaqi, al-Lalika'i in al-Sunnah, and al-Asbahani in al-Hujjah. Al-Qutaybi said: "what troubles you and harms you." Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "what leads you astray."

Al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi said: "what you are unable to complete."

﴿He is eager over you﴾ meaning: over your faith and your righteousness. Qatadah said: "eager over you" meaning: over your misguided ones, that Allah may guide them. ﴿For the believers, he is kind and merciful﴾. It was said: "kind to the obedient, merciful to the sinners."

﴿But if they turn away﴾ meaning: if they turn away from faith and oppose you in war, ﴿then say: "Allah is sufficient for me; there is no deity except Him. Upon Him I have relied, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne."﴾

It is narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "The last of the Qur'an to be revealed were these two verses, ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾ to the end of the surah." And he said: "They are the most recent of the verses in terms of their revelation from Allah." [[Narrated by al-Hakim: 2/338, and Imam Abdullah ibn Ahmad in the Zawa'id al-Musnad: 5/117. Ibn Hajar attributed it in al-Matalib al-Aliyah 3/337 to Ishaq ibn Rahawayh. All of them narrated it without his saying: "They are the most recent of the verses..." al-Haythami said in al-Majma' 7/36: "Abdullah ibn Ahmad and al-Tabarani narrated it, and in its chain is Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, who is trustworthy but has poor memory, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."]]
